Why should they allow themselves to be overcome, since he who works in us is greater than he who rages and rants in this unhappy world? And how great his strength is, and how effective the consolation with which he stands by his wrestlers, the examples of many martyrs teach, who indeed wearied the hands of their executioners by their patience, while they themselves became superior to all tortures.

units.la: Quia vero multi perstant quidem in statione sua, sed interim insyncerius agunt, pergit Paulus, & omnem fraudis doliq; suspicionem procul abs se remouet, & se in ministerio suo sic versari ait, ut non opus sit ipsi villis latebris quibus sese aut impostturas suas occultet. Abdicauimus (inquit) tegumenta siue latebras turpitudinis. Sic autem vocat omnes praetextus, quibus qui mala fide agunt, seipsos & consilia sua palliare solent, ne quales sint deprehendantur. Itaque iensus est, se bene sibi conscium nullas latebras quaerere, ut quem neque sui ministerij pudeat, neque eorum, quae lucuseque in illo fecerit. Est hoc verae integritatis argumentum. Vt enim Veritas non quaerit tenebras, sed luce delectatur, ideoq; simplicissima est eius oratio: ita omnes solent: qui Veritati studenr, & res suas animo syncero atque integro instituunt.
units.tr: Because many indeed persist in their post but meanwhile act insincerely, Paul goes on to remove far from himself every suspicion of deceit and guile, and says that he so conducts himself in his ministry that he has no need of any hidden corners in which to conceal himself or his impostures. "We have renounced," he says, "the hidden things of shame, the coverings and hiding-places." He calls by this name all the pretexts behind which those who act in bad faith are accustomed to cloak themselves and their plans, so that they are not caught for what they are. Thus he signifies that, being conscious of nothing amiss, he seeks no hiding-places, since he is not ashamed of his ministry or of what he has done in it up to now. This is the mark of true integrity. For just as truth does not seek darkness but delights in light, and therefore its speech is most simple, so it is with all who pursue the truth and order their affairs with a sincere and upright mind.

units.la: Habemus autem in Pauli exemplo communem regulam, quam omnes homines, cuiuscunque sint loci aut ordinis, sequi debent: Nimirum vt ita res suas instituant, ne ipsos alicuius dicti aut facti pudere possit, neue cogantur ad latebras aut angulos confugere, quos homines minus ingenui, vel potius improbi impostores, quaerere solent. Semper ergo sibi ipsis occinant: Quid vero si hoc tuum institutum innotescerent? quid si quod nunc instituis, cogitas, facis, alij rescirent? quanta nomini tuo inureretur macula? Adhaec meminerint, Dei oculis abstrusissima quaeque patere, & eundem plerunque suo tempore in lucem proferre ea, quae bene tecta putabamus: quare veteres olim Veritatem temporis filiam esse dixerunt. At si hoc decet Christianos homines, quid de Apostolicis Romanensibus dicemus, qui in ijs quidem, quae ad religionem pertinent, fuco inani se ostentant, interim vero quoad mores in publico helluantur, scortantur, moechantur, belligerantur, deierant, blasphemijs & dirs crepant, idq; fronte plus quam meretricia, cum adeo latere nolint, ut etiam in nequitijs suis glorientur: & ne quid omittant, cum tales sint, irreprehensibiles tamen & sanctissimi, imo ipsa Sanctitas dici & haberi volunt? Vtinam vero hic ab omni culpa puri essent omnes, qui Euangelij doctrinam syncerio-rem profitentur.
units.tr: Moreover, in Paul's example we have a common rule, which all people, of whatever place or rank, ought to follow: namely, that they order their affairs so that no word or deed of theirs can cause them shame, and that they are not forced to flee into hiding-places or corners, which dishonest men, or rather wicked impostors, are accustomed to seek. Let them therefore always say to themselves: "What if this plan of yours became known? What if what you now intend, think or do were discovered by others? How great a stain would be fixed upon your name?" Let them also remember that all the most hidden things lie open to God's eyes, and that he often brings into the light at the proper time those things we thought well concealed. That is why the ancients once said that truth is the daughter of time. But if this befits Christian people, what shall we say of the Roman Apostolics, who in matters pertaining to religion display themselves with empty show, while in their conduct they openly gorge themselves, whore, commit adultery, wage war, swear oaths, and rattle off blasphemies and curses, and do so with a brazen face more than harlot-like, since they are unwilling to be hidden, so that they even glory in their wickedness? And, lest they leave anything out, though they are such men, they wish to be considered and called blameless and most holy, indeed holiness itself! Would that all who profess the more sincere doctrine of the gospel were pure from every fault here.

units.la: Caeterum exponit seipsum Paulus, dicens: Non incedentes in caliditate, neque falsantes ser-monem Dei. Ita suam integritatem asserit, ut simul perstringat pseudoapostolos, qui omnia astutè & fraudulenter faciebant, ut longè alij viderentur plerique quam reuera essent. Primò enim, ut Iudaeos sibi propitios facerent, qui praecipui erant omnium persecutionum authores, Circumcisionem & Legales ceremonias passim in Ecclesijs vrgebant: & cùm non aliud quam otium quaererent, & crucem declinare aut subterfugere cuperent, ij tamen videri volebant, qui Ecclesijs quam optime vellent consulerunt. Astute ergo suis cupiditatibus & studijs priuatus publicam omnium salutem praetexebant, cùm interim alteros illos in seruitutem redigerent, & iugum (ut Petrus dicebat) illorum ceruicibus imponerent prorsus intolerabile. De eo ipse Paulus apertius in Epistola ad Galatas loquitur his verbis:Quicunque volunt speciosi apparere in carne, ij co-gunt vos circumcidi, tantum ne ob Crucem Christi persecutionem patiantur: Nam ne ipsi qui-dem qui circumciduntur, Legem seruant: sed volunt vos circumcidi, ut de vestra carne glorien-tur. Deinde simulabant se quoque nihil postulare ab Ecclesijs, interim autem plus emungebant, quam qui legitimo & ordinario stipendio erant contenti. Adhaec cùm sanctitatis specie se ve-n ditarent, gulæ tamen & ventris mancipia erant, & per omne genus nequitiæ volutabantur. Ideo Paulus eos alibi canes, malos operarios & concisionem vocat: imò hæc de illis scribit: Complures ambulant, de quibus sæpe dixi vobis, nunc autem & flens dico, inimici Crucis Christi, quorum finis perditio est, quorum Deus venter, & gloria in dedecore eorum, qui terrestria curant. Deniq; fucum faciebant imperitis arte dicendi & verborum præstigijs, simulque Euangelij doctrinam adulterabant doctrinæ Legalis additionibus, vt iam sæpe est dictum. Recte igitur illis Paulus πανουργίαν, id est, astutiam eiusmodi tribuit, qua se in omnes formas vertere, & omnium ingeniis sese accommodare norint. Tales hodie multos est passim inuenire, qui interea ne à calumniis quidem abstinent, quibus fidos Christi ministros proscindunt, vt his in odium apud Ecclesias adducti, ipsi facilius res suas possint agere. At ista omnia procul abs se reijcit Paulus, vt qui bona fide & ingenue egerit, atque Euangelium, quod ipsissimum Dei Verbum est, syncerè prædicarit, nullo fuco falsatum aut adulteratum. Confirmationi iisdem seruit, quod in priori epistola scripsit: Ego cum venirem ad vos fratres, non veni cum eminentia orationis aut sapientiæ, annuntians vobis testimonium Dei: Non enim iudicaui me quicquam scire inter vos, nisi IESVM CHRISTVM, eumque crucifixum. Quod item ad Galatas tanta cum libertate pronuntiat: Etiamsi nos, aut Angelus è cælo euangelizet vobis præter id quod euangelizauimus vobis, anathema sit. Galat.1.
units.tr: Paul further explains himself, saying: "Not walking in craftiness, nor adulterating the word of God." Thus he asserts his integrity while at the same time censuring the false apostles, who did everything cunningly and deceitfully, so that most of them appeared far different from what they really were. First, in order to win the favour of the Jews, who were the chief authors of all the persecutions, they everywhere pressed circumcision and the legal ceremonies upon the churches. And although they sought nothing but ease, and wished to avoid or escape the cross, they nevertheless wanted to seem men who had served the churches as well as they could. Cunningly, then, they veiled their private desires and aims under the pretext of the common salvation of all, while at the same time they reduced the others to servitude and laid upon their necks a yoke (as Peter put it) utterly intolerable. Paul speaks more plainly about this in his epistle to the Galatians, in these words: "Those who wish to appear fine in the flesh compel you to be circumcised, only that they may not suffer persecution for the cross of Christ. For not even those who are circumcised keep the law, but they want you to be circumcised so that they may glory in your flesh." Then they also pretended that they asked nothing of the churches, while in fact they squeezed out more than those who were content with a lawful and regular stipend. Moreover, although they sold themselves under the appearance of holiness, they were nonetheless slaves of the belly and gullet, and wallowed in every kind of wickedness. Therefore Paul elsewhere calls them dogs, evil workers and "the concision," and indeed he writes of them: "Many walk, of whom I have often told you, and now I tell you even weeping, enemies of the cross of Christ, whose end is destruction, whose god is the belly, and whose glory is in their shame, who mind earthly things." Finally, they cast a veil over the unlearned by the art of speaking and the sleights of words, and at the same time adulterated the doctrine of the gospel with additions from the legal doctrine, as has often been said. Rightly, then, Paul ascribes to them craftiness [πανουργίαν], that is, such cunning by which they know how to turn themselves into every shape and adapt themselves to everyone's disposition. Many such men are found today everywhere, who meanwhile do not even refrain from the calumnies by which they tear to pieces the faithful ministers of Christ, so that these men, made odious to the churches, may more easily carry out their own designs. But Paul rejects all these things far from himself, since he acted in good faith and openly, and preached the gospel, which is the very Word of God, sincerely, not falsified or adulterated by any disguise. He served the same confirmation in what he wrote in the first epistle: "When I came to you, brothers, I did not come with excellence of speech or wisdom, proclaiming to you the testimony of God. For I determined to know nothing among you except Jesus Christ, and him crucified." He also pronounces with such freedom to the Galatians: "Even if we, or an angel from heaven, preach to you anything other than what we have preached to you, let him be accursed." Galat. 1.

units.la: Docent ista Verbi administros, quid eos facere conueniat, ne cogantur latebras aut tegumenta dedecoris quærere. Abstineant ab omni dolo, & ingenue dicant agantque omnia. Si enim in prophanis turpe est, ex eodem ore calidam & frigidam efflare, quanto turpius fuerit in diuinis tale quid facere, vbi nullus mendacio aut dolo locus est reliquus? Neque alij Ecclesijs nocentiores sunt, quàm qui dolose agunt. Olim certè Imperatores & Episcopos, non sine magno Ecclesiarum malo, ambiguis locutionibus ludificarunt Ariani quidam nebulones, qui Sophisticæ potius quàm Veritati studebant. Et quantum nostro seculo in re Sacramentaria nocuerint, dolosi quidam compositores, qui cothurnis verborum utrique parti fucum facere conabantur, satis notum est. Solent tales dolum sanctum prætexere. Sed nullo dolo opus est Veritati, neque sanctus dici potest dolus, quo illa obscuratur, & qui cum aliqua simulatione coniunctus est. Quicquid enim huius est, id ad diaboli ingenium accedit, quem mendacem atque impostorem esse scimus. Deinde imprimis caveant ministri, ne falsent sermonem Domini. Fit hoc, quando vel humanorum figmentorum palea tritico Dominico miscentur, vel Verbum Dei in sensum alienum detorquetur. Faciunt hoc fere, qui suis potius commodis quàm gloriæ Dei & Ecclesiarum ædificationi student.
units.tr: These things teach the ministers of the Word what they ought to do, so that they are not forced to seek hiding-places or coverings for their disgrace. Let them abstain from all deceit and speak and do everything openly. For if in profane matters it is shameful to blow hot and cold from the same mouth, how much more shameful would it be to do such a thing in divine matters, where no room is left for lies or trickery? Nor do any harm to the churches more than those who act deceitfully. Long ago certain Arian scoundrels, who pursued sophistry rather than truth, mocked emperors and bishops with ambiguous expressions, and not without great harm to the churches. How much harm deceitful compilers have done in our own age in the sacramentarian controversy, who tried to paint a false face on each side with the buskins of words, is well enough known. Such people are accustomed to put forward a "holy" deceit as a cover. But truth needs no deceit, and a deceit by which the truth is obscured, and which is joined with some pretence, cannot be called holy. Whatever is of this kind belongs to the nature of the devil, whom we know to be a liar and an impostor. Above all, then, let ministers take care not to falsify the word of the Lord. This happens when either the chaff of human inventions is mixed with the Lord's wheat, or the Word of God is twisted to a foreign meaning. Those who seek their own advantage rather than the glory of God and the building up of the churches generally do this.

units.la: Addit in præsenti Paulus: Sed declaratione Veritatis commendantes nosipsos apud omnem conscientiam hominum in conspectu Dei. Id est, non aliam gloriam siue commendationem quærimus, quam quæ ex fideli muneris nobis crediti administratione nascitur. Itaque sic agimus, vt non vereamur ipsas hominum conscientias appellare, & in ipsius Dei conspectu nos quibusuis offerre, vt in nos & doctrinam nostram inquirant, eamq; ad regulam Verbi Dei examinent. Quo loco ministri admonentur, quid ipsis spectandum sit, si quando iniquis hominum iudicijs sese premi sentiunt. Accidit id Paulo. Quid autem ille? Num ideo mutata docendi ratione, in posterum omnibus placere studuit? Vel num fuco externo sese occultauit? Nequaquam. Sciebat enim se seruum Christi non fore, si hominibus placere vellet. Hoc ergo curauit, vt quorumuis conscientias, & quidem aduersariorum quoque, suæ fidei & integritatis testes haberet. Id verò facile obtinere poterat, cum se Deo probari sciret, qui in omnium conscientias ius habet. Idem olim Mosem, Samuelem, Dauidem & alios Dei seruos factitauisse legimus.
units.tr: Paul adds here: "But by the manifestation of the truth commending ourselves to every man's conscience in the sight of God." That is, we seek no other glory or commendation than that which arises from the faithful administration of the office entrusted to us. So we act in such a way that we are not afraid to call men's consciences themselves to witness, and to present ourselves before anyone in the sight of God himself, so that they may examine us and our teaching and test it by the rule of God's Word. Here ministers are reminded what they should look to when they feel pressed by the unjust judgments of men. This happened to Paul. But what did he do? Did he change his manner of teaching so as to please everyone from then on? Or did he hide himself behind outward pretence? By no means. For he knew that he would not be a servant of Christ if he wished to please men. Therefore he took care to have the consciences of everyone, and indeed of his opponents too, as witnesses to his faith and integrity. This he could easily obtain, since he knew himself approved before God, who has right over the consciences of all. We read that Moses, Samuel, David and other servants of God did the same long ago.

units.la: Magna igitur virtutis vis est, quæ pessimorum quoq; hominum conscientias potest conuincere. Exemplum eius rei euidens in Saule habetur, cui Dauidis fides & integritas tot modis perspecta, non modo veri confessionem, verumetiam lachrymas expressit. E contra arguitur hisce rum deplorata contumacia, qui cum intra conscientias suas sese conuictos esse sentiant, adhuc tamen contra Veritatem & eius ministros pugnare pergunt, & furiosorum instar quæuis temere arripiunt, quæ in illos eiaculentur. Faciebant hoc Pauli æmuli, quos plerique ex nostris aduersarijs
units.tr: Great, therefore, is the force of virtue, which can convict even the consciences of the worst men. A clear example of this is found in Saul, whom David's faith and integrity, so often proved in many ways, moved not only to confess the truth but even to tears. On the other hand, the stubborn obstinacy of those is condemned who, though they feel within their own consciences that they have been convicted, nevertheless keep on fighting against the truth and its ministers, and, like madmen, seize at random whatever they can hurl at them. Paul's rivals did this, and most of our opponents

units.la: Philip.3.
units.tr: Philip. 3.
1 Cor. 2.

units.la: Quid faciant ministri, ne cogantur latebras quærere.
units.tr: What ministers should do, so that they are not forced to seek hiding places.

units.la: Conscientias aliorum appellant testes.
units.tr: They call others' consciences to witness.

units.la: Virtutis vis magna.
units.tr: The great force of virtue.

units.la: Hostium veritatis contumacia. sarijs hodie imitantur. Fatentur enim hi nobiscum Scripturas sacras, communem nobiscum habent Symboli Apostolici confessionem, orationem Dominicam, Decalogum, veterum item Conciliorum Symbola. Neque negare possunt, Dei Filium IESVM CHRISTVM, ideo in mundum venisse, ut nos seruarent: imò Diuos caelites hoc nomine colunt, quòd in fide Christi constantes, eam aliis tradiderunt, & pro eadem martyrio coronati sunt. Interim nos haereticos esse dicunt, & quousque supplicio dignos, qui illorum doctrinam constanter retinemus, nec eo contenti, ipsum Euangelium aperte oppugnant, quòd Diui illi olim praedicarunt, & pro cuius assertione dirissimos exquisitissimorum tormentorum cruciatus sustinuerunt. Ad eam verò insaniam eos iusto iudicio Deus devenire finit, ut quoniam affectus suos pravos Veritati & gloriae Dei anteponunt, excusso simul cum pudore sensu communi, in propriis conscientias peccent. Sed plura de his mox sequentur. Nunc observemus diligenter, qua fide Apostoli egerint, & proinde eorum doctrinam totis animis complectamur, neque ideo ei reluctemur, quòd nostris cupiditatibus minus conuenit: sed Deum potius oremus, ut Filij sui, IESV CHRISTI, vera cognitione illuminatos seruet & regat ad nominis sui gloriam. Illi debetur benedictio, honor, gloria & potestas in aeternum. Amen.
units.tr: Obstinacy of the enemies of the truth. imitate today. For they agree with us that the holy Scriptures are sacred, they hold in common with us the confession of the Apostles' Creed, the Lord's Prayer, the Decalogue, and likewise the creeds of the ancient Councils. Nor can they deny that the Son of God, IESVM CHRISTVM, came into the world for this reason, that he might save us; indeed, they worship the heavenly saints under this name, because they remained constant in the faith of Christ, handed it on to others, and were crowned with martyrdom for it. Meanwhile they say that we are heretics, and deserving of punishment to whatever degree, because we steadfastly hold to their doctrine; and not content with this, they openly attack the very Gospel that those holy men once preached, and for whose defence they endured the most dreadful torments of the most exquisite kinds. God, by a just judgment, allows them to fall into such madness, so that, since they put their depraved desires before the truth and the glory of God, they sin against their own consciences, with common sense shaken off along with shame. But more about these things will follow shortly. Now let us observe carefully with what faith the Apostles acted, and so embrace their teaching with our whole souls, and not resist it because it agrees less with our desires; rather let us pray God that he keep and rule his Son's IESV CHRISTI people, enlightened by true knowledge, to the glory of his name. To him be blessing, honour, glory and power for ever. Amen.

units.la: HOMILIA XVI.
units.tr: HOMILY XVI.

units.la: Quòd si tectum est Euangelium nostrum, in ijs qui pereunt tectum est: in quibus Deus huius seculi excaecauit mentes infidelium, ne irradiet eos lumen Euangelij gloriae Christi, qui est imago Dei. Non enim nosipsos praedicamus, sed CHRISTVM IESVM, Dominum, nos autem seruos vestros propter IESVM. Quoniam Deus qui dixit, ut e tenebris lux splendesceret, is splenduit in cordibus nostris ad illuminationem cognitionis in facie IESV CHRISTI.
units.tr: But if our Gospel is veiled, it is veiled among those who are perishing, in whom the God of this age has blinded the minds of unbelievers, lest the light of the gospel of the glory of Christ, who is the image of God, should shine on them. For we do not preach ourselves, but CHRIST JESUS as Lord, and ourselves as your servants for JESUS' sake. For God, who said, "Let light shine out of darkness," has shone in our hearts, to give the light of the knowledge of God in the face of JESUS CHRIST.

units.la: Ipsi Euangelium, aeternum Dei Verbum sit, quo is suam voluntatem nobis reuelat, seque ipsum cum bonis suis omnibus nobis offert, tanta tamen est mundi peruersitas, ut plerique illud fastidiant, multi etiam oderint, eò quòd illud prauis suis affectibus obstare sentiunt. Sunt igitur hic duo admodum necessaria observanda. Primum, ut de eo rectè iudicare discamus: quòd nimirum sit Verbum vitae, Regni Dei nuntium, lucerna mundi, thesaurus omne in se bonum continens, & margarita illa pretiosa, propter quam omnium facultatum iactura fieri debeat. Alterum, qua fide illud Apostoli tradiderint. Utrumque Paulus in praesenti tractatione tradit. Hactenus enim ostendit, Euangelium esse ministerium vitae & iustitiae, per quod Dei imago in nobis instauretur. Quibus adde, quòd alibi illud potentiam Dei saluificam dixit, & quòd à Petro semen regenerationis dicitur. Nuper verò fidem & integritatem suam, qua in illo praedicando vsus sit, graviter asseruit. Vbi de eorum, quae dixit, veritate dubitare non possumus, quando cogitamus, illum ijs scripsisse, & eorum conscientias appellauisse, qui omnia eius calumniabantur. Accedit his, quòd fidem & studium suum Apostoli tot laboribus atque periculis, & tandem mortis quoq; & proprij sanguinis testimonio toti mundo approbauerunt: à quibus omnibus immunes esse poterant, si Dei gloriam & hominum salutem voluissent negligere, aut si aliam salutis rationem extra Christum inueniri posse sciuissent. Quid, quod ipse Dei Filius iniquitatis accusari poterat, si propter Euangelium, quo carere poteramus (ut impij quidam loquuntur) homines innocentes, qui se totos ipsi consecrarant, voluisset periculis tam diris obijcere.
units.tr: The Gospel itself is the eternal Word of God, by which he reveals his will to us and offers himself with all his good things to us. Yet the perversity of the world is so great that many loathe it, and many even hate it, because they feel it stands in the way of their evil desires. There are therefore two things here that must be carefully observed. The first is that we learn to judge it rightly: namely, that it is the Word of life, the message of the kingdom of God, the lamp of the world, a treasure containing every good within itself, and that pearl of great price for which all our possessions ought to be given up. The second is with what faith the apostles delivered it. Paul sets out both in the present discussion. For so far he has shown that the Gospel is the ministry of life and righteousness, through which the image of God is restored in us. To these add that elsewhere he calls it the saving power of God, and that it is said by Peter to be the seed of regeneration. More recently he has strongly affirmed his faith and integrity, with which he has used it in preaching. Here we cannot doubt the truth of what he said, when we consider that he wrote to those who were slandering everything about him and appealed to their consciences. To this is added that the apostles, by so many labours and dangers, and finally by the witness of death and of their own blood, approved their faith and zeal before the whole world. They could have been free of all these things if they had wished to neglect the glory of God and the salvation of men, or if they had known that another way of salvation could be found outside Christ. Moreover, what of the fact that the Son of God himself could be accused of wickedness, if for the sake of the Gospel, which we could do without (as some impious men say), he had wished to expose innocent men, who had wholly consecrated themselves to him, to such dire dangers?

units.la: Sed ut ad praesentis loci explicationem accedamus, poterat aliquis obijcere: Si tam bona fide & absque omni dolo hucusque sermonem Dei praedicauisti, qui fit quòd tuam praedicationem siue doctrinam non omnes recipiant? cur plerique ei reluctantur? cur denique multis non minus tenebrosa & obscura est, quàm Iudaeis Lex Mosaica fuit, ut tu modo dixisti? Huic ergo obiectioni per Praeoccupationem respondet, quae Concessionis speciem habet: Quòd si tectum est Euangelium nostrum, in ijs qui pereunt tectum est, &c. Euangelium suum dicit, non quòd ipse huius author effet, aut sibi in illud ius & imperium vendicaret, sed per Mimesim ex aduersariorum sententia loquitur, qui illud ea occasione pro ludibrio haberent, quòd Pauli esse dicerent: eorum nimirum similes, qui hodie etiam clamant: Nescimus quale nam sit nouum illud Lutheri & Zuinglij Euangelium, &c. Vt ergo offendat, ipsum eius nequaquam pudere, sic loquitur sub Concessionis specie, vt modò diximus, & sensus est: Fateor equidem complures esse, qui Euangelium hoc, cuius ego minister sum, non agnoscunt, & in densissimis ignorantiae tenebris demersi haerent, deq; illius obscuritate queruntur, vel etiam audacter illud reiciunt. Sed istorum caecitas siue ignorantia illius luci aut splendori nihil derogat. Nam illis solis velatum siue tectum est, qui pereunt, id est, qui ad perditionem destinati sunt, ideoque indigni sunt, quorum exemplo aliquis electorum moueatur: quin potius omnes eo terreri debent, ne illud imitentur. Et mox eosdem describit, qui nam & quales sint: In quibus Deus huius saeculi excaecauit mentes infidelium, ne irradiet eos lumen Euangelij gloriae Christi, &c. Vocat autem Deum huius saeculi diabolum, eadem ratione, qua eum Dominus in Euangelio principem huius mundi dicit: Non quidem quòd reuera Deus sit, aut ius aliquod in mundum habeat legitimum: sed per Catachresim, & eorum respectu, qui toti huic saeculo immersi, non nisi terrena curant, & diabolo seruiunt: dum prava carnis desideria sectantur. Sic quorundam Deus dicitur Mammon & Venter, vt nuper ex Epistola ad Philippen. audiuimus. At si proprie loquendum est, scimus Deum vnum esse, ad quem terrae & omnium, quae in ea sunt, imperium pertinet, & qui idem Dominus est saeculorum omnium. Sunt autem in his quaedam diligentius consideranda.
units.tr: But to come to the explanation of the present passage, someone could object: "If you have preached the word of God so honestly and without any deceit up to now, how is it that not everyone accepts your preaching or teaching? Why do many resist it? Why, finally, is it to many no less dark and obscure than the Mosaic Law was to the Jews, as you have just said?" To this objection he replies beforehand, by way of anticipation, in the form of a concession: "But if our Gospel is veiled, it is veiled among those who are perishing," etc. He calls it "our Gospel" not because he was its author, or claimed any right or authority over it for himself, but he speaks by mimesis, in the words of his opponents, who on that account would mock it because they said it was Paul's: people like those who even today cry out, "We do not know what that new gospel of Luther and Zwingli is," etc. So that he may not offend, he speaks in the form of a concession, as we have just said, and the sense is this: "I grant indeed that there are many who do not acknowledge this Gospel, whose minister I am, and who remain sunk in the thickest darkness of ignorance, complaining of its obscurity, or even boldly rejecting it. But the blindness or ignorance of these people takes nothing away from its light and splendour. For it is veiled only to those who are perishing, that is, to those who are destined for destruction, and who are therefore unworthy that any of the elect should be moved by their example; rather, all should be terrified lest they imitate them." And immediately he describes who and what sort of people these are: "in whom the God of this age has blinded the minds of unbelievers, lest the light of the gospel of the glory of Christ should shine on them," etc. He calls the devil "the god of this age" for the same reason that the Lord in the Gospel calls him "the prince of this world": not that he is truly God or has any lawful right over the world, but by catachresis, and with regard to those who, immersed in this whole age, care only for earthly things and serve the devil while they pursue the depraved desires of the flesh. Thus Mammon and the belly are called the gods of some people, as we heard recently from the Epistle to the Philippians. But if we speak properly, we know that there is one God, to whom the earth and all that is in it belong, and who is the same Lord of all ages. There are, however, some points in these words that must be considered more carefully.

units.la: Primum, quòd perditionis filios eos esse pronuntiat, qui Euangelij doctrinam non agnoscunt, neque recipiunt. Est hoc magnae fiduciae argumentum, quae Paulum de sua doctrina certissimum fuisse docet, & qua omnes eos armatos esse oportet, qui in hoc ministerio versantur. Interim admonemur contemptum Euangelij pertinacem reprobationis signum esse, sicuti è diuerso fides electionis nota est, secundum illud: Oues meae vocem meam audiunt, & sequuntur eam: Item: Qui audit verba mea, & credit ei qui misit me, habet vitam aeternam. Etenim in Euangelio vox Christi sonat, per quam se totum ille nobis offert. Et quia idem ille solus nobis à Patre iustitia factus est, & solus eundem nobis placat, sequitur, iram Dei (sicuti Baptista testatus est) super omnes manere, qui illum audire dedignantur, neque in eum credunt. Obseruabis autem, hoc non nisi de pertinaci incredulitate, aut pertinacia incurabili dici, quae peccatum est in spiritum sanctum. At quia haec nobis fere incognita est, nec scire possumus, qualis quisque in posterum futurus sit, non temere de quoquam debemus pronuntiare, sed potius preces pro illis fundere ad Deum, qui nunc increduli sunt, & Euangelio audacius reluctantur. Verumtamen certum est, eos qui in finem vsq; increduli esse pergunt, in ista contumacia sua moriuntur, simul in eadem aeternum perire.
units.tr: First, he declares that those who do not acknowledge or receive the doctrine of the Gospel are sons of perdition. This is a sign of great confidence, which shows that Paul was most certain about his doctrine, and with which all who are engaged in this ministry ought to be armed. Meanwhile we are reminded that contempt for the Gospel is a sign of stubborn reprobation, just as on the other hand faith is the mark of election, according to the words: "My sheep hear my voice, and they follow me"; likewise: "He who hears my words and believes him who sent me has eternal life." For in the Gospel the voice of Christ sounds, through which he offers himself wholly to us. And because he alone has been made righteousness for us by the Father, and alone reconciles us to him, it follows that the wrath of God (as the Baptist testified) remains upon all who disdain to hear him and do not believe in him. You will observe, however, that this is said only of obstinate unbelief, or of an incurable obstinacy, which is the sin against the Holy Spirit. But since this is almost unknown to us, and we cannot know what each person will be in the future, we ought not rashly to pronounce judgment on anyone, but rather pour out prayers to God for those who are now unbelieving and resist the Gospel more boldly. Nevertheless it is certain that those who continue unbelieving to the end die in that obstinacy, and at the same time perish eternally in it.

units.la: Deinde de Excaecationis & indurationis istius authore nos locus hic admonet. Est is Deus huius saeculi, Diabolus. Alibi Deus ipse excaecare & indurare dicitur: & certum est, diabolum absque huius permissione nihil posse: quod Micheas Propheta Achabo Regi exitium denuntians eleganti visione docuit. Quia autem Dei iudicia sunt iustitia & veritas, probe in tota hac causa tenere oportet, causam excaecationis propriam in nobis esse, qui natura praui s desiderijs ardemus, & terrenis addicti caelestia negligimus. Itaq; excaecat & indurat Deus, non quod nouam in nobis malitiam creet, (ea enim nequaquam opus est nobis, qui quanti quanti sumus, nihil quàm peccatum sumus) sed dum iusto iudicio nos nobisipsis permittit, & diabolo tradit, qui in sensum reprobum abreptos pro sua libidine versat. Quod magno nostro merito fieri, exempla docent. Quis enim Pharaonem indignum fuisse dixerit, quem Deus induraret, & in quo potentiam & vindictam suam iustam ostenderet, qui horribiles recens natorum infantium caedes & iniustam in Israelitas meliora de Ægypto meritos tyrannidem, cum impia & Cyclopica illa voce diligentius expendent: Quis est Iehoua, vt audiam vocē eius? Idem de Achabo dicemus, si quae ante extremum hunc actum ille fecit, consideremus. Eadem posteà fuit gentis Iudaicae conditio, quae multiplici & sceleratò Euangelij contemptu se dignam offendit, quae incurabili caecitate multata male periret.
units.tr: Next, this passage reminds us about the author of this blinding and hardening. He is the god of this age, the devil. Elsewhere God himself is said to blind and harden, and it is certain that the devil can do nothing without his permission, as the prophet Micaiah taught with a striking vision when he announced ruin to King Ahab. But since the judgments of God are justice and truth, we must hold firmly throughout this whole matter that the proper cause of blindness lies in us, who burn with depraved natural desires and, devoted to earthly things, neglect heavenly ones. God therefore blinds and hardens, not because he creates a new wickedness in us (for there is no need of that in us, who, however great we are, are nothing but sin), but while by his just judgment he allows us to ourselves and hands us over to the devil, who carries us off into a reprobate mind and drives us about at his own pleasure. That this happens with great justice on our part, examples teach. For who would say that Pharaoh did not deserve it, that God should harden him and show in him his power and his just vengeance, when he weighed carefully the horrible recent slaughter of infants and his unjust tyranny against Israelites who had deserved better of Egypt, and that impious and Cyclopean word: "Who is Jehovah, that I should hear his voice?" We will say the same of Ahab, if we consider what he did before this last act. Afterwards the condition of the Jewish nation was the same, which by its manifold and wicked contempt of the Gospel showed itself worthy, and, afflicted with an incurable blindness, perished miserably.

units.la: Sic gentes, cum contempta Dei cognitione, qua is se illis reuelauerat, ex sui ingenij acumine in illius maiestatem altius inuestigare ausi sunt, & eius gloriam cum foedissimorum animalium imaginibus gentibus commutarunt, merito ab eodem in reprobum sensum traditi sunt, ut nephariis libidinibus sua quoque propria corpora polluerent. Et si ad nostra tempora accedamus, de nostri quoque seculi hominibus intelligi debet, quod Christus ait: Haec est condemnatio, quod Lux venit in mundum, sed dilexerunt homines tenebras potius quam lucem. Quis ergo non dixerit dignos, qui in tenebris pereant? Et huc pertinet, quod Paulus Antichristo suis dolis & artibus in eos ius fore dicit, qui Veritatis doctrinam ipsis affulgentem nolunt recipere. Propterea (inquit) mittet illis Deus efficacitatem deceptionis, ut credant mendacio: ut damnentur omnes, qui non crediderunt Veritati, sed acquieuerunt in iniustitia. Nulla ergo ratio est, quae nos Deum vel peccati vel nostrae perditionis authorem facere iubeat. Ut enim nostra sponte peccamus ex propria natura nostrae vitiositate, ita perditio ex nobis est, ex Deo autem salus nostra. Admonent ergo haec ne oblatam nobis diuinitus Euangelij lucem respuamus, ne idem nobis quoq; contingat. Incredulitate enim & contumacia occasio datur diabolo, ut vel prauis opinionibus de Deo nos decipiat, vel superstitionibus aut sceleribus nos immergat, ad quae natura nostra plus satis proclivis est.
units.tr: So the nations, having despised the knowledge of God by which he had revealed himself to them, dared to investigate his majesty more deeply by the keenness of their own minds, and exchanged his glory for images of the most foul animals. Therefore God justly handed them over to a reprobate mind, so that they polluted their own bodies with unspeakable lusts. If we come down to our own times, what Christ says must be understood of the people of our age too: "This is the condemnation, that light has come into the world, but men loved darkness rather than light." Who then would not say that those who perish in darkness deserve it? To this belongs also what Paul says: that Antichrist, by his deceits and arts, will have power over those who are unwilling to receive the doctrine of the truth shining upon them. "For this reason," he says, "God will send them a working of deception, so that they believe the lie, and so that all may be condemned who did not believe the truth but consented to unrighteousness." So there is no reason that should bid us make God the author either of sin or of our destruction. For as we sin of our own accord, from the vice of our own nature, so the destruction is from us, but our salvation is from God. These words therefore warn us not to reject the light of the gospel offered to us from heaven, lest the same thing happen to us too. For by unbelief and obstinacy an opening is given to the devil, so that he may deceive us either with wicked opinions about God, or plunge us into superstitions or crimes, to which our nature is more than prone enough.

units.la: Et huc facit finis, propter quem diabolus homines excaecat, de quo Paulus sic loquitur: Ne irradiet eos lumen Euangelij gloriae Christi, qui est imago Dei, id est, Euangelium illud, quo gloria IESV CHRISTI nobis revelatur. Etenim Satan totus in eo est, ut homines a vera salutis via abductos aeternae perditioni mancipet. At salus nostra a Veritatis Euangelicae cognitione dependet, quod Paulus non obscure innuit, quando in priori ad Timoth. scribit: Deus vult omnes homines salvos fieri, & in Veritatis notitiam venire. Nam hoc dicendo, Veritatis cognitionem & salutem res coniunctas esse ostendit. Et consentit ei Christus, dicens: Si manseritis in sermone meo, cognoscetis Veritatem, & Veritas reddet vos liberos. Quo Constantinus respiciens ad Synodum Tyriam scribebat: ὁ τὼ ἀλλθειαν ἀγνοῶν, ὁ τὸν θεὸν ἐπιγινώσκει, id est, qui Veritatem ignorat, is ne Deum quidem agnoscit. Etenim Veritas est ipse aeternus Dei Filius, IESVS CHRISTVS, in quo promissiones quoq; Dei omnes sunt Etiam & Amen, sicuti in primo Cap. didicimus. Ergo huius cognitioni Satan se ipse maxime opponit, quod in praesenti Apostolus monet, quando illum homines ideo excaecare dicit, ne irradiet eos lumen Euangelij gloriae Christi, qui est imago Dei. Et hoc de Christo addit, ut quanta sit excaecationis huius efficacitas ostendat, quando ipsam quoq; Dei imaginem nobis obscuriorem facere potest. Sic autem proprie dicitur Christus, non quod nuda solummodo Dei imago, non autem revera Deus ipse sit, sed quod Patris imago vi-ua est atque essentialis, in qua Deus, qui natura invisibilis est, se nobis repraesentat & cognoscendum praebet, secundum illud Euangelistae dictum: Deum nemo vidit unquam, Vnigenitus autem ille Filius, qui est in sinu Patris, manifestauit nobis. Quo etiam pertinet, quod Paulus de Christo loquens, Deum in carne manifestatum esse scribit. Itaque nemo ex praesenti loco colligat: Si imago Dei est Christus, ergo non est verus Deus. Si enim de essentia sermo sit, perpetuo verum est, quod ille dixit: Ego & Pater unum sumus. Ite, qui me videt, Patrem videt. Non credis quod ego sum in Patre, & Pater in me? Quoad vero pietatis mysterium (ut Paulus loquitur) cui ex aeterno Patris decreto destinatus fuit, illius imago dicitur, eo quod in eo nobis manifesta fiunt, quaecunque ad veram & salutarem Dei cognitionem faciunt.
units.tr: And to this end, for which the devil blinds men, Paul speaks thus: "lest the light of the gospel of the glory of Christ, who is the image of God, should shine upon them." That is, the gospel by which the glory of JESUS CHRIST is revealed to us. For Satan is wholly intent on handing men, led away from the true way of salvation, over to eternal perdition. But our salvation depends on the knowledge of the gospel truth, as Paul hints not obscurely when he writes in the first letter to Timothy: "God wills all men to be saved and to come to the knowledge of the truth." For by saying this he shows that knowledge of the truth and salvation are joined together. Christ agrees with him, saying: "If you abide in my word, you will know the truth, and the truth will make you free." Looking to this, Constantine wrote to the Synod of Tyre: ὁ τὴν ἀλήθειαν ἀγνοῶν, ὁ τὸν θεὸν ἐπιγινώσκει [he who is ignorant of the truth does not even know God]. Truly the Truth is the eternal Son of God himself, JESUS CHRIST, in whom all the promises of God are "Yea and Amen," as we learned in the first chapter. Therefore Satan sets himself most strongly against this knowledge, which the Apostle warns of in the present passage, when he says that men are blinded by him, lest the light of the gospel of the glory of Christ, who is the image of God, should shine upon them. And he adds this about Christ to show how great the power of this blinding is, since it can make even the image of God itself less clear to us. Christ is called the image in this proper sense not because he is merely a bare image of God and not really God himself, but because he is the living and essential image of the Father, in whom God, who is invisible by nature, presents himself to us and offers himself to be known, according to the saying of the evangelist: "No one has ever seen God; the only-begotten Son, who is in the bosom of the Father, has made him known to us." To this also belongs what Paul writes about Christ, that God was manifested in the flesh. Therefore let no one gather from the present passage: "If Christ is the image of God, then he is not the true God." For if the discussion concerns his essence, it is always true what he said: "I and the Father are one." "He who sees me sees the Father." "Do you not believe that I am in the Father, and the Father in me?" But as regards the mystery of godliness (as Paul speaks), to which he was destined from the eternal decree of the Father, he is called the image of the Father, because in him are made manifest to us all those things which pertain to the true and saving knowledge of God.

units.la: Porro quoad praesentem locum, discimus, nullam esse veri Dei cognitionem absque Christo, & proinde ne cultum quidem Dei aliquem esse apud eos, qui illius cognitione destituuntur, quae ex solo Euangelio discitur. Docet hoc ipse, apud Ioannem dicens: Qui non honorat Filium, is ne Patrem quidem honorat. Sufficit hoc ad euertendum omnes aliarum gentium superstitiones, quae salutem alibi quam in uno IESV CHRISTO monstrant. Sequitur etiam ex huius loci authoritate, diaboli ministros & seruos esse omnes eos, quotquot Euangelij doctrinae obstant, ne per eam vera Christi cognitio hominibus manifestetur. Imo ijdem pessimi & nocentissimi generis humani hostes sunt: quia publicae saluti officiunt, non contenti seipsos perdidisse, nisi plures alios secum in exitium abripiant. Econtra & Deo fideles sunt, & publicae saluti optime consulunt, qui Euangelij praedicationem promouent, ut Veritatis lux per eam longe lateq; spargatur.
units.tr: Further, as regards the present passage, we learn that there is no true knowledge of God apart from Christ, and therefore that there is no worship of God at all among those who lack the knowledge of him that is learned from the gospel alone. He himself teaches this, saying in John: "He who does not honour the Son does not honour the Father either." This is enough to overthrow all the superstitions of the other nations, which point to salvation anywhere but in the one JESUS CHRIST. It also follows from the authority of this passage that all who oppose the teaching of the gospel, so that the true knowledge of Christ may not be made known to men through it, are the ministers and slaves of the devil. Indeed they are the most wicked enemies and most harmful of the human race, because they hinder the common salvation, not content to have destroyed themselves unless they drag many others with them into ruin. On the contrary, those who promote the preaching of the gospel, so that the light of the truth may be spread far and wide through it, are both faithful to God and most excellently care for the common salvation.

units.la: Caeterum redit Paulus ad asserendam fidem sui ministerij: & quia nuper dixerat, se potuisse esse, ut se examini omnium conscientiarum sistat in conspectu Dei, nunc unde haec fiducia ipsi facerit nascatur, docet. Non enim (inquit) nosipsos prædicamus, sed CHRISTVM IESVM; Dominum, nos autem seruos vestros propter IESVM. Seipsos prædicant, qui non Christi, sed suam causam agunt, dum vel gloriæ triuatæ, vel quæstui student, & ideo sibi ipsis discipulos faciunt, non Christo. Id vero faciunt non modo qui à Christo prorsus alieni sunt, verumetiam interdum qui illum semper in ore habent. Ideo hic se in magno illo die multis, qui dicunt, Domine Domine; respon-surum ait: Non novi vos, &c. Rursus ergo Paulus hic pseudoapostolos perstringit, qui cum etiam ipsi vellent Christi prædicares haberi, hoc tamen vnum agebant, vt ipsi supra omnes eminerent, & proinde sectarum manifesti erant authores. Rursus CHRISTVM IESVM prædicare Dominum, est omnes ad hunc deducere, vt eum suum vindicem, redemptorem & Dominum agnoscant, ei vni fidant, vnum colant, seq; totos ei subijciant. Huc ergo respiciens Paulus, ait: Non nosipsos prædicamus, sed CHRISTVM IESVM, Dominum, nos autem seruos vestros propter IESVM: qui scilicet ita vos dilexit, vt me vobis seruum dederit. Huic igitur obedire studeo, & propter hunc facio quæcunque facio, non priuati quæstus aut gloriæ studio. Et hæc illum vere scripsisse, ex eo apparet, quod solum Christum eis prædicauit, & ne à seipso quidem aliquos denominari voluit, cum in diuersas sectas scindi cœpissent. Ita vero simul stolidam Corinthiorum ingratitudinem perstringit, qui hoc eius studium non agnoscebant, sed ipsum reijcientes, qui eorum seruus esse cupiebat, eos audirebant, qui superbum in illos dominium affectabant, non sine publica eorum ignominia.
units.tr: Moreover, Paul returns to asserting the trustworthiness of his ministry, and because he had said just before that it could happen that he would stand before the judgement of the consciences of all in the sight of God, he now teaches whence this confidence of his arises. "For," he says, "we do not preach ourselves, but CHRIST JESUS as Lord, and ourselves as your servants for JESUS' sake." Those preach themselves who do not act for Christ's cause but for their own, while they pursue either private glory or gain, and therefore make disciples for themselves and not for Christ. And they do this not only those who are wholly alien to Christ, but sometimes also those who always have him on their lips. Therefore he says that in that great day he will answer many who say, "Lord, Lord": "I never knew you," etc. Again, then, Paul here censures the false apostles, who, while they also wanted to be regarded as preachers of Christ, yet pursued this one aim, that they themselves should stand out above all others, and therefore were evident authors of sects. Again, to preach CHRIST JESUS as Lord is to lead everyone to this, that they acknowledge him as their defender, redeemer and Lord, trust in him alone, worship him alone, and submit themselves wholly to him. Looking to this, Paul says: "We do not preach ourselves, but CHRIST JESUS, as Lord, and ourselves as your servants for JESUS' sake," namely, because he loved you so much that he gave me to you as a servant. Therefore I strive to obey him, and for his sake I do whatever I do, not from a desire for private gain or glory. And that he truly wrote these things is clear from the fact that he preached to them only Christ, and did not wish even to be named after himself when they had begun to split into different sects. At the same time he rebukes the foolish ingratitude of the Corinthians, who did not recognise this zeal of his, but rejected him, who wished to be their servant, and listened to those who aimed at a proud lordship over them, to their public disgrace.

units.la: Rursus autem ministri Ecclesiarum sui officij admonentur. Primum eius caput est, vt non seipsos prædicent, sed vnum IESVM CHRISTVM. Est hoc necessarium valde, eò quòd in illo vno salus habetur, neq; aliud nomen sub cœlo hominibus datum est, in quo nos seruari oporteat. Et qui seipsos quærunt, ne ipsi quidem credere possunt. Vnde Christus Iudæorum sacerdotibus dicebat: Quomodo vos potestis credere, cum gloriam alij ab alijs captetis, & gloriâ, quæ à solo Deo proficiscitur, non quæritis? Et sane scribit Ioannes, multos ex principibus credidisse in IESVM, sed nonausos fuisse illum profiteri propter pharisæos, ne ex synagoga eijcerentur. Hic ergo nostri ipsius abnegatione opus est, sine qua nihil proficiemus. Deinde meminerint, se ecclesiæ seruos esse, non dominos. Gloriatur quide hoc titulo Papa, sed quàm ridicule, imò quàm scurriliter sub eo toti orbi Christiano insultet, res ipsa loquitur. Seruitium enim Ecclesiæ non inani titulo constat, sed doctrina & assiduo publicæ omnium salutis studio: qua de re multa præclarè dicuntur Ezech. 34. Actor. 20. 2. Tim. 4. Finis autem omnium est, vt homines Christo adducantur: ideoq; omnia ministri propter illum facere debent, qui eos gregi suo præfecit. Quid ergo de illis iudices, qui homines perire malunt, quàm suæ existimationi & quæstui aliquid decedere? Itaq; Pauli exemplum imitentur, qui germani Christi serui esse volunt.
units.tr: Again, the ministers of the churches are reminded of their office. Its first head is that they should preach not themselves but the one JESUS CHRIST. This is very necessary, because salvation is found in him alone, and "there is no other name under heaven given to men by which we must be saved." Those who seek themselves cannot even believe. Hence Christ said to the priests of the Jews: "How can you believe, when you seek glory from one another, and do not seek the glory that comes from God alone?" And indeed John writes that many of the leaders believed in JESUS, but did not dare to confess him because of the Pharisees, lest they be cast out of the synagogue. Here, then, there is need of self-denial, without which we shall accomplish nothing. Next, let them remember that they are servants of the Church, not its lords. The Pope indeed boasts of this title, but how ridiculously, or rather how scurrilously, he insults the whole Christian world under it, the thing itself speaks. For the service of the Church does not consist in an empty title, but in teaching and in constant zeal for the common salvation of all, concerning which many excellent things are said in Ezekiel 34, Acts 20, and 2 Timothy 4. The aim of all is that men be brought to Christ, and therefore ministers ought to do everything for the sake of him who set them over his flock. What then will you think of those who prefer that men perish rather than that anything be lost from their reputation and gain? Let them therefore imitate the example of Paul, who want to be the true servants of Christ.

units.la: E contra Christianorum hominum est, pastores suos ita pro seruis suis agnoscere, vt eos sine mul Christi seruos esse meminerint. Hic enim multum hodie peccatur, maximè à principibus viris, qui doctores aut Verbi præcones seruorum quidem loco habent, sed eorum, in quos ipsis ius sit, quibus dicendi & tacendi leges pro sua libidine præscribant, vt olim Iudæorum principes, qui Prophetis dicebant: Ne prophetetis, neq; stilletis: Ne videatis, ne contemplemini nobis plana loquimini, ni nobis blanda, contemplamini illusiones, recedite à via, declinate à semita, facite quiescere à facie nostra Sanctum Israelis. Hæc & horum similia hodie ex multorum ore audiuntur, qui præcipui Euangelicæ doctrinæ patroni haberi volunt, si quando liberius ob vitia sua corripiantur, aut officij admoneantur. At non eiusmodi seruos Ecclesiæ suæ Christus dedit, qui talium hominum petulantibus edictis aut minis cedant. Et tu quis es, qui in seruum alienum tibi ius & imperium vendicas? Imò qui IESV CHRISTI seruum pro tuo arbitrio loqui aut tacere iubes? Discant potius Christiani homines Ecclesiæ ministros ex Christi maiestate & munere sui dignitate æstimare, eosq; legatos Domini exercituum esse meminerint.
units.tr: On the other hand, it is the duty of Christians to acknowledge their ministers as servants of their own, yet to remember that they are first and foremost servants of Christ. For much wrong is done today, chiefly by men of high rank, who regard teachers and heralds of the Word as servants, but as servants of the kind over whom they hold authority, and whom they prescribe what they may say and keep silent about, according to their own whim. So did the princes of the Jews of old, who said to the prophets: "Do not prophesy, do not preach; do not see, do not look at us; speak smooth things to us, look at illusions; turn aside from the way, leave the path, make the Holy One of Israel cease from before our face." Words like these and their like are heard today from the mouths of many who want to be considered the chief patrons of the Gospel doctrine, if at any time they are rebuked more freely for their faults or reminded of their duty. But Christ did not give his Church servants of this sort, who yield to the insolent edicts or threats of such men. And who are you, who claim right and rule over another's servant? Or rather, who command the servant of JESUS CHRIST to speak or be silent at your pleasure? Let Christian people rather learn to value the ministers of the Church by the majesty of Christ and the dignity of their office, and remember that they are ambassadors of the Lord of hosts.

units.la: Sed rationem reddit Paulus, cur solum IESVM CHRISTVM prædicet, non seipsum, cur item se ipsorum seruum esse profiteatur. Quoniam Deus est, qui dixit, vt ex tenebris lux splenderet: is splenduit in cordibus nostris ad illuminationem cognitionis in facie IESV CHRISTI. STI. Sensus horum verborum est: Quia non nostrum, sed Dei negotium agimus. Vt enim in olim in creatione mundi, cum omnem illam massam, Verbi virtute ex nihilo produĉtam, tenebrae occuparent, eodem Verbo lucem e tenebris protulit: ita etiam nunc, cum ignorantia tenebrae totum terrarum orbem occupauissent, ille ipse nostris cordibus illuxit, nosque Apostolos Filij sui cognitione irradiauit: non vt lucem istam salutiferam nobis solis seruemus, sed vt eadem cognitione alij quoque illuminentur in facie IESV CHRISTI, in quo scilicet, teu viua imagine (vt modo diximus) seipsum toti mundo reuelat. Facit ergo ad huius loci expositionem, quod de Pauli vocatione & missione ad gentes in Actis habetur: Ad hoc apparui tibi, vt designarem te ministrum ac testem cum eorum quae vidisti, tum eorum in quibus apparebo tibi, eximens te ex hoc populo & gentibus, ad quos nunc te mitto: Vt aperias oculos eorum, vt se conuertant a tenebris ad lucem, & a potestate Satanae ad Deum, &c. Voluit autem in praesenti facie Christi meminisse, vt in capta allusione persistens docet, nos in Christo plus habere, quam Iudaei olim in Mosis facie splendente habuerint.
units.tr: But Paul gives the reason why he preaches only JESUS CHRIST and not himself, and why he likewise professes himself to be their servant: because it is God who said, "Let light shine out of darkness," and he has shone in our hearts, to give the light of the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of JESUS CHRIST. The sense of these words is: because we are carrying on not our own business but God's. For as in the beginning of the creation of the world, when darkness covered that whole mass, produced out of nothing by the power of the Word, God by the same Word brought light out of the darkness, so now too, when ignorance had covered the whole orb of the earth with darkness, he himself has shone in our hearts and enlightened us Apostles with the knowledge of his Son. He did this not so that we should keep that saving light to ourselves alone, but so that by the same knowledge others too might be enlightened in the face of JESUS CHRIST, in whom, as a living image (as we have just said), he reveals himself to the whole world. Therefore what is recorded in Acts about Paul's calling and sending to the Gentiles helps the explanation of this passage: "For this purpose I have appeared to you, to appoint you a minister and witness both of those things which you have seen and of those things in which I will appear to you, delivering you from this people and from the Gentiles, to whom I now send you, to open their eyes, that they may turn from darkness to light and from the power of Satan to God," and so on. He chose to call to mind the present face of Christ, as he persistently teaches in the figure of light, that we have in Christ more than the Jews of old had in the shining face of Moses.

units.la: Testatur autem locus iste, totum Euangelij negotium, cuius administri fuerunt Apostoli, non humanum, sed diuinum esse, & ex aeterno Dei consilio siue decreto pendere. In nobis enim nihil quam tenebras est inuenire: & nisi ille Prophetarum & Apostolorum corda illuminauisset, non habuissent isti quod nobis traderent. Vicißim nisi idem nostris cordibus irradiaret & ea efficaciter traheret, nunquam crederemus. Ergo quicquid habemus diuinae cognitionis & fidei, id omne gratuitum misericordiae Dei donum est: quod vnum ad destruendam omnium nostrorum meritorum fiduciam abunde sufficit. Interim seruit hoc ministrorum quoque institutioni, vt meminerint, se quicquid habent cognitionis & donorum spiritualium, habere propter alios, quibus illuminandis studere debeant. Quod personatos illos doĉtores arguit, qui illuminati & Seraphici dici volunt, & Ecclesiae candelabra, cum nemini praeluceant, imo laterna fuliginosa obscuriores sint, adeoque (vt Christus de Scribis Iudaeorum pronunciat) caeci sint caecorum duces. Soletur praeterea nos locus hic aduersus audaces hostium Euangelij conatus. Quia enim Deus ministros Verbi sui excitat, & quotidie horum opera aliquos illuminari vult, nemo certe obstare poterit, quo minus fiat, quod ille decreuit.
units.tr: This passage also bears witness that the whole business of the Gospel, whose ministers the Apostles were, is not human but divine, and depends on the eternal counsel or decree of God. For in us there is nothing to be found but darkness; and unless he had enlightened the hearts of the Prophets and Apostles, they would not have had what they could hand on to us. Conversely, unless he shone the same light into our hearts and effectively drew us to it, we would never believe. Therefore whatever knowledge and faith of God we have, all of it is the free gift of God's mercy, which alone is enough to destroy all confidence in our own merits. Meanwhile this also serves the instruction of ministers, that they may remember that whatever knowledge and spiritual gifts they have, they have for the sake of others, whom they ought to labour to enlighten. This condemns those masked teachers who want to be called illuminati and Seraphic, and candlesticks of the Church, yet give light to no one; rather they are darker than a sooty lantern, and so (as Christ declares of the scribes of the Jews) are blind leaders of the blind. Moreover, this passage comforts us against the bold attempts of the enemies of the Gospel. For since God raises up ministers of his Word, and wills that some be enlightened daily through their labour, surely no one will be able to hinder what he has decreed.

units.la: Sed finis quoque Euangelij exprimitur a Paulo, qui est, vt praebeat illuminationem cognitionis gloriae Dei. Ita vero loquitur, quia gloria Dei nuspiam clarius & euidentius conspicitur, quam in Christo, qui per Euangelium praedicatur. In eo enim, veu in speculo limpidissimo, cernere possumus, quaecunque de Dei iustitia, bonitate, veritate, sapientia, omnipotentia in Scripturis traduntur. Nimium ergo & plus quam aliter delirant, qui Dei cognitionem ex mutis simulachris petunt, quos laicorum libros esse nugantur. In facie Christi imago Dei inuenitur, non pitta aut sculpta, sed viua & efficax in omnibus iis, qui Euangelium cum fide audiunt. In hunc ergo vnum intenti simus, & in eo nobis oblatam salutem toto corde ampleĉtamur, curemus autem, vt ipsi quoque vita & moribus Dei imaginem referamus, quam aeternus eius Filius, IESVS CHRISTVS, in nobis instaurauit. Ipsi debetur benediĉtio, honor, gloria & potestas in aeternum. Amen.
units.tr: But the end of the Gospel is also set forth by Paul, namely, that it may give "the illumination of the knowledge of the glory of God." He speaks thus because the glory of God is nowhere seen more clearly and evidently than in Christ, who is preached through the Gospel. For in him, as in the clearest mirror, we can discern whatever the Scriptures teach about God's justice, goodness, truth, wisdom and omnipotence. Therefore those rave too much and more than otherwise who seek the knowledge of God from dumb images, which they trifle are the books of the laity. The image of God is found in the face of Christ, not painted or carved, but living and effective in all those who hear the Gospel with faith. Let us therefore be intent on this one thing alone, and embrace with our whole heart the salvation offered us in him; and let us take care that we ourselves also, in life and manners, reflect the image of God, which his eternal Son, JESUS CHRIST, has restored in us. To him be blessing, honour, glory and power for ever. Amen.

units.la: HOMILIA XVII.
units.tr: Homily XVII.

units.la: Habemus autem thesaurum hunc in testaceis vasculis, vt praestantia virtutis sit Dei, & non ex nobis: Dum in omnibus premimur, at non coarĉtamur: haesitamus, at non prorsus haeremus: persecutionem patimur, sed in ea non deserimur: deiĉimur, at non perimus: Quolibet mortificationem Domini IESV in corpore circumferentes, vt etiam vita illa IESV in corpore nostro manifesta fiat. Semper enim nos qui viuimus, morti tradimur propter IESVM, vt etiam vita IESV manifesta fiat in mortali carne nostra. Itaque mors quidem in nobis agit, vita vero in vobis.
units.tr: We hold this treasure in earthen vessels, so that the excellence of the power may be God's and not ours. We are pressed on every side, yet not crushed; we are perplexed, yet not in despair; we are persecuted, yet not forsaken; we are cast down, yet not destroyed. Always we carry about in the body the dying of the Lord Jesus, so that the life of Jesus may also be made manifest in our body. For we who live are always being delivered to death for Jesus' sake, so that the life of Jesus may also be made manifest in our mortal flesh. So death works in us, but life in you.

units.la: VT mundus hic in omnibus aliis rebus externo splendore ducitur: ita in religione quoq; & doctrina illum spectare solet. Quae causa est, quod Euangelium, etsi non omnibus exosum aut invisum fit, à plerisq; tamen contemnatur, eò quòd eius praecones nulla huius seculi dignitate illustres, sed plerunq; homines obscuri & contemptibiles, adhaec omnis generis calamitatibus obnoxij sunt. Vix enim credibile videtur humanae rationi, illos Dei seruos esse, quos hic tot periculis exagitari finit. Prodest ergo nos in hac causa diligenter instituì, ne propter externam speciem, Veritatis & salutis aeternae doctrinam magno nostro malo reijciamus. Etenim semper ratum erit, quod aeternus Dei Filius pronuntiauit: Quisquis crediderit Euangelio, seruabitur: qui vero non crediderit, condemnabitur. Facit autem huc imprimis praesens iste locus, quem ijs, quae proximè praecesserunt, Paulus commodè subtexit. Multa enim praeclarè de Euangelio & ministerij eius excellentia dixerat, & suam in illo obeundo fidem constanter à calumniis vindicauerat. Id vero multis ridiculum videbatur, quòd Apostoli homines essent vulgo contempti & omnium iniurijs expositi: & prae aliis quidem Paulus, de quo Dominus initio pronuntiarat: Ego ei ostendam, quam multa eum pati oporteat pro meo nomine. Et credibile est vili & misera eius specie vehementer offensos fuisse Corinthios, qui vt diuites & mercaturae dediti solent, nihil magnificum ducebant, quam quod splendore aliquo externo commendaretur. Ideo vt scandalum istud remoueat, diligenter nunc rationem reddit omnium eorum, quae Apostolis aduersa & tristia accidebant.
units.tr: Just as the world in all other matters is led by outward show, so it is accustomed to look for the same in religion and teaching. This is why the Gospel, though it is not wholly hated or detested by everyone, is nonetheless despised by many, because its heralds are not distinguished by any dignity of this age but are for the most part obscure and contemptible men, and are moreover exposed to every kind of calamity. For it seems hardly credible to human reason that those are servants of God whom God here allows to be harassed by so many dangers. It is therefore useful for us to be carefully instructed in this matter, lest on account of outward appearance we cast away to our great harm the teaching of the truth and of eternal salvation. For what the eternal Son of God has declared will always stand: whoever believes the Gospel will be saved, but whoever does not believe will be condemned. The present passage is especially relevant here, and Paul has aptly appended it to what came just before. For he had said many splendid things about the Gospel and the excellence of its ministry, and had steadfastly defended his own faithfulness in carrying it out against slanders. Yet this seemed ridiculous to many: that the apostles were men generally despised and exposed to the injuries of all, and Paul above the rest, of whom the Lord said at the beginning: "I will show him how many things he must suffer for my name." It is also credible that the Corinthians, who were offended greatly by his humble and wretched appearance, judged nothing worthy of esteem unless it was commended by some outward splendour, as rich men devoted to trade are wont to do. So, to remove this stumbling block, he now carefully gives an account of all the adversities and sorrows that befell the apostles.

units.la: Et primò quidem ingenuè fatetur, quod aduersarij obijciebant, vt Euangelium vulgo contemptum facerent. Habemus thesaurum hunc (inquit) in testaceis vasculis, &c. Thesauri nomine Euangelium intelligit, quod nuper ministerium iustitiae, gratiae & vitae dixit: & alludit ad thesauri parabolam, qua Christus illud ipsum nobis commendans vsus fuerat. Et sanè thesaurus est, quo nullus sub caelo pretiosior inuenitur. Nam si huius seculi opes spectemus, haec non nisi perituris rebus constat: Euangelium vero bona caelestia & aeterna continet. Opes praesenti solummodo vitae seruiunt, & ne hanc quidem seruare possunt, quando finis eius appropinquat: imò multis exitio sunt, qui voluptatibus immodicis sese perdunt, vel ab aliis occiduntur, qui pecuniis illorum insidias struunt. Ad aeternam vero vitam adeò nihil conferunt, vt eam impediant potius: quia illis plerunque coniuncta est radix omnium malorum auaritia, ambitio, superbia, petulantia morum & quidvis audendi licentia: vel si ista definit, edaces curae: quae omnia vt Verbi Dei semen in cordibus conceptum suffocant: ita viam ad caelos nobis difficillimam faciunt, sicuti diuitiis illius primatus exemplo docemur. Euangelium vero vtriq; vitae seruit. In praesenti enim inter varia tentationum certamina Christum nobis offert, qui lux & via est, panis est, fons aquae viuentis est, pastor item non minus fortis ac potens quàm robustus. Idem nos Patri reconciliat: quo fit, vt in eo acquiescamus, & forte nostra contenti simus: quem quaestum verrimum esse, Paulus alibi testatur, & quem non alia ratione possumus assequi. Tandem vero, vbi huius vitae cursum emensi sumus, alacri fide instructos ad ipsum Christum in caelos deducit Euangelij doctrina, vbi vitam viuemus aeternam & nullius indigam. Adde hoc, quòd opes eripi possunt, Euangelium ita nos Christo vnit, vt nec ipsi ab eo diuelli possimus, nec ipse nos sibi ex manibus suis rapi patiatur. Quis nos separabit (inquit Paulus) à dilectione Dei, &c? Et Christus: Oues meas nemo potest rapere ex manu mea. Est ergo Euangelium reuera thesaurus nobilissimus, cum quo si totius Orientis gazas, imò quaecunque orbis totus habet, contulerIs, haec prae illo quisquilias, pulueres, imò stercora esse videbis. Ad hunc ergo omnes aspirent, reliquis omnibus alijs, quae infelix hic mundus admiratur.
units.tr: And first of all he frankly admits what the opponents were objecting, in order to make the Gospel contemptible to the crowd. "We have this treasure," he says, "in earthen vessels," and so on. By "treasure" he means the Gospel, which he had just called the ministry of righteousness, grace and life; and he alludes to the parable of the treasure, by which Christ himself had used to commend it to us. And indeed it is a treasure than which none under heaven is more precious. For if we look at the riches of this age, these consist only of perishable things, whereas the Gospel contains heavenly and eternal goods. Riches serve only the present life, and cannot even preserve this when its end draws near; indeed they are a ruin to many who waste themselves in immoderate pleasures, or are killed by others who lay plots against their money. As for eternal life, riches contribute nothing to it, and rather hinder it, since avarice, ambition, pride, wantonness of manners and a license to dare anything are usually joined to them as the root of all evils; or if these cease, there are gnawing cares. All these things, like thorns, choke the seed of the Word of God conceived in the heart, and so make the way to heaven most difficult for us, as we are taught by the example of the rich young ruler. But the Gospel serves both lives. In the present life, amid the various struggles of temptations, it offers us Christ, who is the light and the way, the bread, the fountain of living water, and likewise a minister no less strong and powerful than he is robust. The same Christ reconciles us to the Father, so that we rest in him and are content with our lot, which Paul elsewhere declares to be the greatest gain, and which we cannot attain by any other means. Finally, when we have run the course of this life, the teaching of the Gospel leads us, equipped with a ready faith, up to Christ himself in heaven, where we shall live an eternal life that lacks nothing. Add to this that riches can be snatched away, whereas the Gospel so unites us to Christ that we cannot be torn from him, nor will he allow us to be snatched from his hands. "Who shall separate us," says Paul, "from the love of God?" and Christ: "No one can snatch my sheep out of my hand." The Gospel is therefore truly a most noble treasure; set beside it the riches of all the East, or whatever the whole world possesses, and you will see these as mere trifles, dust, and even dung. Let all, then, aspire to this treasure, and let them value all the other things which this unhappy world admires as nothing.

units.la: Quoad vero praesentem locum, Apostolos thesaurum istum in vasculis testaceis aut fictilibus gestare ait. Ita vocans corpus hoc, quod è terra sumptum, non corruptibile modò & mortale est, verumetiam dum viuit, variis casibus atque periculis obnoxium est: adeò, vt si humanae rationis calculo res aestimetur, millies in die frangi & perire queat. Finis autem Comparationis istius est, Euangelium propter ipsos, qui contempti, miseri & mortales sint, non contemni, sed ipsum in se aestimari debere. Etenim iure stultus diceretur, qui auri thesaurum vel gemmas nobilissimas ideo asspernaretur, quòd in theca coriacea aut lignea eas asseruari cerneret: quanto autem stultior fuerit, qui aeterna ac caelestis vitae thesauros fastidit propter Euangelij praeconem obscurum atque contemcontemptibilem? Qui id faciunt, ij certè non meminerunt, qualis in terris hisce Christus fuerit, de quo Propheta in Spiritu dixit: Non est illi forma neque decor: videbimus eum, sed non est ei aspectus, ut cupiamus eum: despectus est, & reiectus inter viros, &c. At simul rationem reddit Paulus, cur ita Deus rem instituerit: Nimirum, ut praestantia virtutis sit Dei, & non ex nobis, id est, ut omnibus constet, omnem illam virtutem atque efficacitatem, quae per Euangelium non sine totius orbis admiratione sese exerit, non ex nobis, sed ex Deo esse, adeoque totum hoc negotium Euangelicum non humana, sed divina virtute gubernari conseruarique. Vide similem locum 1. Corinth. 1.
units.tr: As for the present passage, he says that the apostles carry this treasure in earthen or clay vessels. He calls by this name the body, which, taken from the earth, is not only corruptible and mortal, but also while it lives is subject to various chances and dangers, so that, if the matter is reckoned by the reckoning of human reason, it may be broken and perish a thousand times a day. The purpose of this comparison is that the Gospel should not be despised on account of those who preach it, who are contemptible, wretched and mortal, but should be esteemed for its own sake. For he would rightly be called foolish who scorned a treasure of gold or most noble gems because he saw them kept in a leather or wooden case. How much more foolish, then, is he who despises the treasures of eternal and heavenly life on account of the obscure and contemptible herald of the Gospel? Those who do this certainly do not remember what kind of man Christ was on this earth, of whom the Prophet said by the Spirit: "He has no form nor comeliness; we shall see him, but there is no appearance in him that we should desire him; he is despised and rejected among men," and so on. But at the same time Paul gives the reason why God has so arranged the matter: namely, "that the excellence of the power may be God's and not ours." That is, it is to be plain to all that all that power and efficacy which shows itself through the Gospel, to the wonder of the whole world, is not from us but from God; and so this whole Gospel business is governed and preserved not by human but by divine power. See a similar passage in 1 Corinthians 1.

units.la: Est autem hic perpetuus Dei mos, ut res maximas per media contemptibilia perficiat. Quod enim hic de Apostolis dicitur, hoc in toto humanae redemptionis negotio observatu esse scimus. Cum enim foedus fuit, ex quo illud depender, instaurare vellet Deus, ad rem tanti momenti Abrahamum delegit, eumq; prius peregrinum & extorrem fieri voluit, ne quid hic humanae authoritati posset tribui. Ita cum populum suum ex Aegypto educere statuisset, ad id Mosis opera usus est, quem infantem expositicium primo, deinde exulem quoque fuisse scimus. Quid de Maria Virgine & tota domo Davidis dicemus, cum illa quidem pauperucula, haec autem contemptissima fuerit, cum Christus nasceabatur: adeo, ut ex nobilissima illa tot Regum stirpe, vix truncus quidam reliquus esse videretur? quod ita fore, olim Isaias praedixerat. Sed & ipse Christus in hoc mundo pauper & contemptibilis vixit, ut multi eius vili specie offensi fuerint. Et ut Apostolos habuit pauperes, contemptibiles & nullius in mundo existimationis: ita Euangelij quoque praeditatio simplex atque humilis, adhaec cum cruce & multis aduersis coniuncta est. Perrupit tamen per omnia obstacula, & obscuri illi servi IESV CHRISTI per mille mortes de toto terrarum orbe triumpharunt. Agnoscamus ergo totum hoc negotium Dei esse, & ideo huic soli omnem gloriam transcribamus, neq; dubitemus de eius voluntate & potentia, qua in posterum quoq; Euangelij doctrinam in terris conseruabit. Facit ergo hoc multum ad confutandum eos, qui Divos suae salutis authores faciunt. Peccant enim directe in Dei consilium, qui vilibus & obscuris ministris uti voluit, ut ipsi soli omnis ista gloria cederet.
units.tr: Now it is God's constant custom to accomplish the greatest things through means that are contemptible. For what is said here of the apostles we know to have been observed in the whole business of human redemption. When God wished to renew the covenant on which that depends, he chose Abraham for a matter of such great importance, and first willed him to become a stranger and an exile, so that nothing might be attributed here to human authority. So too, when he had decided to lead his people out of Egypt, he used the work of Moses, whom we know to have been first an exposed infant and afterwards also an exile. What shall we say of the Virgin Mary and the whole house of David, when she was indeed a very poor little woman and that house the most despised at the time Christ was born, so that out of that most noble line of so many kings there seemed scarcely any stump left? Isaiah had long ago foretold that this would be so. But Christ himself lived in this world poor and contemptible, so that many were offended by his humble appearance. And just as he had apostles who were poor, contemptible, and of no esteem in the world, so too the preaching of the Gospel is simple and humble, and moreover is joined with the cross and many adversities. Yet it has broken through all obstacles, and those obscure servants of Jesus Christ have triumphed over the whole world through a thousand deaths. Let us therefore acknowledge that this whole business is God's, and so let us ascribe all glory to him alone, and let us not doubt his will and power, by which he will also in time to come preserve the teaching of the Gospel on earth. This therefore greatly serves to refute those who make the saints the authors of their salvation. For they sin directly against God's counsel, since he chose to use vile and obscure ministers so that all this glory might belong to himself alone.

units.la: Debet etiam hinc generalis doctrina peti, quam omnes sibi applicent. Nam thesaurum hunc pretiosissimum Deus omnibus per Euangelium offert, & idem a nobis sola fide percipitur. At qui nos sumus? Vasa nimirum testacea, de quo vel primi parentis creatio nos admonere potest, quem ex luto factum fuisse Moses scribit. Fragiles ergo sumus, quanti quanti sumus. Anima enim affectibus variis obnoxia tumultuatur & turbatur: Corpus infirmum, caducum, morborum mille officina, & mortale est. Via totius vitae lubrica & plena periculi, cum natura ad malum proclives simus, & insuper mundi illecebris & diaboli suggestionibus nunquam non tentemur.
