For, as can be gathered from the context, they were also trying to snatch from him the praise of the Corinthian church, which had been converted. So he says: "But we will not boast of things beyond our measure, but according to the measure of the rule which God has allotted to us, so as to reach even as far as you," etc. By these words he seems to say: If I had not come as far as you, I could be said to boast beyond the measure assigned me by God, and so be counted among those who more insolently boast of what they never did. But I do not extend myself beyond due bounds, as if I had not come to you; that is, I do not extend the account of my labours to things not accomplished by me, when I glory in you who have been converted. For it cannot be denied that I have come to you in the Gospel of Christ, that is, by my ministry, through which I preach the Gospel of Christ. For who preached to you before me? Did I not beget you in Christ Jesus, so that you, who once were alienated from God and wallowed in most empty superstitions and every kind of wickedness, might now be the Church of Christ and sons of God? Rightly, therefore, do I glory in you, nor do I deserve to be numbered among those who attribute more to themselves than is fitting, since I keep myself within the measure of the rule, that is, within the just and regular extent of that measure which God has allotted to me. By the word "measure" he understands that part of the world which God had assigned to him, so that through his ministry the teaching of the Gospel might be made known. He says these things about himself in such a way as again to censure the boasting of his rivals, who gloried in long journeys and, as ambitious generals are wont to do, enumerated in grand words the nations they had conquered, though they themselves (as we have said elsewhere) had founded no churches, but disturbed those founded by others.

units.la: Est autem hic obseruatu dignum, quod certæ mensuræ meminit, qua Deus sui apostolatus fines aut limites ipsi assignauerit. Ita enim solet ille, qui certa quoque discrimina donorum & ministeriorum constituit inter seruos suos, & vniuscuiusque opera pro facultatum, quas singulis dedit, ratione vtitur. Neque tamen in his affectui indulget, sed dimensione regulari, id est, legitima & iusta vtitur. Debent ergo intra huius fines singuli sese continere, & quam ipsis Deus partitus est prouinciam ornare. Qui hoc faciunt, si reuera Regulares sive Canonici sunt. Gloriantur hoc titulo hodie multi ex Monachis & Ecclesiarum, quas Cathedrales vocant, præsulibus. At si eorum mores & facta inspicias, prorsus Irregulares esse videbis. Nam canum instar in præsepi non modo nihil faciunt eorum, quæ ad Ecclesiæ ministerium pertinent, sed ne alios quidem hoc obire patiuntur. Adhæc omnes pietatis & honestatis leges, imo sensus quoque communis regulam transgressi, vitam omnem in luxu & libidine transfigunt: taceo nunc tyrannidem, qua in Christi fideles crudeliter grassantur.
units.tr: It is worth noting here that he mentions a certain measure by which God has assigned to him the bounds or limits of his apostleship. For the one who also sets fixed distinctions of gifts and ministries among his servants is accustomed to deal with each person's work according to the abilities he has given to each. Yet he does not indulge feeling in these matters, but uses a regular measure, that is, a lawful and just one. Each person therefore ought to keep within these bounds and adorn the province God has allotted to him. Those who do this are truly regular, or canons. Many today, from among the monks and from the prelates of the churches which they call cathedral, boast of this title. But if you look at their morals and deeds, you will see that they are altogether irregular. For, like dogs in a manger, they not only do none of the things pertaining to the ministry of the Church, but do not even allow others to perform them. Moreover, having transgressed all the laws of piety and decency, indeed the rule of common sense too, they spend their whole lives in luxury and lust. I say nothing now of the tyranny with which they cruelly rage against the faithful of Christ.

units.la: Deinde obseruabis, quod Paulus se cum Euangelio Christi Corinthum venisse scribit. Non ergo otiosis aut curiosis atque inutilibus peregrinationibus vacauerunt Apostoli, sed cum Euangelij prædicatione orbem terrarum circumierunt, qua aut conuertebant eos, qui à Dei veri cognitione & fide adhuc alieni erant, aut iam ante conuersis donum aliquod spirituale impertiebantur (vt ad Romanos scribitur) quo eos in fide confirmarent. Horum igitur exemplo confutantur primum homines superstitiosi, qui religionis ergo peregrinationes suscipiunt, & gratiam Dei vnà cum merito Christi certis locis alligant. Est hæc vetus superstitio, quæ D. Hieronymi sæculo eo vsque excreuerat, vt eam grauiter reprehenderit, & Nepotianum immodico terræ Sanctæ desiderio flagrantem abstulerit. Pugnat enim cum Christi verbis, qui locorum discrimina sustulit, & veros adoratores preces suas non certis locis astringere, sed Deum vbique in spiritu & veritate adorare dicit. Deinde arguit exemplum Pauli eos, qui immodica & ambitiosa curiositate extimulati hinc inde vagantur, neque suarum Ecclesiarum finibus contenti, peregrinis Ecclesijs atque Scholis negotium faciunt, & cum passim turbas dent, tamen quasi re bene gesta peregrinationum suarum historiam non sine aliorum ignominia & contemptu diuulgant. Sunt hi nocentissimi homines, & grauissimorum dissidiorum authores, ideoq; omnibus sæculis male audierunt. Et extat vetus Canon,
units.tr: Next you will observe that Paul writes that he came to Corinth with the Gospel of Christ. The apostles, therefore, were not occupied with idle, curious and useless journeys, but went round the world preaching the Gospel, by which they either converted those still alien from the knowledge and faith of the true God, or imparted some spiritual gift to those already converted (as is written to the Romans), by which they might confirm them in the faith. By the example of these men, first those superstitious people are refuted who undertake pilgrimages for the sake of religion, and tie God's grace, together with the merit of Christ, to certain places. This is an old superstition, which in the age of St Jerome had grown so far that he sharply rebuked it and dissuaded Nepotianus, who was burning with an immoderate desire for the Holy Land. For it conflicts with the words of Christ, who abolished the distinction of places and says that true worshippers do not bind their prayers to certain places, but worship God everywhere in spirit and truth. Then Paul's example condemns those who, stirred by immoderate and ambitious curiosity, wander hither and thither, and, not content with the bounds of their own churches, make trouble for foreign churches and schools. Though they cause disturbance everywhere, they nonetheless publish the account of their journeys, as if they had done well, not without the disgrace and contempt of others. These are most harmful men, and authors of very grave dissensions, and therefore in all ages they have had a bad name. And there is an old canon,

units.la: Deus singulis suam mensuram assignat.
units.tr: God assigns to each his own measure.

units.la: Peregrinationes Apostolorum quales fuerint.
units.tr: Peregrinationes Apostolorum quales fuerint. What the journeys of the apostles were like.

units.la: Ioan. 4. Canon, quo olim sancitum fuit, ne quis Episcopus ab Ecclesia sua in aliam transferretur, neue quis in aliena Ecclesia sibi aliquod ius sumeret. Et scimus eo nomine Epiphanium à Chrysostomo graviter reprehensum fuisse.
units.tr: John 4. A canon by which it was once decreed that no bishop should be transferred from his own Church to another, nor that anyone should assume for himself any right in another's Church. And we know that on this account Epiphanius was severely rebuked by Chrysostom.

units.la: Caeterum quia sciebat Paulus nullam defensionem inuidus & malitiosus sufficere, amplius illustrat quod dixit. Non de iis quae non sunt nostrae mensurae gloriantes in alienis laboribus. Pertinet ad huius explicationem quod ad Romanos scribit, sibi hoc propositum esse vt Euangelium in iis locis praedicet, vbi Christi nomen nondum auditum sit, ne super alienum fundamentum aedificet. Fuit hoc studium omnibus Apostolis commune. Rursus autem pseudoapostolos perstringit, qui in alienos labores falcem mittebant, & ab aliis constitutas Ecclesias (vt ante quoque diximus) turbabant. Vbi discimus, neminem debere aliorum laudem sibi vendicare. Si enim nemini licet de iis, quae ipse fecit, ambitiose gloriari, multo minus ex aliorum laboribus gloria quaeri debet. Faciunt hoc ignaui milites, qui cum nunquam non arma, pugnas & victorias in ore habeant, fere seipsos risui exponunt, si quid cum periculo aggredi oportet. In Repub. autem & Ecclesia ambitio ista simulcates noxias parit, neque ex ea alium fructum metunt superbi illi alienae virtutis ostentatores, quàm quod cornicula Æsopica instar omnibus ludibrium fiunt, vt qui alienis plumis se vendicarint.
units.tr: Moreover, because Paul knew that the envious and malicious accept no defence, he illustrates more fully what he has said: not boasting of things that are not our measure, in the labours of others. To the explanation of this belongs what he writes to the Romans, that it was his purpose to preach the Gospel in those places where the name of Christ had not yet been heard, lest he build on another's foundation. This zeal was common to all the apostles. Again he censures the false apostles, who put their sickle into others' labours and disturbed churches founded by others (as we said before). Here we learn that no one ought to claim for himself the praise of others. For if no one is permitted to boast ambitiously of what he himself has done, much less ought glory to be sought from the labours of others. Lazy soldiers do this: though they always have arms, battles and victories on their lips, they nearly expose themselves to laughter whenever something must be attempted with danger. In the commonwealth and in the Church, however, this ambition breeds harmful quarrels, nor do those proud displayers of another's virtue reap any other fruit from it than that, like Aesop's jackdaw, they become a laughing-stock to all, since they have claimed for themselves the credit of others' feathers.

units.la: At quia nuper dixerat, Deum sibi sui ministerij mensuram ad Corinthios vsq; extendisse, obijceret aliquis: Ergo nunc cursum tuum absoluisti Paule, & num tibi ipsi ferias indices? huic etiam obiectioni occurrens, se adhuc ad omne obsequium Christi paratum esse dicit, vt qui speret, Deum sibi funiculum suum longius extensurum esse. Speramus (inquit) quod augescente fide vestra, nos in vobis abunde magnificandos fore secundum nostram mensuram: vt in locis quae vltra vos sunt euangelizem, &c. Idem dicit quod ad Romanos, quem locum supra adduximus. Quia autem hoc totum in Dei manu erat, cuius arcanum consilium ipse ignorabat, non confidenter de suo instituto pronuntiat, sed Sperandi verbo vtitur, vt se totum à Dei prouidentia pendere ostendat. Interim hoc tunc futurum ait, quando Corinthiorum fides aucta magis q confirmata fuerit. Non quod aliarum gentium fides atq; salus ab illorum profectu penderet, sed quod ipse vlterius progredi non posset, quoad ipsos videbat adhuc sua cura & ministerio opus habere. Ita vero ipsos graviter accusat, qui suis dissidijs & vitijs varijs regni Dei propagationem hucusq; impedierint.
units.tr: But since he had said recently that God had extended to him the measure of his ministry as far as Corinth, someone might object: "So now you have finished your course, Paul, and are you declaring yourself a holiday?" Meeting this objection too, he says that he is still ready for every service of Christ, as one who hopes that God will stretch his line further still. "We hope," he says, "that as your faith grows, we shall be greatly enlarged among you according to our measure, so that we may preach the gospel in regions beyond you," etc. He says the same thing as in the letter to the Romans, which passage we cited above. But since all this lay in the hand of God, whose secret counsel he himself did not know, he does not pronounce confidently about his own plan but uses the word "hope," so as to show that he wholly depends on the providence of God. Meanwhile he says that this will happen when the faith of the Corinthians has been increased and strengthened more. Not that the faith and salvation of the other nations depended on the progress of those people, but that he himself could not go further while he saw that they still needed his care and ministry. Thus he severely accuses them, since by their dissensions and various vices they have so far hindered the spread of the kingdom of God.

units.la: Potest hoc ipsum hodie multis obijci, qui scurriliter quaerunt: Si verum & germanum est Euangelium, quod vos praedicatis, cur non omnes ei credunt? cur plures illud auersantur atq; fastidiunt? Responderi (inquam) his potest: Quia vos ex illo minus hucusq; profecisse vident, & vestris moribus offenduntur, quos sub Euangelij praetextu effrenem quaduis designandi licentiam quaerere conspicantur. Etenim si fidem vestram crescere & eius fructus meliores viderent, amplior esset Euangelij ad ipsos propagandi occasio. Hic ergo officij sui admonentur omnes, quos Deus Verbi sui doctrina illuminare dignatus est: Nimirum, vt eandem ad alios quoq; propagari curent. Postulat hoc Dei gloria, ad quam initiò creati sumus, vt iam de redemptione per Christum facta nihil dicam, qui nos sibi acquisiuit, vt eius laudes praedicemus, qui nos ex tenebris translulit in lucem suam admirabilem. De eodem etiam nos Orationis Dominicae ordo admonet, cuius prima petitio est, vt Dei nomen in nobis sanctificetur: Altera, vt regnum ipsius adueniat: Tertia, vt voluntas eius in terris fiat, perinde vt in caelo. Iubet idem Lex charitatis, quam proximo debemus, & quam nunquam praestabimus, nisi de illo ad Christum & salutis aeternae hereditatem adducendo soliciti simus. Est ergo hoc ingens & multiplex scelus, si malo nostro exemplo regni Dei cursum remoremur, & multis alijs simus perditionis authores.
units.tr: This same charge can be brought against many today, who ask scornfully: "If the Gospel that you preach is true and genuine, why do not all believe it? Why do many turn away from it and loathe it?" It can be answered to them (I say): because they see that you have made less progress from it until now, and they are offended by your manners, which they observe seeking, under the pretext of the gospel, an unbridled license to plunder whatever they like. For if they saw your faith growing and its fruits better, there would be a greater opportunity for spreading the gospel to them. Here, therefore, all whom God has deigned to illuminate with the teaching of his Word are reminded of their duty: namely, that they take care to spread the same to others also. The glory of God demands this, for which we were created at the beginning. I say nothing yet of the redemption made through Christ, who acquired us for himself, that we might proclaim the praises of him who brought us out of darkness into his marvellous light. The order of the Lord's Prayer also reminds us of the same thing: its first petition is that God's name be hallowed in us; the second, that his kingdom come; the third, that his will be done on earth as in heaven. The law of charity, which we owe to our neighbour, and which we will never fulfil unless we are anxious to bring him to Christ and to the inheritance of eternal salvation, likewise commands it. It is therefore a great and manifold wickedness, if by our bad example we hinder the course of the kingdom of God, and become the authors of perdition for many others.

units.la: Sed concludit locum hunc Apostolus, dicens: Caeterum qui gloriatur, in Domino glorietur. Quasi diceret: Quid multis opus est? si cui libet gloriari, curet in Domino glorietur. Est autem in Domino gloriari, hunc omnium quae habes authorem agnoscere, & ad eius gratiam omnia referre: Item, illius iudicio acquiescere, & pro nihilo ducere aliorum de nobis iudicia, modò de illius erga nos voluntate & studio certi simus. Et postremum hoc huius loci argumento proprie conuenit. Nam huius admonitiunculae hanc rationem adducit Paulus: Non enim qui seipsum commendat, is probatus est, sed is quem Dominus commendat. Seipsum commendat, qui sibi omnia tribuit, At idem illa ipsa detrahit Deo, quod sacrilegium est nulla venia dignum. Quid enim habes, quod non accepisti? Deinde qui seipsos commendant, non possunt non suo iudicio falli, propter philautiam, qua excaecati non vident quam multum adhuc ipsis deest. Quod si vero hominibus probari cupias, non minus falleris: quia illi quoque errare possunt, vel ignorantia, vel prauo aliquo affectu decepti. Solus Deus non fallitur, vt qui corda & renes hominum inspicit: neque aliquem fallit ipse, cum ipsissima sit Veritas.
units.tr: But the Apostle concludes this passage, saying: "But let him who glories glory in the Lord." As if he were to say: "Why need there be many words? If anyone wishes to glory, let him take care to glory in the Lord." To glory in the Lord, however, is to acknowledge him as the author of all that you have, and to refer everything to his grace; likewise, to acquiesce in his judgment and to count the judgments of others about us as nothing, provided we are sure of his will and goodwill towards us. And this last point properly suits the argument of this passage. For Paul adduces this reason for this little admonition: "For it is not he who commends himself who is approved, but he whom the Lord commends." He commends himself who ascribes everything to himself; but such a person in doing so takes away from God the very things that are due to him, which is sacrilege deserving no pardon. "For what do you have that you did not receive?" Then those who commend themselves cannot but be deceived in their own judgment, on account of self-love, by which blinded they do not see how much they still lack. But if indeed you desire to be approved by men, you are no less mistaken, since they too can err, deceived either by ignorance or by some perverse affection. God alone is not deceived, since he searches hearts and reins; nor does he deceive anyone, since he is truth itself.

units.la: Docet igitur hic locus, quae vera & certa sit gloriam consequendi ratio? Ea nimirum, vt nos Dei iudicio approbemus. At it eos probat & honore dignos iudicat, qui ipsius gloriam promouere student. Honorantes me (per Prophetam ait) honorabo. Et sola stabilis atque solida est gloria, qua nos ille dignatur. Mundi & carnis gloria omnis inanis & euanida est. Haec ergo ad se transferant omnis loci & ordinis homines, neque multum morentur huius mundi iudicia, qui totus in malo iacet, & non nisi sui similibus delectatur. Peribit ille tandem & sempiterna ignominia multabitur. At qui Deo probati fuerint, hi aeternum viuent, & coronam iustitiae olim donabuntur in magno illo die, quo ad iudicium veniet Dominus noster, IESVS CHRISTVS, vt digna suis seruis praemia retribuat. Ipsi debetur benedictio, honor, gloria & potestas in aeternum, Amen.
units.tr: This passage teaches, therefore, what is the true and sure way of obtaining glory? Namely, that we be approved by the judgment of God. Now he approves and judges worthy of honour those who strive to promote his glory. "Those who honour me," he says through the Prophet, "I will honour." The only stable and solid glory is that with which he deigns to honour us; all glory of the world and the flesh is empty and vanishing. Let men of every rank and station therefore apply this to themselves, and let them not much dwell on the judgments of this world, which lies wholly in evil and delights only in its own kind. That world will perish at last and be punished with everlasting ignominy. But those who have been approved by God will live for ever, and will be given the crown of righteousness one day, on that great day when our Lord Jesus Christ comes to judgment, to render worthy rewards to his servants. To him be blessing, honour, glory and power for ever. Amen.

units.la: CAPUT XI. HOMILIA XLVI.
units.tr: CHAPTER XI. HOMILY XLVI.

units.la: VTinam toleraretis paulisper insipientiam meam: imo etiam tolerate me. Ambio enim vos Dei zelotypia. Praeparaui enim vos vni viro virginem puram sistere, nempe Christo. Sed metuo ne quo modo, sicut serpens ille Euam seduxit calliditate sua: ita mentes vestrae corruptae degenerent a simplicitate, quae est in Christo.
units.tr: Would that you could bear with my foolishness for a little while; indeed, do bear with me. For I am jealous over you with the jealousy of God. For I have betrothed you to one husband, to present you as a pure virgin to Christ. But I fear that, as the serpent deceived Eve by his cunning, so your minds may be corrupted and fall away from the simplicity that is in Christ.

units.la: QVONIAM mundus hic veram de fide & cultu Dei doctrinam non potest rationibus idoneis euertere, ipsos doctores omni calumniarum genere petit, vt in horum personam illam suspectam & inuisam reddat. Factum hoc est omnibus seculis, sicuti veterum Prophetarum & Apostolorum exempla testantur. Et haec causa est, quod idem de sua functione toties differunt: quod inter Apostolos Paulum prae aliis fecisse videmus: quia huic magis quam aliis Satan infensus fuit, quod regnum suum ab illo inter gentes mirifico cum successu euerti videret. Licet ergo hucusque multa pro se dixisset, quia tamen Corinthiorum animos pseudoapostolorum mendacijs atque splendore fascinatos esse sentiebat, vt de ipso vix possent honorifice sentire, hoc Cap. plenius (quod dici solet) velis in eos inuebitur, & illos fi secum conferantur, omnino nullos esse demonstrat. Ne tamen aemuli eius, ex eo nouam arriperent calumniandi occasionem, initio statim diligenti & artificiosa insinuatione animos eorum sibi conciliat.
units.tr: Since this world cannot overthrow the true doctrine concerning faith and the worship of God by sound arguments, it attacks the teachers themselves with every kind of slander, so as to make their office suspected and hated. This has happened in every age, as the examples of the ancient Prophets and Apostles bear witness. This is also why they so often speak about their own office, as we see Paul did more than the other Apostles. Satan was more hostile to him than to the others, because he saw his own kingdom being overthrown among the Gentiles with remarkable success. So although Paul had said much in his own defence up to this point, he still perceived that the minds of the Corinthians had been bewitched by the lies and splendour of the false apostles, so that they could hardly think well of him. Therefore, in this chapter, he will attack them more fully (as the saying goes) with all his sails set, and he shows that, when compared with him, they are altogether nothing. Yet, lest his rivals seize on this as a new occasion for slander, he wins their minds to himself at once, at the very start, by a careful and skilful approach.

units.la: Nam a voto oritur cum euidenti & pathetica beneuolentia sua erga ipsos significatione: vt intelligant ipsum de re magni momenti acturum, ex qua omnis ipsorum salus pendeat: Vtinam toleraretis paulisper insipientiam meam, imo etiam tolerate me. Insipientiam dicit suam laudum praedicationem, quam instituebat. Vulgo enim inter viros cordatos & graues parum prudens habetur, qui seipsum commendat. Habent ergo verba haec Concessionis speciem. Quasi diceret: Scio equidem me nonnullis rursus posse insipientem videri, si iterum in mei ministerij & rerum abs me gestarum commendationem digrediar. Sed vtinam feratis paulisper hanc meam insipientiam, & vt id faciatis quaeso vos: quando vt ista dicam non tam mea quam vestra interest.
units.tr: For he begins with a wish, and with a clear and heartfelt declaration of his goodwill towards them, so that they understand he is about to speak of a matter of great importance, on which all their salvation depends: "Would that you could bear with my foolishness for a little while; indeed, do bear with me." He calls his praising of himself "foolishness," since he is about to set out his own commendation. For among sensible and serious men it is generally held to be rather foolish for a man to commend himself. So these words have the form of a concession, as if he were saying: "I know that some may again think me foolish if I digress once more into commending my ministry and the things I have done. But I beg you, bear with this foolishness of mine for a little while, and please do so, since it concerns you not less than me that I say these things."

units.la: Est autem hic obseruatu dignum, quod iustam & necessariam ministerij sui & suae fidei atq; industriae commendationem, insipientiam dicit. Eo enim primum testatur, se nihil propriae laudis vel gloriae studio dicere, ut qui facile intelligat, ad se nihil quàm insipientis titulum redire posse. Deinde simul ambitiosos illos iactatores perstringit, ut discant, quales ipsi quoque censeantur ab omnibus cordatis, dum sese ostentant, & virtutes suas tam magnificè praedicant, in quibus nihil insit solidum & laude aliqua dignum. Insipientis enim est de ijs, quae cum magna laude fecimus, vel insolentius, vel abstq; graui & necessaria causa gloriari. Quis ergo non impudentes quoque dixerit eos, qui falsa laudum suarum praedicatione sese omnibus ridiculos praebent? Quo igitur loco haberi debent, qui cùm virtutes in se nullas habeant, insuper vitia quoq; sibi ipsis affingunt, dum sua stupra, caedes, rapinas, imposituras, & alia his nequiora iactant? Est vanitas ista vulgaris admodum apud senes, de quibus verissimè illud dixeris: Nequitia est, quae vos non finit esse senes. Cùm verò huius turpitudinem gentium poetae observare potuerint, quanto magis illam abominari debent Christiani homines, quorum dicta factaq; omnia salem illum Euangelicum spirare debent?
units.tr: It is worth noting here that he calls the just and necessary commendation of his ministry, of his faith and of his diligence, "foolishness." By this he first testifies that he is not speaking out of any desire for his own praise or glory, since anyone can easily see that nothing but the title of a fool can come back to himself from such talk. Then at the same time he rebukes those ambitious boasters, so that they may learn what they themselves are thought of by all sensible people, when they display themselves and praise their own virtues so magnificently, although there is nothing solid in them and nothing worthy of any praise. For it is the mark of a fool to boast, either too arrogantly or without a serious and necessary cause, about deeds we have done with great praise. Who then would not call shameless those who make themselves ridiculous to everyone by a false boasting of their own praises? What place, then, should be given to those who, having no virtues in themselves, moreover invent vices for themselves, boasting of their adulteries, murders, robberies, frauds, and other things even worse than these? This vanity is quite common among old men, of whom you could most truly say that wickedness is what prevents you from being old. But if the poets among the Gentiles could observe the ugliness of this, how much more should Christians abominate it, whose words and deeds ought all to breathe that gospel salt?

units.la: Porrò, quod à Corinthijs petit Paulus, id omnes eos decet, qui loco inferiori sunt: ut nimirum quoad eius fieri potest, patienter ferant eos, qui ex Dei instituto aliquod in ipsos ius habent. Tales sunt parentes, quibus natura in filios imperium concessit, quod Deus suis legibus confirmavit, idque tanta cum seueritate, ut capitis supplicium illis decernat, qui parentibus maledixerint. Etsi ergo illi interdum vel per ignorantiam errent, vel propter aetatem delirent, aut etiam aequo morosiores sint, liberorum tamen fuerit, eos patienter ferre: & tunc eis in mentem veniat, quanta in ipsos indulgentia illi usi sint, quàm patienter ipsorum insipientiam tulerint, quantum fastidij, laboris & molestiae devorauerint, ut ipsos possent euchere. Idem de ijs sentiendum, qui magistratus gerunt. Non possunt hi semper videre quid facto opus sit, & saepe gravibus causis impediuntur, ut quod maximè vellent, non possint effectum dare. Tunc ergo in meliorem partem interpretentur omnia subditi, neque bene meritis de Republ. novam molestiam sua importunitate exhibeant. Eadem est ministrorum Ecclesiae conditio, qui etiam ipsi patrum loco sunt, ut alibi est dictum: At hic simul diligenter cavendum est, ne facilitas illa adhibeatur in ferendis manifestis erroribus circa fidem & religionem: quod hodie à nobis petere audent Pontifices, ut nimirum tunc quoque à nemine reprehendantur, quando officij sui immemores, insuper animas hominum caeratim secum ad inferos abripiunt. Sunt haec intolerabilia auditu Christianis hominibus. Ferenda quidem sunt multa in fidei pastoribus: at si qui doctrinam Verbi Dei corrumpunt, cultus falsos instituunt, à salutis via populum abducunt, Ecclesiam in sectas scindunt, & Republ. pernitiosè turbant, ij nullo modo ferri debent: sed in eos illud Apostoli torqueri debet: Utinam abscindantur, qui vos inquietant. Gal. 5.
units.tr: Furthermore, what Paul asks of the Corinthians is fitting for all who hold an inferior position: namely, that, as far as possible, they patiently bear with those who by God's appointment have some right over them. Such are parents, to whom nature has granted authority over their children, which God has confirmed by his laws, and with such severity that he decrees the penalty of death for those who curse their parents. So even if parents sometimes err through ignorance, or grow foolish because of their age, or are even more peevish than they should be, it is still the duty of children to bear with them patiently. And then let them call to mind how much indulgence their parents have shown towards them, how patiently they have borne their childish folly, how much weariness, labour and trouble they have endured so as to bring them up. The same should be thought of those who hold the magistracy. They cannot always see what needs to be done, and they are often hindered by serious causes, so that they cannot carry out what they most want. Therefore subjects should interpret everything in the better part, and not, by their own unreasonable demands, cause new trouble to the commonwealth, which has done them good. The condition of the ministers of the Church is the same, for they too stand in the place of fathers, as has been said elsewhere. But here we must take great care that this readiness to put up with things is not applied to the bearing of plain errors concerning faith and religion. This is what the Pontiffs today dare to ask of us: that no one should rebuke them even when, forgetting their office, they drag the souls of men headlong with them to hell. Such things are intolerable to hear for Christian people. Indeed, many things must be borne in the pastors of the faith; but if any corrupt the teaching of the Word of God, establish false worship, lead the people away from the way of salvation, split the Church into sects, and throw the commonwealth into dangerous disorder, such men must in no way be tolerated. Against them the words of the Apostle ought to be aimed: "Would that those who trouble you were cut off." Gal. 5.

units.la: Caeterum causam adducit Paulus, cur ipsum ferre debeant. Ambio enim vos Dei zelotypia, &c. Id est, Quicquid facio, non mei honoris aut quaestus causa facio, vel ut mihi imperium in-ter vos vendicem, sed divino zelo motus, quo vror, ut vobis consulam. Differunt enim inter se (ut Chrysostomus annotauit) zelus Dei & hominum. Zelus autem sive zelotypia ex amore nimio nascitur, & proprie de coniugibus dicitur. Plerunque autem qui ea vruntur, ij sua quaerunt, ut nimirum eos quos amant sibi solis vendicent, & proinde rivalem aut socium non possunt ferre. Sed aliter Deus, qui licet se quoque zelotypum esse testetur, & nos sibi soli consecratos velit, id tamen non propter seipsum facit (quid enim commodi ex nobis ad illum redire potest? ) sed propter nos: ut nimirum nos seruet, qui nisi ipsi totis animis coniuncti simus, falsi esse non possumus. Eo igitur affectu Paulus se Corinthios prosequi ait, ne ex eorum numero esse videatur, qui non nisi suis commodis studebant: ut nimirum ipsi in honore essent, opulenti fierent, & vitam viuerent securam: eorum similes, qui in gentium Ecclesijs Circumcisionem ideo vrgebant, ut in pretio haberentur, amicos sibi parárent, & persecutionem subterfugerent, quam Iudaei passim mouebant ijs, qui solam fidem in Christum praedicabant. Vide Galat. 5. & 6.
units.tr: Next, Paul gives the reason why they ought to bear with him: "For I am jealous over you with the jealousy of God," and so on. That is to say: whatever I do, I do not do for my own honour or gain, nor to claim authority over you, but moved by a divine zeal, by which I am burning, so that I may look after your good. For (as Chrysostom observed) the zeal of God and the zeal of men differ from each other. Zeal, or jealousy, arises from excessive love, and is properly said of spouses. Yet those who feel it usually seek their own interests, namely, that they may claim for themselves alone those whom they love, and therefore they cannot bear a rival or a partner. But God acts otherwise. Although he too declares himself to be jealous, and wants us to be consecrated to him alone, he does not do this for his own sake (for what advantage can come back to him from us?), but for our sake, so that he may keep us safe, since we cannot be safe unless we are joined to him with our whole hearts. With this same feeling, then, Paul says that he pursues the Corinthians, so that he may not seem to belong to the number of those who looked only to their own advantage: that is, to be honoured, to grow rich, and to live a secure life. He was unlike those who in the churches of the Gentiles insisted on circumcision so that they might be held in esteem, win friends for themselves, and escape the persecution which the Jews everywhere stirred up against those who preached faith in Christ alone. See Gal. 5 and 6.

units.la: Admonet autem Paulus suo exemplo omnes Ecclesiarum ministros, quos in ipsis affectus esse, quos item eis omnium suorum studiorum, consiliorum & actionum finis propositus esse debeat. Ament suae fidei creditas Ecclesias, & ita quidem, ut earum zelo quoque vrantur. Nisi enim id fiat, nunquam satis fidi erunt, sed laboribus, periculis & ingratitudini atque iniurijs multorum facile succumbent. Neque tamen zelus ille apud eos locum habebit, nisi IESVM CHRISTVM ex toto corde diligant, qui sponsam atque oues suas ipsis committere dignatus est. Ideo ille, cum Petrum suo loco restituere vellet, ter eum num se diligeret, interrogauit. Finis autem zeli istius sit totius Ecclesiae adificatio & singulorum salus. Talibus animis olim Prophetae & Apostoli praediti fuerunt, quos nulli vel labores vel pericula flectere potuerunt, vt sibi a Deo mandatam stationem desererent.
units.tr: Moreover, by his own example Paul admonishes all the ministers of the Churches what feelings they ought to have towards them, and likewise what goal should be set before them as the end of all their studies, counsels and actions. Let them love the Churches entrusted to their faith, and indeed in such a way that they are also set on fire with zeal for them. For unless this happens, they will never be faithful enough, but will easily give way to labours, dangers, the ingratitude and wrongs of many. Yet that zeal will have no place among them unless they love Jesus Christ with their whole heart, he who deigned to entrust his bride and his sheep to them. For this reason he, when he wished to restore Peter to his place, asked him three times whether he loved him. The aim of this zeal should be the building up of the whole Church and the salvation of each individual. Prophets and Apostles of old were endowed with such minds, whom neither labours nor dangers could bend, so that they would abandon the post entrusted to them by God.

units.la: At zelotypiae suae rationem quoq; reddit Paulus. Nam diceret aliquis: Quid vero necesse est, vt tu nos ambias, & zelo tanto propter nos vrarus? Quid enim ad te qui & quales simus, aut quid de nobis fiat? Ita enim solent multi iniqui & ingrati ministerij Ecclesiastici aestimatores, qui animine admoneri aut coerceri volunt. His ergo vt respondeat, Paulus ait: Praeparaui enim vos vni viro virginem puram sistere, nempe Christo. Proci personam suscipit, sed talis, qui non sibi ipsi, sed alteri ambit Virginis alicuius nuptias. In eo fides potissimum requiritur, vt amici causam perinde vt suam agat, neq; aliquod studium aut diligentiam intermittat. Dicit ergo: Quia me aeternus Dei Filius isto honore dignatus est, vt eius nomine procum agam, no potero ei satis fidelis censeri, nisi ipsius affectum induam: qui cum Ecclesiae suae amantissimus sit, & seipsum pro illa in mortem tradiderit, minime decet vt eius causam apud vos remissius aut frigidius agam. Et quia idem ille sponsam suam castam, vel puram potius & incorruptam esse vult, ea etiam mihi cura potissimum incumbit, ne fides qua illi obstrictae esse debetis, aliqua ex parte in vobis labefactetur.
units.tr: Paul also gives an account of his zeal. Someone might say: "Why is it necessary that you court us and burn with such zeal on our behalf? What concern is it of yours who and what sort of people we are, or what becomes of us?" Many unjust and ungrateful judges of the ecclesiastical ministry speak in this way, and they do not want to be admonished or restrained. To answer them, Paul says: "For I have betrothed you to one husband, to present a pure virgin to Christ, namely to Christ." He takes on the role of a suitor, but of a kind who woos a virgin not for himself but for another. In such a case faithfulness above all is required: the friend must plead his cause as though it were his own and spare no care or diligence. So he says: since the eternal Son of God has deemed me worthy of this honour, that I should woo on his behalf, I could not be considered faithful to him unless I put on his own affection. Since he loves his Church most dearly, and has given himself up to death for her, it is wholly fitting that I should not plead his cause among you in a more half-hearted or cold manner. And since he wishes his bride to be chaste, or rather pure and uncorrupted, this care above all presses upon me, lest the faith by which you ought to be bound to him be weakened in any part among you.

units.la: Continet autem parabola haec totum CHRISTI IESV & Ecclesiae eius mysterium, ex quo omnis salus nostra dependet. Haec in eo consistit, vt Deo coeliemur atq; vniamur, qui vnus & solus omnium bonorum atq; verae felicitatis fons est. At natura ab eo alieni sumus, & omnibus hominibus feruit, quod de gentibus Paulus scribit ad Ephesios, quod nimirum filij irae & Dei expertes fuerint. Accesit tamen insuper manifesta defectio a Deo, qualis apud Ezechielem describitur, siue Iudaeos siue gentes spectes. At hic noster ille misertus, nos sibi conciliauit, imo desponsit in Filio suo aeterno & sibi consubstantiali: qui in mundum venit, & homo verus factus nos sibi vniuit, vt ipsius iam Sponsa simus, membra nimirum corporis sui, & (quod Adam de Eua sua dicebat) caro ex carne eius & os ex ossibus eius. Sumus ergo eius consortes, & eiusdem cum ipso regni atque beatitudinis participes, adeo, cohaeredes. Hoc enim coniugij ius est, vt sicuti corpora vniuntur, & qui duo erant vna caro fiunt: ita bonorum quoque communio vtrinque fiat, & eandem fortunam, siue laetam siue tristem, vna ferant. Id vero inter nos & Christum quam maxime locum habet. Vt enim hic propter nos in mundum venit & nostros labores atque infirmitates in se transfulit: ita nos quoque ad crucem vocat, & eos qui in ea ferenda ipsi conformes fiunt, caelestis etiam regni & gloriae cohaeredes facit, in quam per mortem diram & infamem ingressus est. Quod enim Apostolis dicitur: Vos estis, qui mecum permansistis in tentationibus meis, & ego vobis paciscor, prout mihi pactus est Pater meus Regnum, &c. hoc ipsum ad omnes credentes extendi debet. Nam hoc Filij Dei testamentum est, quod iam mortem aditurus condidit: Volo Pater, vt vbi sum ego, illic etiam sint quos dedisti mihi. Et ne quis hoc ad solos Apostolos restringi debere putaret, prius dixerat: Non pro his solis rogo, verumetiam pro omnibus, qui creditypи sunt per sermonem eorum in me. Et huius generis multa in vtriusque Testamenti libris occurrunt, quae omnia admirabilem & plus quam paternam Dei bonitatem nobis commendant. Finge enim Regem potentissimum puellae ignobilis & pauperculae nuptias ambire, & eandem regni sui & coronae consortem facere: quis non istud miraretur? quis principis illius humanitatem & modestiam non praedicaret? Atqui nulla ea esset, si cum eo conferatur quod Deus fecit. Illic enim est natura similitudo, & licet puellae conditio inferior sit, non minus tamen homo est, quam Rex nobilissimus. Magna item ad amorem conciliandum vis est formae & virtutis, quae in pauperrimis saepe locum habent. At inter Deum & nos nulla neque naturae neque conditionis differentia, nihil praeterea in nobis fuit amore dignum: quia quanti quanti sumus, corrupti & peccatis polluti sumus, & tales, quales per Ezechielem Dominus describit. Quare totum hoc gratuitae misericordiae opus est.
units.tr: This parable contains the whole mystery of Christ Jesus and his Church, on which all our salvation depends. It consists in this: that we are joined to God and united with him, who alone is the one fount of all good things and of true happiness. But by nature we are alien from him, and we are all liable to wrath, as Paul writes of the Gentiles to the Ephesians, that they were without doubt children of wrath and strangers to God. Moreover, there is also a manifest defection from God, such as is described in Ezekiel, whether you look at the Jews or the Gentiles. But this merciful God, our Lord, has won us to himself, indeed has betrothed us in his eternal Son, who is consubstantial with him. He came into the world, and having become true man, he united us to himself, so that we are now his bride, namely the members of his body, and (as Adam said of his Eve) flesh of his flesh and bone of his bones. We are therefore his partners, and sharers with him in the same kingdom and blessedness, and indeed co-heirs. For this is the right of marriage: just as bodies are united, and the two who were one flesh become one, so also the sharing of goods is made mutual on both sides, and they bear the same fortune, whether joyful or sad. And this holds especially true between us and Christ. For just as he came into the world for our sake and transferred our labours and infirmities onto himself, so he also calls us to the cross, and makes those who are conformed to him in bearing it co-heirs of the heavenly kingdom and glory, into which he entered through a cruel and infamous death. For what is said to the Apostles: "You are those who have remained with me in my trials, and I make a covenant with you, just as my Father has covenanted the kingdom with me," etc., this same thing must be extended to all believers. For this is the testament of the Son of God, which he made when he was about to meet death: "Father, I desire that where I am, there also may be those whom you have given me." And lest anyone think that this should be restricted to the Apostles alone, he had said earlier: "I do not pray for these alone, but also for all who believe in me through their word." Many things of this kind occur in the books of both Testaments, and all of them commend to us the admirable and more than paternal goodness of God. Imagine a most powerful king wooing the marriage of an obscure and poor girl, and making her the partner of his kingdom and crown: who would not marvel at this? Who would not praise that prince's kindness and modesty? Yet this would be nothing if compared with what God has done. For there is a likeness of nature in that case, and although the girl's condition is lower, she is no less a human being than the most noble king. Likewise, beauty and virtue, which are often found among the poorest, have great power to win love. But between God and us there is no difference either of nature or of condition, and there was nothing in us worthy of love; for however great we are, we are corrupt and polluted by sins, and such as the Lord describes through Ezekiel. Therefore this whole matter is a work of free mercy.

units.la: At hic illud quoque considerandum dignum est, quod Paulus se procum fingit, cui ab ipso Christo hoc negotium datum sit, vt Corinthios ipsi Virginem puram adducat. Tale quid de semetipso metipso Baptista discipulis suis dixit: Etsi enim Deus solus hoc coniugium perficiat, idque ex gratuito amore, quo nos complexus est, & quo nostra quoque corda sibi conciliat (quis enim, nisi ipse hoc confectum vellet, nos ad tantam dignitatem posset evehere? )idem tamen hominum opera vti dignatur: quod nouum est bonitatis eius argumentum. Inter homines fere ea insolentia regnat, vt nemo pene nisi coactus se inferiorum ministerio vtatur. At Deus miseros mortales sibi cooperarios & quasi adiutores asciscit in re omnium maxima, qua & gloria eius illustratur, & salus nostra omnis perficitur. Qui vero sunt illi? Verbi sui praeconesper quos nos, qui ab ipso natura alieni sumus, vocat, trahit, regenerat, innouat & sibi conciliat. Ab his ergo requiritur, primum, vt Christum sponsum Ecclesiae ament. Deinde vt sponsam huic vni adducant, & quidem virginem, nullo falsorum Deorum amore praeoccupatam, aut superstitionibus corruptam. Imo ne sibi ipsis quidem illam vendicare cupiant. Hoc enim impostorum est, qui vnicam illam Christi sponsam in sectas distrahunt, vt alibi diximus. Tertio, vt zelo Dei accensi nihil ferre possint, quo Ecclesiae fides & integritas violetur, aut saltem in suspicionem veniat. Talis olim Moses erat, qui conspecto vitulo aureo, quo Dei iram Israelitae provocabant, totus exarsit, & abiectis tabulis Dei digito inscriptis (quibus nihil in terra nobilius & pretiosius vnquam visum fuit) ad vindictam sese accinxit. Similem zelum in Elia & reliquis Prophetis fuisse scimus: vt postea in Apostolis, quibus intolerabilis blasphemia visa fuit, si qui Deo debitos honores voluerunt in ipsos transferre. Qui hic frigent, nunquam rem facient, & facile priuati honoris & gloriae studio sese superari patientur.
units.tr: Here it is also worth considering that Paul pictures himself as a suitor, to whom this business has been given by Christ himself, so that he may bring the Corinthians to him as a pure virgin. John the Baptist said something similar about himself to his disciples. For although God alone accomplishes this marriage, and does so out of the free love with which he has embraced us, and by which he also wins our hearts to himself (for who, unless he himself wished this to be done, could raise us to such a dignity?), he nevertheless deigns to use the work of men, which is a new proof of his goodness. Among men, arrogance generally reigns, so that almost no one uses the service of his inferiors unless compelled to do so. But God takes wretched mortals as his fellow-workers and, as it were, helpers, in the greatest matter of all, by which his glory is made illustrious and all our salvation is brought to completion. And who are these? They are the heralds of his Word, through whom he calls, draws, regenerates, renews and wins to himself us, who are by nature alien from him. Of these, therefore, three things are required: first, that they love Christ as the bridegroom of the Church; second, that they bring the bride to this one husband, and indeed a virgin, not preoccupied by any love of false gods, nor corrupted by superstitions; and indeed that they not even desire to claim her for themselves. For this belongs to impostors, who tear that one bride of Christ into sects, as we have said elsewhere. Third, that, kindled with zeal for God, they can bear nothing by which the faith and integrity of the Church would be violated, or at least come under suspicion. Moses was such a man of old: when he saw the golden calf by which the Israelites provoked God's anger, he blazed up entirely, and, casting down the tablets inscribed by God's finger (than which nothing more noble and precious was ever seen on earth), he girded himself for vengeance. We know that Elijah and the other Prophets had a similar zeal, and afterwards so did the Apostles, to whom blasphemy seemed intolerable if anyone sought to transfer to themselves the honours owed to God. Those who grow cold here will never accomplish anything, and will easily allow themselves to be overcome by the desire for private honour and glory.

units.la: Ista vero simul de Ecclesia & singulorum fidelium officio nos admonent. Praecipuum hic est, vt Virgines sint purae. Virgo dicitur, quae nullum virum experta, & proinde incorrupta est. Castitas latius patet, & vxori quoq; tribuitur, quae fidem coniugalem seruat inuiolatam. Ea igitur conditione nos Christus sibi desponsauit, vt virginitatem ad eum afferamus puram, & eandem ipsi seruemus integram atq; inuiolatam. Magnum mysterium, quod Chrysostomus quoq; hoc loco obseruauit. Quae inter homines nubunt, hae ex virginibus mulieres fiunt. At qui Christo nubunt, ij virgines manent: imo qui non fuerunt virgines, fiunt. Quae autem est illa Virginitas? Ab vno Deo pendere confitanti fide per IESVM CHRISTVM, quem ille nobis Mediatorem dedit, illum vnum diligere ex toto corde, colere item & adorare in spiritu & veritate, sicut ille nobis praecepit. Etenim scortari aut fornicari dicitur in Scripturis, qui relicto vno vero Deo ad Deos alienos defiiciut, & idola siue simulachra venerantur. Itaq; huc pertinent, quae Deus in foedere cū Abrahamo facto, in Lege item de se vno diligendo, inuocando & colendo tradit. Et debent singuli sibi ipsis applicare, quod in Psalmo canitur: Audi filia, & vide, & inclina aurem tuam: obliuiscere populi tui, & domus patris tui, &c. Qui ista praestant, hi sponsa Christi sunt, & Ecclesia illa Catholica, quam in Symbolo profitemur. Cum qua si Romanam conferas, quae titulum hunc sibi soli vendicat, mox videbis, quid de ea iudicari debeat. Quomodo enim Virgo dicetur, quae iam pridem infinitis alijs sui copiam fecit? quae relicto Deo vno, innumeros sibi patronos & auxiliatores accerfuit? quae Christo debitum amorem & honorem in Diuos caelites transtulit? Qua item ratione casta dicetur, quae scortari nunquam definit? quae ad muta simulachra prosternitur? illa adorat & omni cultus genere prosequitur? cuius membra deniq; Christo quasi abiecto, cui in baptismo nomen dederunt, Franciscani, Dominicani, Benedictini, Bernhardini, Augustiniani, Iacobitae & quid non, potius quam Christiani dici volunt? Est ergo non Virgo illa pura & Christi sponsa incorrupta, de qua hic agitur: sed magna illa mater scortationum, quae abrupto Christianae fidei vinculo impudentissime scortatur in triuijs & compitis & sub omni arbore frondosa (vt Ezechiel loquitur) & cum qua etiam reges terrae scortantur. Vide Apoc.17.
units.tr: These things, however, admonish us at the same time about the Church and about the duty of each faithful person. The chief point here is that the virgins should be pure. A virgin is called one who has known no man and is therefore uncorrupted. Chastity extends more widely, and is also attributed to a wife who keeps her marriage faith inviolate. Christ has therefore betrothed us to himself on this condition, that we bring our virginity to him pure, and keep the same for him whole and inviolate. This is a great mystery, which Chrysostom also observed in this passage. Those who marry among men become women from virgins; but those who marry Christ remain virgins, indeed those who were not virgins become so. What, then, is that virginity? It is to depend on the one God alone by confessing faith in Jesus Christ, whom he gave us as Mediator, to love him alone with the whole heart, likewise to worship and adore him in spirit and in truth, as he has commanded us. For in the Scriptures those are said to commit fornication or whoredom who, having abandoned the one true God, fall away to strange gods and venerate idols or images. Therefore those things pertain to this which God hands down in the covenant made with Abraham, and in the Law, concerning himself as the one to be loved, invoked and worshipped. And each person ought to apply to himself what is sung in the Psalm: "Hear, O daughter, and see, and incline your ear: forget your people and your father's house," etc. Those who do these things are the bride of Christ, and that Catholic Church which we profess in the Creed. If you compare with her the Roman church, which claims this title for itself alone, you will soon see what ought to be judged of her. For how can she be called a virgin who long ago made herself available to countless others? Who, having abandoned the one God, has summoned for herself innumerable patrons and helpers? Who has transferred the love and honour owed to Christ to the heavenly saints? And by what reasoning will she be called chaste, who never ceases to commit fornication? Who prostrates herself before dumb images, and worships them and pays them every kind of cult? Whose members, finally, having cast off Christ, into whose name they were baptised, want to be called Franciscans, Dominicans, Benedictines, Bernardines, Augustinians, Jacobites, and whatever else, rather than Christians. She is therefore not that pure virgin and incorrupt bride of Christ of whom we speak here, but that great mother of fornications, who, having broken the bond of the Christian faith, most shamelessly commits fornication at the crossroads and in the streets, and under every leafy tree (as Ezekiel says), and with whom also the kings of the earth commit fornication. See Revelation 17.

units.la: Caeterum redit Paulus ad id quod de zelo suo dixerat, & ne praeter causam eo vri videatur, ostendit se periculo ipsis imminenti excitari. Ea enim zelotyporum natura est, vt licet nunquam quiescant, tunc tamen toto corde exardeant atq; turbentur, si quid videant, quod ipsis no immerito suspicionem mouere possit. Id vero sibi nunc accidere testatur, dicens: Nam metuo, ne quo modo sicut serpens ille Euam seduxit calliditate sua: ita mentes vestrae corruptae degenerent a simplicitate, quae est in Christo. Timebat Apostolus, non sibi, sed Corinthijs. Et se non praeter causam timewe re exemplo veteri probat: quando diabolus iam olim coeperit in primis parentibus humani generis saluti insidias struere, neq; ingenium suum ab eo tempore mutarit. Historia extat in Genesi Cap. 3. Et probè convenit exemplum illud praesenti argumento, eò quòd primum illud Adami & Evae coniugium euidentem habuit typum Christi & Ecclesiae. Etenim vt Adamus prior à Deo creatus & omnis creaturae dominus fuit princeps constitutus fuit: Ita Christus omnis creaturae primogenitus dicitur, non quòd inter creaturas numerari debeat, sed quia ante mundi creationem ab aeterno ineffabili generatione ex Patre genitus, eidem coaeternus & consubstantialis, & tandē quoad assumptam quoq; humanitatem, omnium dominus constitutus est, & omnem potestatem accepit in coelo & in terra. Deinde vt ex Adami dormientis latere mulier desumpta est: Sic ex Christi morte Ecclesia enata est. Vt Adamus etiam Euam ex se natam mox pro carne & osse suo agnoscit, & eandem sibi arctissimo vinculo despondet; Ita Christus quoq; suum corpus agnoscit Ecclesiam, eamq; sibi vnit & copulat. Ac inter haec semper meminisse oportet, ista de Ecclesia dici, quae adhuc in terris militat, & proinde rem non esse extra periculum.
units.tr: Paul now returns to what he had said about his zeal, and to show that it is not without cause that he burns with it, he declares that he is roused by the danger threatening them. For it is the nature of jealous lovers that, although they are never at rest, they then burn and are thrown into turmoil with their whole heart when they see something that can rightly stir suspicion in them. This, he testifies, is now happening to him, saying: "For I fear lest somehow, as the serpent deceived Eve by his cunning, so your minds be corrupted and fall away from the simplicity that is in Christ." The Apostle feared not for himself but for the Corinthians. And he proves by an ancient example that his fear is not without cause: the devil, who from the beginning began to lay snares for the salvation of the first parents of the human race, has not changed his nature since that time. The story is found in Genesis chapter 3. This example fits the present argument very well, because that first marriage of Adam and Eve clearly bore the type of Christ and the Church. For just as Adam, created first by God and set up as lord of every creature, was made prince, so Christ is called the firstborn of every creature, not because he should be counted among the creatures, but because before the creation of the world he was begotten of the Father from eternity by an ineffable generation, coeternal and consubstantial with him, and finally, also as regards the humanity he assumed, he was made lord of all and received all power in heaven and on earth. Next, just as the woman was taken from the side of the sleeping Adam, so the Church was born from the death of Christ. As Adam, when Eve was brought forth from himself, at once acknowledged her as flesh of his flesh and bone of his bone and betrothed her to himself by the closest bond, so Christ also acknowledges his body, the Church, and joins and unites her to himself. In all this we must always remember that these things are said of the Church which still fights on earth, and therefore the matter is not beyond danger.

units.la: De eo admonet nos Paulus, quando se hoc timere ait, ne Corinthiorum mentes corruptae degenerent à simplicitate, quae est in Christo. Consultò autem sic loquitur: Nec enim homines subito à fide prorsus deficiunt, sed paulatim & quasi per gradus ab eius simplicitate degenerant. Simplicitatis huius regula atque forma in Euangelio habetur, quod docet, quis nam Christus sit, quid nobis in eo datum, quid item nos ei vicissim debeamus? Vt ergo coniugiorum pacta in tabulas consignantur: ita in Euangelio spiritualis huius coniugij pacta descripta sunt. Vt verò tabulis sigilla appendi solent: ita Christus Euangelium & totum illud nouum Testamentum sanguine suo obsignauit, in corda autem nostra dedit arrham Spiritus sancti, cui extrinsecus accedit Baptismus. Quae omnia Paulus supra Capite primo his verbis complexus est: Qui confirmat nos vnà vobiscum in Christum, & qui vnxit nos, Deus est: qui etiam obsignauit nos, & dedit arrham Spiritus in cordibus nostris, &c. Hic ergo videndum est, vt simpliciter insistamus Euangelio, & nec Christum fingamus alium quàm reuera est, neque in eius statutis aliquid ex nostro arbitrio mutemus. In priori errabant pseudoapostoli, qui Christum non sufficere dicebant, nisi Circumcisio & Legis iustitia cum fide in illum coniungerentur: & hi Galatas seduxerunt, quos Paulus in aliud Euangelium translatos esse scribit. In posteriori verò Corinthij offenderunt, qui ritum Coenae mutarunt, & pleraque in coetibus suis faciebant aliter quàm Christus ordinarat. Hodie in utroque passim peccatur. Fingitur enim Christus, qui quotidie immoletur pro peccatis viuentium & mortuorum; cuius item iustitiam nostris operibus & meritis Diuorum perfici oporteat, & apud quem Diuus intercessoribus opus sit. Mutantur etiam ritus Baptismi, Coenae Dominicae, precum item, vnà cum tota Oeconomia Ecclesiae ab Apostolis tradita. Et haec omnia non simul inuecta esse, sed paulatim irrepsisse constat. Ad nos igitur non minus quàm ad Corinthios haec admonitio pertinet, ne videlicet securi simus, sed anxij caueamus, ne quid huius nobis accidat. Si enim Legi Mosis nihil addere licuit, neque ab ea vel ad dexteram vel ad sinistram declinare, multò magis nobis rata esse debet Euangelij per Christum traditi authoritas. Etenim qui vel in minimis sibi aliquid permittunt, mox viterius progressi à simplicitate fidei & religionis Christianae paulatim omnino deficiunt.
units.tr: Paul warns us of this when he says that he fears lest the minds of the Corinthians, being corrupted, fall away from the simplicity that is in Christ. He speaks this way deliberately: men do not fall away from the faith altogether all at once, but gradually and, as it were, step by step they decline from its simplicity. The rule and form of this simplicity is found in the Gospel, which teaches who Christ is, what has been given to us in him, and what in turn we owe to him. Just as the terms of marriage are written down in documents, so the terms of this spiritual marriage are described in the Gospel. And just as seals are commonly hung from documents, so Christ sealed the Gospel and the whole New Testament with his blood, and gave the pledge of the Holy Spirit into our hearts, to which Baptism is added from without. Paul summed up all these things in the first chapter above in these words: "Now he who establishes us with you in Christ, and who anointed us, is God; who also sealed us and gave the pledge of the Spirit in our hearts," and so on. Here, then, we must see that we simply cling to the Gospel, neither feigning Christ to be other than he truly is, nor changing anything in his ordinances by our own judgment. In the former error the false apostles went astray, who said that Christ was not enough unless circumcision and the righteousness of the Law were joined with faith in him; and these led the Galatians astray, whom Paul writes were carried over to another gospel. In the latter the Corinthians stumbled, who changed the rite of the Lord's Supper and did many things in their assemblies otherwise than Christ had ordained. Today men sin everywhere in both ways. For Christ is feigned to be one who is sacrificed daily for the sins of the living and the dead; and it is said that his righteousness must be completed by our works and the merits of the saints, and that with him the saints need intercessors. The rites of Baptism, of the Lord's Supper, and likewise of prayers are changed, together with the whole order of the Church handed down by the Apostles. It is evident that all these things were not introduced at once, but crept in gradually. This warning therefore applies to us no less than to the Corinthians: that we should not be secure, but anxiously take care lest anything of this kind happen to us. For if nothing was allowed to be added to the Law of Moses, nor to turn aside from it either to the right or to the left, much more ought the authority of the Gospel delivered through Christ to remain firm for us. Indeed, those who permit themselves anything even in the smallest matters soon advance further and gradually fall away altogether from the simplicity of the faith and the Christian religion.

units.la: Excitet nos tanti mali author, quem Paulus eundem nobis monstrat, qui omnium nostrum matrem, Euam, seduxit sub serpentis specie: & illi astutiam tribuit, quae & tunc mirifica fuit, & qua adhuc hodie uti solet. Primò enim astutiae fuit, quòd non Adamum, sed Euam priorem aggressus est, quam sciebat infirmiorem esse, & proinde facilius vinci posse. Ita hodie infirmiores imprimis tentare solet, & quidem mulierculis maximè insidiatur, quas natura procliuiores esse constat ad superstitiones simul & morum leuitatem. Et huc pertinet, quod Paulus alibi scribit suo tempore fuisse impostores, qui familijs sese insinuabant, vt mulierculas, quae peccatis onerat erant, & cupiditatibus variis agebantur, captiuas ducerent. Quod vt hodie in Papatu per Monachos & sub confessionis auricularis praetextu fiat, notius est quàm vt demonstrationem requirat. Deinde solam Euam aggreditur, quae non sola vagari, sed viro comes & socia indiuulsa haerere debebat. Ita hodie eos adoritur Satan, qui αὐτοσχεδιάζοντες sunt, & proinde solis sibi sapiunt, & in
units.tr: Let us be stirred by the author of so great an evil, whom Paul shows to us as the same one who seduced Eve, the mother of us all, under the appearance of a serpent; and he attributes to him a cunning which was remarkable then and which he still customarily uses today. First, it was a mark of his cunning that he attacked not Adam but Eve first, whom he knew to be the weaker and therefore more easily overcome. So today he is accustomed above all to tempt the weaker, and he especially lays snares for silly women, who are known to be more prone by nature to superstition and to lightness of morals. To this belongs what Paul writes elsewhere, that in his time there were impostors who insinuated themselves into households and led captive the little women who were weighed down with sins and driven by various desires. That this is done today in Papistry through the monks and under the pretext of auricular confession is better known than that it needs proof. Second, he attacked Eve alone, though she ought not to wander alone but cling inseparably to her husband as companion and partner. So today Satan assails those who are self-taught, and who therefore are wise only to themselves, and who wander in the intention and pleasures of their own minds. [Thus the text continues in the next unit.]

units.la: 2. Tim. 3. & in sui animi intentione atque placitis vagantur. Curent ergo omnes, ne quid suo ingenio indulgeant, neque à Christo sponso vnquam discedant, sed (vt Pater cœlitus iussit) hunc vnum audiant. Curent item ministri, ne ipsi ab Ecclesijs suis temere discedant, & dum ipsi vagantur, eos vagari & seduci sinant, pro quibus olim rationem Christo reddere cogentur. Tertiò larvam serpentis, animalium astutissimi accepit diabolus, qua se occultaret. Ita fere sub larua sapientiæ se venditat, & per eos rem suam conficere studet, qui apud rude vulgus summam doctrinæ & sapientiæ existimationem sustinent. Fecit hoc olim per Magos, Baalamum, pseudoprophetas, Pharisæos, Scribas & gentium philosophos: & hodie idem facit per Doctores Seraphicos, Magistros nostros, Iuris & legum peritos, qui religionis causam ad humanæ rationis calculum revocant. Quartò beneuolentiam simulauit, & quod hominum saluti consultum cuperet: imò quasi rerum ignarus de Dei edicto Euam scisci tatur, vt facilius se huius animo insinuet. Ita hodie eius organa mirificè se apud omnis loci & ordinis homines insinuant, quaritantur item de multorum ignorantia & cæcitate, se totis visceribus commoueri dicunt propter miserabilem Ecclesiæ distractionem, & si ipsi audiantur, non modò pacem & læta omnia, verumetiam ipsos cœlos pollicentur. Finis verò omnium hic illi propositus fuit olim, vt Eua contempto Dei edicto ex arbore vetita comedat: & ideo hunc falsi simul atque odij insimulauit. Fiebat hoc apud Corinthios, vt ex licentia morum apparet, quam scioli inuexerant. Fit idem hodie quoque. Fingitur Deus alius quàm reuera sit, Verbo eius fides derogatur, vt ita ab illo discedamus, in quo vno salus inuenitur. Itaque primi huius stratagematis diaboli memores assiduè vigilemus. Huius enim lenones sunt, quicunque nos solicitant, vt ab Euangelij simplicitate vel latum vnguem discedamus: & vt matronæ pudicitia suspecta fit, quàm primum lenonibus aures præbet, & eadem fere tandem expugnatur: Ita fieri vix potest, quin nostræ etiam mentes inficiantur, si tales audiamus. Ergo quod de ouibus suis CHRISTVS IESVS monuit, huius solius vocem sectemur, & ab eo traditæ doctrinæ insistamus, quæ nos falli non sinet. Ipsi debetur benedictio, honor, gloria & potestas in æternum. Amen.
units.tr: (2 Tim. 3.) Let all therefore take care not to indulge their own wit in anything, nor ever depart from Christ the bridegroom, but hear this one alone, as the Father commanded from heaven. Let ministers likewise take care not to leave their congregations rashly, and, while they themselves wander, not to allow others to wander and be seduced; for these they will one day be compelled to give account to Christ. Third, the devil took on the mask of the serpent, the most cunning of animals, in order to hide himself. So he commonly presents himself under the mask of wisdom, and strives to accomplish his purpose through those who among the uneducated crowd are held in highest esteem for learning and wisdom. He did this formerly through the Magi, Balaam, the false prophets, the Pharisees, the Scribes and the philosophers of the Gentiles; and today he does the same through the Seraphic Doctors, our Masters, and the experts in law and statutes, who call the cause of religion back to the reckoning of human reason. Fourth, he feigned goodwill and concern for the salvation of men; indeed, pretending to be ignorant of the things, he questions Eve about God's command, so that he may more easily insinuate himself into her mind. So today his instruments insinuate themselves wonderfully among men of every place and rank, complain of the ignorance and blindness of many, say that they are moved to the depths of their being by the miserable division of the Church, and promise, if they are heard, not only peace and all good things but even heaven itself. Yet the end proposed to all of them was once this: that Eve, having despised God's command, should eat from the forbidden tree; and therefore he has accused him of falsehood and hatred at the same time. This was happening among the Corinthians, as is clear from the license of morals which the half-learned had introduced. The same happens today also. God is feigned to be other than he really is, faith in his Word is disparaged, so that we may thus depart from him in whom alone salvation is found. Therefore let us keep the first stratagems of the devil constantly in mind and watch. For those are his pimps who solicit us to depart even a hair's breadth from the simplicity of the Gospel; and just as the reputation of a matron becomes suspect as soon as she lends her ears to pimps, and is at last nearly always overcome, so it can hardly fail that our minds too are infected if we listen to such people. Therefore, what Christ Jesus warned concerning his sheep, let us follow the voice of him alone, and keep to the doctrine handed down by him, which will not allow us to be deceived. To him be blessing, honour, glory and power for ever. Amen.

units.la: HOMILIA XLVII.
units.tr: HOMILY XLVII.

units.la: Enimuerò si is qui venit, alium IESVM prædicet, quem non prædicauimus: aut si spiritum alium accipiatis, quem non accepistis: aut Euangelium aliud, quod non accepistis: recte eum tolerastis. Puto enim me nihilo inferiorem fuisse ijs, qui sunt summi Apostoli. Quòd si rudis sum sermone, non tamen cognitione; sed omnino manifesti facti sumus in omnibus erga vos.
units.tr: For if he who comes preaches another Jesus, whom we have not preached, or if you receive another spirit, which you have not received, or another gospel, which you have not received, you tolerate him well enough. For I think I was not a whit inferior to those who are the chief apostles. But even if I am rude in speech, I am not so in knowledge; rather, we have been thoroughly made manifest to you in all things.

units.la: QVoniam in æternæ salutis negotio non sufficit Euangelium audiuisse, & Christo semel nomen dedisse, nisi in fidei simplicitate & eius vera professione in finem vsque perseueremus: ministrorum quoque Verbi Dei est, vt homines non solum adducant Christo, verumetiam sedulò hoc agant, vt qui hunc semel amplexi sunt, in fide constantes, nullis rationibus se à simplici eius Veritate dimoueri patiantur. Nam si hoc fiat, iam labor omnis illis perit, & eorum similes sunt, qui magnis laboribus parta negligentius custodiunt, & rursus dilabi sinunt. Obseruarunt hoc diligenter Apostoli, qui ideo Ecclesias abs se constitutas frequenter inuisebant, vt infirmiores in fide confirmarent, vitijs mederentur & collapsa instaurarent: & si id per negotia non licebat, missis ad eas literis admonebant de ijs, quæ factu necessaria erant. Faciunt huc imprimis quæ in proximo Sermone audiuimus. Testatur enim Paulus, se Corinthios quidem Christo præparauisse, vt huic eos sistat instar puræ & castæ Virginis: At simul non dissimulat solicitudinem suam, quæ zelotypum faciat, adeò vt timeat, ne diaboli insidijs & dolis locum dent, vt olim Eua fecit, & ita à fidei simplicitate deficiant. Ne autem quis ipsum timore non necessario angi diceret, nunc ad rem ipsam propius accedit, & eorum leuitatem apertius accusat, qua impostores pseudoapostolos, saniorís doctrinæ corruptores, admiserint. Sic autem ait:
units.tr: Since in the business of eternal salvation it is not enough to have heard the gospel and to have given one's name to Christ once, unless we persevere to the end in the simplicity of faith and its true profession, it is also the duty of the ministers of God's Word not only to bring men to Christ, but also to take care that those who have once embraced him stay constant in faith and suffer themselves to be turned away from his simple truth by no arguments. For if this happens, all their labour is lost, and they are like those who keep carelessly what they have won with great toil, and allow it to slip away again. The apostles observed this carefully. This is why they often revisited the churches they had founded, to strengthen the weaker in faith, to remedy faults, and to restore what had fallen; and when they could not do so because of their affairs, they sent letters to them, admonishing them about what was necessary to be done. What we heard in the sermon just before bears on this above all. For Paul testifies that he had prepared the Corinthians for Christ, so as to present them to him as a pure and chaste virgin. But at the same time he does not conceal his anxiety, which makes him jealous, so much so that he fears they may give the devil's snares and tricks a place, as Eve once did, and so fall away from the simplicity of faith. Lest anyone should say that he is troubled by a needless fear, he now comes closer to the matter itself and more openly accuses their levity, by which they admitted deceivers, false apostles and corrupters of the sounder doctrine. He speaks thus:

units.la: Enimuero si is qui venit, alium IESVM praedicet, quem non praedicauimus, &c. Loquitur de certo quodam & insigni impostore, qui à nemine legitimè missus Corinthum venerat, & quem ipsi non sine sua ignominia receperant. Videtur autem idem ille fuisse, cuius verba in praecedenti Capite adduxit, quod nimirum de ipso soleret dicere: Epistolae quidem graues sunt & validae: sed praesentia corporis infirma, & sermo nihili. Quia vero toti ab illo pendebant Corinthij, adeo vt Paulum & alios germanos Christi Apostolos fastidirent, offendit his verbis quam indigne hoc faciant: & tria ex ordine recenseт, quae hic ipsis sint consideranda: Primum, an alium IESVM siue Seruatorem praedicet, de quo prius non audierint. Alterum, an ex illius praedicatione alium spiritum acceperint, quam quem prius habuerint. Loquitur autem de miraculoso Spiritus sancti dono, quod tunc credentibus conferebatur, vt in Actorum historia & in epistola ad Galatas esse videre, in quibus similem leuitatem Apostolus reprehendit. Tertium, an aliud Euangelium à nouo illo doctore annuntietur, id est, an doctrinam afferat pleniorem & perfectiorem de humanae salutis ratione, quam quae ab Apostolis hucusque sit tradita, qui suam ex ipso Christo acceperint.
units.tr: "For if he who comes preaches another Jesus, whom we have not preached," etc. He is speaking of a certain notable impostor who had come to Corinth without being lawfully sent by anyone, and whom they had received, not without his own disgrace. Now it seems that this was the same man whose words he quoted in the preceding chapter, which he would evidently say about him: "His letters are weighty and strong, but his bodily presence is weak, and his speech is worthless." Since the Corinthians depended wholly on this man, so much so that they despised Paul and the other true apostles of Christ, he is offended, and in these words he shows how unworthily they act; and he lists three things in order which they should consider here. First, whether he preaches another Jesus or Saviour, of whom they had not heard before. Second, whether through his preaching they have received another spirit than the one they had before. He speaks here of the miraculous gift of the Holy Spirit, which was then conferred on believers, as we see in the history of the Acts and in the epistle to the Galatians, where the apostle rebukes a similar levity. Third, whether another gospel is announced by this new teacher, that is, whether he brings a fuller and more perfect doctrine of the way of human salvation than that which has been handed down until now by the apostles, who received theirs from Christ himself.

units.la: Videntur autem ista pugnare cum eo quod ad Galatas Capite primo habetur, vbi eos reprehendit, qui se in aliud Euangelium transferri passi erant, & addit: Si nos, aut Angelus è caelo euangelizet vobis praeter id, quod euangelizauimus vobis, anathema sit. At si rem ipsam considerec, nulla est contradictio. Illic enim aliud Euangelium dicitur pro falso, fictitio & adulterino, quod Euangelio vero & germano opponitur: Et praeterid quod Apostoli praedicarunt euangelizare dicuntur, qui illorum doctrinā aliquid addunt, nouos fidei articulos condunt, aut aliam salutis rationem monstrant ab ea, quae nobis ab Apostolis est tradita. In praesenti simplicius & conditionaliter loquitur Paulus, & sensus est: Si nouus ille & obreptitius doctor aliquid afferret profectius, melius, certius, vt per ipsum pleniori cognitione instrueremini, dona item praestantiora & veriora vobis conferret, ita vt ex eo intelligeretis nos aliquid omisisse eorum, quae traditu & cognitu necessaria sunt, merito sane illum tolerareti. Sed cum nihil huius dici posset, & quoad fidei atque salutis capita nihil vobis tradi queat à quoquam, quod non prius ex nobis didiceritis, adhuc iam ante etiam excelleritis omni scientia, cognitione, fide, charitate, prophetia, linguarum & interpretationis dono, ista vero nihil praeter humanae sapientiae figmenta, fucato sermonis ad ostentationem compositi splendore palliata, afferat: nimium profecto faciles, vel potius leues estis, qui me contempto illum tanti facitis, & praeter causam necessariam, vestra hac instabilitate totam Christianae religionis causam apud cives & vicinos vestros in suspicionem adducitis.
units.tr: These things seem to conflict with what is found in the first chapter to the Galatians, where he rebukes those who had allowed themselves to be transferred to another gospel, and adds: "If we, or an angel from heaven, preach to you anything beyond what we have preached to you, let him be accursed." But if one considers the matter itself, there is no contradiction. There "another gospel" is spoken of as false, fictitious and counterfeit, opposed to the true and genuine gospel; and by "beyond what the apostles preached" are meant those who add something to their teaching, invent new articles of faith, or show a way of salvation other than that handed down to us by the apostles. In the present passage Paul speaks more simply and conditionally, and the sense is this: if that new and sneaking teacher brought something more advantageous, better and more certain, so that through him you might be instructed in a fuller knowledge, and if he conferred on you more excellent and truer gifts, so that you might understand that we had omitted any of the things that are necessary to be taught and known, then indeed you would be right to tolerate him.
