If this should happen, then I, who ought to receive joy and consolation from you, shall be humbled by God and cast down in my whole mind, seeing that the success of my ministry has not been as happy as I thought. Indeed, if I find some who have not yet repented, who have sinned most shamefully before by fornication and every kind of impurity, and who, although admonished, still persist obstinately in their sins, I shall be forced to mourn, I who hoped to rejoice with you. But in saying this he throws the blame for all the severity he has so far used upon those who, by their stubborn insolence, compel him to be other than he wishes. Paul therefore acts here just as a father who, abroad, writes to a household that he has learned lives too loosely: "I indeed, dearest ones, desire to return home, and I burn wholly with longing for you; yet I cannot deal with you now as I would wish. For I hear such things about you as make me greatly anxious, so that on my return I shall be tormented more, and, shamed by that wantonness and insolence of yours, I shall be forced to show myself other than you wish, since you too are other than I would wish you to be."

units.la: Possunt haec & alia huius generis hodie multis dici, qui de nimio ministrorum Verbi rigore queruntur, & vellent doctores habere blandos, mites & suaues, qui nihil quàm Dei gratiam praedicent, & amicis diuini fauoris pollicitationibus omnes consolentur, & tantumnon cum impijs illis, quos Isaias corripit, Dei serui dicunt: Ne contemplemini nobis plana, loquimini nobis blanda, contemplemini illusiones, recedite à via, declinate à semita, facite quiescere a facie nostra Sanctum Israelis. Atqui diuinae gratiae praedicatio ibi locum habet, vbi peccatorum agnitio est, vbi animorum contritio, vbi studium reconciliationis cum Deo, vbi deniq; minister dicere potest, quod olim Paulus de Thessal. suis dicebat: Vos estis gloria nostra & gaudium. At si nostra tempora propius consideres, latius istis gratiae Dei & meriti IESV CHRISTI denuntiationibus minimè opus est, quando peccatorum sensu nemo tangitur, nemo irae Dei metu contremiscit, nemo poenis infelicem hunc mundum vndique vrgentibus mouetur, vt de Deo placando serio cogitet: sed potius omnis loci & ordinis homines effreni & indomita licentia in sceleribus pergunt. Contritis & fractis μαλάγματα siue dolorem mitigantia vnguenta adhibentur, emortua verò & stupentia membra durius tractari, & interdum vri vel etiam resecari necesse est, ne alias quoq; corpo ris partes inficiant. Insunt autem his Pauli verbis nonnulla, quae diligentius considerari merentur.
units.tr: These things, and others of this kind, can be said today to many who complain of the excessive rigour of the ministers of the Word, and who would like teachers to be flattering, mild and gentle, who preach nothing but the grace of God and console everyone with promises of friendly divine favour, and who, just like those wicked men whom Isaiah rebukes, say: "Speak to us smooth things, prophesy to us deceits; get out of the way, turn aside from the path, cause the Holy One of Israel to cease from before us." Yet the preaching of divine grace has its place where there is recognition of sins, where there is contrition of souls, where there is a zeal for reconciliation with God, and where at last the minister can say what Paul once said to his Thessalonians: "You are our glory and joy." But if we consider our own times more closely, there is by no means so much need of these proclamations of the grace of God and the merit of Jesus Christ, since no one is touched by a sense of sins, no one trembles at the fear of God's wrath, no one is moved by the punishments that press upon this unhappy world on every side, so as to think seriously about appeasing God; rather, men of every rank and station persist in their crimes with unbridled and untamed license. For the bruised and broken, soothing ointments [μαλάγματα] or softening unguents are applied; but dead and numb limbs must be handled more harshly, and sometimes burned or even cut away, lest they infect the other parts of the body too. Yet there are in these words of Paul some things which deserve to be considered more carefully.

units.la: Primum, quòd postea scriptam ad ipsos priorem epistolam adhuc tales fuerunt, neque à vitiis illis emendati sunt, quae Apostolus tanta cum grauitate & seueritate corripuerat. Ergo ne Apostoli quidem semper potuerunt effectum dare quod volebant: quod ipsum de Prophetis quoque potest dici, qui interdum non sine acerbis lachrymis de populi contumacia & sua sorte conqueruntur. Ex quibus apparet, nullam diligentiam nimiam censeri posse, quae in corripiendis & corrigendis hominum vitijs adhibetur. Semper enim haerent veteres peccati reliquiae, & noua iidem vitia in moribus pullulant, dum indies nouis illecebris nos mundus hic cum suo principe ine scare & irretire studet. Nunquam non ergo ministri in excubijs esse, & operi insistare debent, ne qui ipsorum culpa pereant.
units.tr: First, that after the earlier epistle was written to them, they were still such, and had not been amended of those faults which the apostle had rebuked with such gravity and severity. Therefore not even the apostles could always bring about what they wished; and this can also be said of the prophets, who sometimes complain, not without bitter tears, of the people's obstinacy and their own lot. From these things it appears that no diligence can be considered excessive which is applied in rebuking and correcting men's faults. For the remnants of old sin always cling on, and new vices sprout again in morals, while this world, with its prince, daily strives to ensnare and entangle us with fresh allurements. Therefore ministers must never cease to be on watch and to keep at their work, lest any perish through their fault.

units.la: Interim admonet nos locus iste, non temere damnari debere ministros, in quorum ecclesijs non omnes ipsorum votis atque laboribus respondent. Vt enim boni parentes non omnia semper in suis emendare possunt, & Reges quoq; optimi in suis multa praeter animi voluntatem tolerant, quos nec commode ferre, neq; tutò eijcere aut dimittere possunt: Ita fere in Ecclesijs solet fieri, ijs praesertim, quae populosiores sunt, & cum vicinis à fide alienis commercia habere coguntur, aut etiam sub principibus agunt, qui religionem veram oderunt. Illic enim si quis omnia ad viuum resecare conetur, Ecclesiam citius omnem turbauerit, quàm omnes in ordinem redegerit. Quid ve-rò tunc aliud faciat minister, quàm vt lugeat, & occasionem expectet commodiorem, qua quod vult aliquando effectum dare possit? Nemo tamen ex his sibi suae ignauiae patrocinium quaerat, vt se tunc quoq; putet excusatum fore apud Deum, si turpiter ad ea connniueat, quae emendari poterant, si officium vellet facere.
units.tr: Meanwhile this passage admonishes us that ministers should not be rashly condemned in whose Churches not all things answer to their wishes and labours. For just as good parents cannot always correct everything in their own households, and even the best kings tolerate many things in their realms against their will, which they can neither bear easily nor remove or dismiss safely, so it generally happens in Churches, especially those that are more populous, and that are forced to have dealings with neighbours alien to the faith, or even live under princes who hate the true religion. For there, if anyone tries to cut away everything to the quick, he will sooner throw the whole Church into turmoil than bring all into order. What else, then, can the minister do but mourn, and wait for a more convenient opportunity by which he may at some time bring about what he wishes? Yet let no one seek from this a defence for his own laziness, thinking that he will then also be excused before God if he shamefully connives at those things which could have been corrected, had he wished to do his duty.

units.la: Deinde praestat catalogum vitiorum excutere, quae Paulum de Corinthijs solicitum fecerunt. Potest in duas partes diuici. Prima continentur, quae philautia & ambitio inter ipsos pepererat, & ex quibus sectae fuerant enatae, sicuti in priori epistola audiuimus. Ex hoc fonte aemulatio nes nascebantur, dum quisq; illum sibi defendendum proponebat, quem sibi magistrum delegerat. Id verò non sine animorum commotione fiebat, à qua indignatio & ira non potest abesse. Sequebantur ex ea apertae contentiones & rixae. Concurrebant cū his obtrectationes, susurri & calumniae. Inter ista verò alij contra alios inflabantur, quae perpetua tumultuū atq; turbarū causa erat, quibus Ecclesia turbabatur. Sunt haec nobis in eum finem consideranda, vt videamus ex leuibus initijs turbas graues oriri posse, quàm primū carnis affectibus & aemulationi caecae locus datur. Itaq; singuli hac procul relicta vnitatiin CHRISTO IESV studeant, alius alium honore praeeniat, de nemine tamen sublimius sentiat, quàm de homine sentiri debet. Vide 1. Corinth. 3. 4. Cap.
units.tr: Next, he thinks it right to go through the list of vices that troubled Paul about the Corinthians. These may be divided into two parts. The first comprises those things which self-love and ambition had produced among them, and from which factions had sprung, as we heard in the earlier epistle. From this source rose rivalries, since each man set out to defend the one whom he had chosen as his teacher. This could not happen without a stirring of minds, and indignation and anger cannot be absent from such a stirring. From this followed open contentions and quarrels. Along with these came detractions, whisperings and slanders. Meanwhile, some were puffed up against others, which was the constant cause of tumults and disturbances by which the Church was troubled. We must consider these things for this purpose: that we may see how grave disturbances can arise from slight beginnings, as soon as room is given to fleshly passions and to blind rivalry. Therefore, let each one put this far from him and strive for unity in CHRIST JESUS; let one anticipate another in honour, yet let no one think of anyone more highly than a man ought to be thought of. See 1 Corinthians 3 and 4.

units.la: Altera pars ea habet, quae cum sanctimonia pugnant, cui nos Christus consecrauit, & sine quae (vt alibi Paulus monet) nemo videbit Deū. Perpetuò enim ratum manebit, quod in Lege toties inculcatur: Sancti estote, quoniam & ego Sanctus sum. Item: Haec est voluntas Dei, nempe sanctificatio vestra. Pugnat cum hac Impuritas, quam hic vt genus primo loco ponit, sub qua species omnes complectitur, ex quibus duas modo nominat: Scortationem & Proteruiam. Ad Scortationem referri debent omnes libidines vagae & illicitae, quae singulae corpora nostra polluunt, quae Christus vt Spiritus Sancti templa sint, sanguine suo consecrauit. Proteruia impudentem & lasciuam animi petulantiam significat, quae se in vestitu, gestibus, cantu, scurrilibus dictis aliisq; similibus animi inhonesti indicijs exerit. Erant autem omnia ista nimis vulgaria apud Corinth. adeò vt ipsorum vrbs propter libidines proverbijs quoq; notaretur, vt alibi diximus. Merito igitur de his illos Paulus in praesenti admonet. Nos verò ista ideo scriptus mandata & in hodiernum vsq; diem conseruata esse cogitemus, vt omnes discant, vitia haec à Christianis hominibus alienissima esse debere, nimium verò impudentes esse eos, qui illa excusare audent.
units.tr: The second part contains those things which are at odds with the holiness to which Christ has consecrated us, and without which (as Paul warns elsewhere) no one will see God. For what is so often impressed upon us in the Law will remain forever true: "Be holy, for I am holy." Likewise: "This is the will of God, namely your sanctification." Against this stands impurity, which here Paul places first as the genus, under which he embraces all the species, of which he names only two: fornication and wantonness. To fornication must be referred all wandering and unlawful lusts, which each defile our bodies, which Christ consecrated with his own blood so that they might be temples of the Holy Spirit. Wantonness signifies a shameless and lascivious petulance of mind, which shows itself in dress, gestures, singing, buffoonish speech and other similar signs of a dishonourable mind. All these things were indeed far too common among the Corinthians, so that their city was even marked by proverbs because of its lusts, as we have said elsewhere. Rightly, therefore, Paul admonishes them about these matters here. And we should consider that these things were written as commands and have been preserved down to the present day, so that all may learn that these vices ought to be most alien to Christian people, and that those who dare to excuse them are exceedingly shameless.

units.la: Praeterea obseruatu dignū est, quid Paulus se de iis decreuisse aut statuisse dicat. Nū minatur, quòd istos omnes excommunicare & diabolo tradere velit? Nū vt Caena Domini arceantur iubet? Nihil huius dicit. Atqui ea scelera hic nominantur, quae quàm maximè excommunicatione multari debent, si eos audiamus, qui hodie causam ista agunt. At quis chirurgum probauerit, qui membrum male affectum absque mora resecat? Lentius remedijs opus est, priusquam ad extremum hoc veniatur. Et Paulus eo non nisi in iis vsus est, qui vel secundum Dei Leges capite plecti merebantur (vt alibi in hominis incesti exemplo vidimus) vel nulla alia ratione curari & in ordinem redigi poterant, vt infra in Capite proximo patebit. In praesenti hoc solum dicit: Metuo, ne dum venero, deprimat aut humiliet me Deus meus apud vos, & lugeam multos eorum, qui antea peccarunt, nec resipuerunt super impuritate & scortatione & proteruia, quam patrauerunt. Equidem excommunicare & Satanae tradere possunt omnes, aut saltem se posse exi-stimant, qui imperium sibi sumunt in alios: & prae aliis multum se posse putant hypocritae, qui quos uis prae se fastidiunt, vt in Pharisaeis est videre. Sed aliorum peccata lachrymis ex non ficta charitate manantibus deflere, deq; eorum salute serio cogitare, hoc non nisi piorum & fidelium Christi ministrorum opus est. In eo igitur hodie etiam sint Ecclesiarum pastores, vt primò ex animo doleant, si quos peccare vident cum propriae salutis periculo. Sic Saulem olim Samuel lugebat, quod ipsum alios quoque Prophetas fecisse scimus. Deinde redargutionis, correptionis & exhortā& exhortationis remedia adhibeant. At hic apparet nostri seculi infelicitas: quando plerique ad omnia conniuent, multi etiam risu & iocis ea prosequuntur, quae acerbis lachrymis defleri merebantur: quod in stuprís & vagis libidinibus passim solet fieri. Sed magno constabit aliquando infelici mundo hæc leuitas atque petulantia. Et iam nunc multi manum Domini sentire poterât, nisi toti obstupuissent. At neminem moueat publici exempli authoritas: quin potius æterni Dei Filium, IESVM CHRISTVM, audiamus, quem nobis Pater pœnitentiæ simul & remissionis peccatorum Mediatorem dedit, vt in ipso peccatis mortui vitam viuamus nouam quæ si-dei nostræ professioni respondeat. Ipsi debetur benedictio, honor, gloria & potestas in æternum. Amen.
units.tr: Moreover, it is worth noting what Paul says he has decided or determined about those men. Does he threaten that he will excommunicate all of them and hand them over to Satan? Does he order that they be kept from the Lord's Supper? He says nothing of this. Yet these are the crimes named here, which ought most of all to be punished by excommunication, if we listen to those who today plead this cause. But who would approve a surgeon who cuts off at once a badly diseased limb? Remedies must be gentler before one comes to this extreme. And Paul used it only against those who deserved to be put to death under God's laws (as we saw elsewhere in the example of the incestuous man), or who could not be cured or brought back to order by any other means, as will become clear below in the next chapter. In the present passage he says only this: "I fear that when I come, my God will humble me among you, and I shall mourn many of those who sinned before and have not repented of the impurity, fornication and wantonness which they committed." Indeed, all men may excommunicate and hand over to Satan, or at least think they can, who assume authority over others; and hypocrites, who despise whomever they wish in their own eyes, think they have much power beyond others, as may be seen in the Pharisees. But to lament the sins of others with tears flowing from unfeigned charity, and to think seriously about their salvation, this is the work only of pious and faithful ministers of Christ. Therefore, let the pastors of the Churches today also be such, so that first they grieve in their hearts if they see anyone sinning to the peril of his own salvation. Thus Samuel once mourned Saul, as we know the other prophets also did. Then let them apply the remedies of rebuke, correction and exhortation. But here appears the unhappiness of our age: when most men connive at everything, many even pursue with laughter and jokes those things which deserved to be mourned with bitter tears; this happens commonly in cases of debauchery and wandering lusts. But this lightness and petulance will one day cost the unhappy world dearly. And already now many could perceive the hand of the Lord, had they not been struck completely senseless. Yet let no one be moved by the authority of public example; rather let us listen to the eternal Son of God, JESUS CHRIST, whom the Father has given us as Mediator of repentance and at the same time of forgiveness of sins, so that dead to sins in him we may live a new life which corresponds to our profession of faith. To him be blessing, honour, glory and power forever. Amen.

units.la: CAPVT XIII.
units.tr: CHAPTER XIII.

units.la: HOMILIA LXI.
units.tr: HOMILY LXI.

units.la: TErtia hac vice venio ad vos. In ore duorum aut trium testium consistet omne verbum. Prædixi, & secundò prædico vt præsens, & absens nunc scribo iis, qui ante peccarunt, & reliquis omnibus, fore vt si denuo venero, non parcam: Quandoquidem experimentum quæritis in me loquentis Christi: qui erga vos non est infirmus, sed potens est in vobis. Nam etsi crucifixus fuit ex infirmitate, viuit tamen ex potentia Dei. Nam & nos infirmi sumus in eo, sed viuemus cum eo ex virtute Dei erga vos.
units.tr: For the third time I am coming to you. "By the mouth of two or three witnesses every word shall be established." I have forewarned you, and now, though absent, I warn you a second time, as I did when present, and I write now to those who sinned before and to all the rest: if I come again, I will not spare you. You seek proof that Christ is speaking in me. He is not weak toward you but is powerful among you. For although he was crucified in weakness, he lives by the power of God. We too are weak in him, but we shall live with him by the power of God toward you.

units.la: Tsi magnus esset apud Corinthios eorum numerus, qui de Paulo & eius doctrina honorificè sentiebant, & in ea tuenda erant constantes: non deerant tamen homines improbi & Veritatis osores, qui omnia eius calumniabantur, totiq; in hoc incumbebant, vt tam ipsum quàm eius doctrinam in contemptum adducerent. Hi inter alia eius rigorem accusabant, qua in epistolis contra contumaces & proteruos disciplinæ cotemptores vtebatur, & hunc non debere à quoquam magni fieri dicebant, quando satis constaret, ipsum hominem esse vilem & nullius pretij, qui absens quidem minis grauissimis fulminaret, coràm verò nihil posset, imò ne auderet quidem alicui in faciem dicere quæ literis mandaret. His nuper grauiter respondere cœpit, deq; ipsorum pertinacia conquestus est, adhæc minatus quoque, quod ipsum si venerit ad eos, longè alium experturi sint quàm vellent. Id verò nunc diligentius explicat, & expostulatione vtitur graui, eò quod ipsorum contumaciam maiorem esse videret, quàm vt leuiori admonitione domari posset. Docet autè tota hæc actio, ministros quidem humanos & faciles esse debere, qui malos cum lenitate ferre possint, si quo modo emendentur: at eosdem ijs nequaquam cedere debere, qui aduersus Dei Verbum sese insolentius & pertinacius attollunt, simulq; multos alios suo exemplo offendunt. Debent huc referri Prophetarum exempla, quæ in Scriptura veteri habentur, & de quibus sæpe diximus. Nunc ad huius loci tractationem accedamus.
units.tr: Although the number of the Corinthians who thought well of Paul and his teaching, and who stood firm in defending it, was large, there were still wicked men who hated the truth. They slandered everything he did and devoted all their effort to bringing both him and his teaching into contempt. Among other things, they criticised his severity, which he used in his letters against the stubborn and insolent despisers of discipline. They said that no one should think much of him, since it was clear that the man was worthless and of no account: when absent he thundered out the most severe threats, but when present he could do nothing, and indeed did not even dare to say to anyone's face what he committed to writing. Paul had recently begun to answer these people severely, complaining of their obstinacy and threatening that if he came to them they would find him very different from what they wished. Now he explains this more carefully, and he uses a grave rebuke, because he saw that their obstinacy was too great to be tamed by a gentle admonition. This whole passage teaches that human ministers ought to be gentle and easy-going, able to bear with the wicked patiently if they might in some way be amended; yet they must by no means yield to those who lift themselves up more insolently and stubbornly against the Word of God, and at the same time give offence to many others by their example. The examples of the prophets found in the Old Testament belong here, and we have often spoken of them. Let us now come to the treatment of this passage.

units.la: Principio docet dignos esse, qui durius tractetur, nec habere eos, quo sese excusent, quia abun de admoniti, adhuc tamen pergant in sua contumacia. Tertia hac vice (inquit) venio ad vos. Debet hoc de epistola hac intelligi, quæ de omnibus, quæ ipsis dicenda erant, perinde egit, ac si coràm præsens adfuisset. Et hunc tertium suum ad ipsos aduentum dicit, quia priorem quoque epistolam scripserat, quæ secundi aduentus instar fuerat, cùm prius apud eos per sesquiannum docuisset. Nam quod aliqui Paulum secundò Corinthum venisse putant, constare non potest, si historiæ seriem propius consideremus. Quia ergo primùm apud eos (vt modò diximus) docuerat, quando eos ad fidem Christi conuertit, & Ecclesiam illic constituit nulla in re aliis inferiorem: deinde priorem ad eosdem epistolam miserat, quæ quæ à suo discessu collapsa erant, diligenter instaurauit: & nunc hanc quoque submittat, cui (vt Cap. octauo dictum est) legatos cum suo sum Ecclesiarum nomine adiunxit, quos sciebat non segnius rem actu-ros esse, quàm si ipse coràm adesset: rectè se iam tertia vice ad ipsos venire dicit. Et quia admonitiones testimonia sunt diuinæ bonitatis nos in viam reuocantis, aduentus hosce suos testium loco fore ait, quibus in Dei conspectu conuincantur, ideoque his accommodat Legem, quæ in Mose habetur: In ore duorum aut trium testium consistet omne verbum, id est, omnis controversia siue forensis actio. Argumen-tum sic formari potest, vt sensus fit magis perspicuus: Inexcusabiles sunt, qui duobus aut tribus testibus idoneis conuinci possunt, quod de aliqua re abunde sint praemoniti: At vos plus satis ad-monitos, neque aliquid erga vos praetermissum esse, quod vobis emendandis seruire poterat, bi tres mei aduentus testantur: Ergo nulla vobis excusatio reliqua est, & digni estis, qui posthac du-rius tractemini. Ad probationem siue confirmationem Minoris facit, quod subiicitur: Praedixi (nimirum in priori epistola, me si ita lubeat vobis pergere, cum virga & baculo venturum esse) & nunc secundo praedico vt praesens, dum absens corpore haec scribo ijs, qui prius peccauerunt, & vnà reliquis omnibus, quòd si venire me amplius oporteat, nolim vobis parcere, sed virga illa vti, qua me Dominus armauit. Nam vt saepe diximus, & multi ex Veteribus annotauerunt, corporalibus etiam poenis coercere potuerunt Apostoli eos, qui sua contumacia id merebantur, vt in Ananiae & Elymae Magi exemplis est videre. D. Augustinus certe lib. tertio contra epist. Parmeniani Cap. secundo in haec Pauli verba sic scribit: Quid aliud dixit hic, Non parcam, nisi quod superius ait, Et lugeam multos: Vt luctus eius impetraret flagellum a Domino, quo illi corriperentur, qui iam propter multitudinem non poterant ita corripi, vt ab eorum coniunctione se caeteri continerent? &c.
units.tr: First, he teaches that those who have been admonished many times and still persist in their obstinacy deserve to be dealt with more harshly, and have no excuse. "For the third time," he says, "I am coming to you." This should be understood of this letter, which dealt with all the matters he had to speak about just as if he were present in person. He calls this his third coming to them because he had already written an earlier letter, which was like a second visit, since he had first taught among them for a year and a half. For that Paul went to Corinth a second time cannot be established if we consider the sequence of the history more closely. Since he had first taught among them (as we have just said), when he converted them to the faith of Christ and founded a church there in no way inferior to the others, and then had sent them an earlier letter, by which he carefully restored what had fallen into ruin after his departure, and now sends this one as well, to which (as was said in chapter eight) he added envoys on behalf of the churches, whom he knew would be no less diligent in the matter than if he were there himself, he rightly says that he is now coming to them for the third time. And since admonitions are witnesses of divine goodness calling us back to the right way, he says that his visits will serve as witnesses by which they are convicted in the sight of God. Therefore he applies to this the law found in Moses: "By the mouth of two or three witnesses every word shall be established," that is, every dispute or legal action. The argument may be formed thus, so that the sense becomes clearer: those are without excuse who can be convicted by two or three competent witnesses that they have been sufficiently forewarned about some matter. But you have been admonished more than enough, and nothing has been left undone on our side that could serve to correct you; these three visits of mine bear witness. Therefore you have no excuse left, and you deserve to be dealt with more harshly from now on. What follows supports or confirms the minor premise: "I have forewarned" (namely in the earlier letter, that if you continue as you are, I will come with a rod and a staff), "and now I forewarn a second time, as present, while absent in body I write this to those who sinned before and to all the rest, that if I must come again I will not spare you, but will use that rod with which the Lord has armed me." For, as we have often said, and as many of the ancients have noted, the apostles could also punish with bodily penalties those who deserved it by their obstinacy, as may be seen in the examples of Ananias and of Elymas the magician. St Augustine certainly, in the third book against the letter of Parmenianus, chapter two, writes thus on these words of Paul: "What else did he mean by 'I will not spare', except what he said above, 'and I shall mourn many': that his mourning might obtain from the Lord a scourge by which those would be chastised who, because of their number, could no longer be corrected in such a way that the rest would keep themselves from their fellowship? etc."

units.la: At nos in praesenti obseruemus, quo loco haberi debeant admonitiones seruorum Dei, siue illi coram, siue absentes per literas nos de rebus agendis admoneant. Nimirum, vt testimonia esse meminerimus, quibus Deus ipse suum erga nos studium atque fauorem testatur, quibus item nos inexcusabilis contumaciae convincat, si illas improbe aspernemur. Docet hoc Christus, quando Euangelium aliquibus in testimonium praedicari dicit, & Apostolos puluerem ex pedibus excu-tere iubet aduersus illos in testimonium, qui praedicationi ipsorum locum dare detrectant. Quod si vero puluis ex ministrorum pedibus aut vestimentis excussus sufficit conuincendis Euangeli-cae doctrinae contemptoribus, quanto maius in hac causa pondus erit concionum, scriptorum, pri-matarum admonitionum, laborum, peregrinationum, vigiliarum, tormentorum denique, quae fide-les Christi serui subeunt, dum aeternae salutis Verbum annuntiant, & ad illius hereditatem om-nes adducere satagunt? In his certe ipse Deus contemnitur, sicuti in eius querelis apparet, in qui-bus se nequicquam mane surrexisse & expansis manibus totum diem stetisse dicit, vt rebelles & contumaces ad se conuerteret. Idem Christi querimoniae de colonis perfidis & tota Iudaeorum gen-te docent. Itaque ista nobis applicemus, viri Germani, quibus ea quam maximè seruiunt. Etenim ad nos quoque venit IESVS CHRISTVS, & cum Antichristianae tenebrae omnium mentes occupauissent, nobis laetam atque salutiferam Verbi sui lucem attulit. Ab eo autem tempore non bis aut ter (vt Paulus in praesenti ait) sed millies nos inuisit, imò quotidie ad nos venit monens, hortans, vrgens, increpans, & vt verbis suis fidem faciat, interdum virgas & flagella adhibet. Ni si ergo ei fideles simus, quae obsecro nobis excusatio erit, qui multis millibus testiû conuincimur?
units.tr: But let us observe here what place should be given to the admonitions of the servants of God, whether they admonish us in person or absent by letter about matters to be done. Namely, that we should remember they are witnesses by which God himself attests his zeal and favour toward us, and by which he convicts us of inexcusable obstinacy if we wickedly spurn them. Christ teaches this when he says that the gospel is to be preached to some for a testimony, and bids the apostles to shake the dust from their feet as a testimony against those who refuse to receive their preaching. But if dust shaken from the feet or clothes of ministers is enough to convict the despisers of evangelical doctrine, how much greater weight will there be in this matter of sermons, writings, earlier admonitions, labours, journeys, watchings, and finally the torments which the faithful servants of Christ undergo while they announce the Word of eternal salvation and strive to bring all to its inheritance? In such things God himself is despised, as appears in his complaints, in which he says that he rose early in vain and stood all day with outstretched hands to turn rebels and the stubborn to himself. Christ's complaints about the faithless tenants and the whole nation of the Jews teach the same. So let us apply these things to ourselves, men of Germany, to whom they most of all pertain. For Jesus Christ has come to us too, and when the darkness of Antichrist had possessed the minds of all, he brought us the joyful and saving light of his Word. Since that time he has visited us not twice or three times (as Paul says in the present passage) but a thousand times; indeed he comes to us every day, warning, exhorting, urging, rebuking, and, to make his words believed, sometimes applies rods and scourges. If therefore we are not faithful to him, what excuse, I beg you, will we have, since we are convicted by many thousands of witnesses?

units.la: Obseruabis item hoc loco, quòd tam aperte aliquos perstringit Paulus, vel potius ceu digito notat, vt omnes potuerint intelligere, de quibus nam loqueretur. Quòd si, cur hoc fecerit, quaeras, in promptu est ratio: Nimirum, quòd peccata eorum non occulta, sed publica & omnibus nota, imò cum publico scandalo coniuncta erant. Simili ergo modo cum omnibus agi debet in Ecclesia, qui isti orum similes sunt. Ita enim Apostolus Timotheo suo praecipit: Eos qui peccant, coram om-nibus argue, vt & reliqui timeant. Nam licet quorundam proteruia maior fit, quàm vt vinci aut emendari queat, de multis alijs spes est, quòd correptionibus istorum territi in seipsos defcen-dant, & diligentiorem in posterum habeant vitae suae rationem. Quòd si ne hoc quidem fiat, non ta-men irritus erit doctoris labor, qui hac ratione animam suam liberabit (vt olim Ezechieli dice-bat Dominus) ne ex ipsius manibus exigatur eorum sanguis, qui sua contumacia sibi ipsis exi-tium accersunt. Horum consideratio Prophetas olim excitauit, vt in effreni morum licentia non silendum sibi esse putarent, & ne a principibus quidem abstinerent, quos interdum nominatim perstrinxerunt, vt Isaiam in Sobna, Ieremiam in Iehoiakimo & alijs fecisse legimus. Nec aliam rationem praedicandi in Nouo Testamento teneri debere, Ioannis Baptistae & Apostolorum exemplis docemur, vt iam nihil dicamus de CHRISTO IESV, cuius solius authoritas nobis debet
units.tr: You will also observe at this point that Paul so plainly pricks some people, or rather points them out as with a finger, that everyone could understand whom he was speaking of. If you ask why he did this, the reason is ready to hand: namely, because their sins were not hidden but public and known to all, and indeed were joined with public scandal. Therefore in the same way, all who are like them ought to be dealt with in the Church. For so the Apostle instructs his Timothy: "Those who sin, rebuke before all, so that the rest may fear." For although the stubbornness of some becomes too great to be overcome or amended, there is hope for many others, that being frightened by the rebukes of these people they will come to themselves and take more careful account of their life in future. But if not even this happens, the labour of the teacher will not be in vain, since in this way he will free his own soul (as the Lord once said to Ezekiel), so that their blood is not required at his hands, since they bring ruin upon themselves by their obstinacy. The consideration of this once stirred up the prophets so that, in the unbridled licence of morals, they thought they must not be silent, and they did not even refrain from rebuking rulers, whom they sometimes named openly; we read that Isaiah did this with Shebna, and Jeremiah with Jehoiakim and others. Nor are we taught by the examples of John the Baptist and the apostles that any other manner of preaching should be held in the New Testament; to say nothing yet of Jesus Christ, whose authority alone ought to be enough for us

units.la: {a} Mat. 10. Luc. 9. debet sufficere. Nemini ergo hoc nouum aut insolens videri debet, si idem hodie fiat. Quàm enim hoc necessarium sit, facilè videbunt, qui nostri seculi mores & studia propius inspiciunt, quando alij omni pudore procul abiecto licenter quiduis faciunt, alij circa cultus superstitiosos occupantur, & eosdem alijs etiam obtrudere student.
units.tr: {a} Mat. 10. Luc. 9. ought to be enough. Therefore no one should think this new or unusual if the same thing is done today. How necessary it is will be readily seen by those who look closely at the morals and pursuits of our own age: some, with all shame cast aside, do whatever they please without restraint, while others are preoccupied with superstitious worship and strive to force it on others as well.

units.la: Sed & hoc non ofcitanter praetereundum est, quòd etsi Paulus de ijs potissimum loquatur, qui hactenus nulla vel admonitione vel correptione corrigi & in viam reduci potuerunt, simul tamen se reliquis etiam omnibus scribere testatur. Atqui iniquus censeri poterat, qui toti Ecclesiae quasi litem mouere voluerit propter paucos aliquos, qui lasciuius proteruiebant. Sed necesse erat simul omnes pungi, vt qui hucusque securiores aequo fuerant in ferendis apertis scandalis, de officio suo diligentius cogitare inciperent. Adhaec periculum erat, ne contagione plures alij infi‐cerentur, si securitas illa diutius duraret. Debent ergo Ecclesiarum ministri non eos modò corri‐pere, qui apertum scandalum dederunt, verumetiam de illis soliciti esse, qui nondum peccarunt. Est enim vita hominis plena periculi, & passim scandala obijciuntur, quando nunquam quiescit Satan, contra cuius insidias indesinenter excubare debent ij, quos Deus publicae salutis custodes constituit. Admonemur praeterea hoc loco, nullam iniuriam fieri Ecclesijs, si propter paucos, qui contumacius & licentiosius agunt, corripiantur. Nam etsi reliqui omnes integri ac seleris puri sint, tamen reprehensionem meretur ignauia ista, qua manifestas Ecclesiae labes ferunt, quibus alij infici possunt non sine publica Euangelicae praedicationis & Christiani nominis contumelia. Etenim qui in his ferendis aequo indulgentiores sunt, ij simul aliorum sceleribus communicant. Et sicut prodest consolationes vniuersales Ecclesijs proponi: ita correptiones quoq; vniuersales sint, vt singuli de suis vitijs, quae adhuc latent, cogitandi occasionem habeant.
units.tr: But this must not be passed over carelessly either: although Paul speaks chiefly of those who until now could not be corrected or brought back to the right way by any admonition or rebuke, he also testifies that he is writing to all the rest. Yet he might have seemed unfair if he wished to stir up a quarrel against the whole Church on account of a few who were behaving wantonly and shamelessly. But it was necessary that everyone be pricked at once, so that those who until now had been more careless than they should have been in tolerating open scandals might begin to think more carefully about their duty. Besides, there was a danger that many others would be infected by contagion if that carelessness lasted longer. Therefore the ministers of the Churches ought not only to rebuke those who have given open scandal, but also to be concerned about those who have not yet sinned. For human life is full of danger, and scandals are thrown in everywhere, since Satan never rests, and against his snares those whom God has appointed as guardians of the public welfare must keep watch without ceasing. We are also reminded here that no injury is done to the Churches if a rebuke is given on account of a few who act more stubbornly and licentiously. For even if all the rest are sound and pure in their conduct, that sloth deserves reproof by which they tolerate manifest blemishes in the Church, blemishes by which others can be infected, not without public disgrace to the preaching of the Gospel and to the Christian name. For those who are too indulgent in putting up with these things share in the sins of others at the same time. And just as it is useful for general consolations to be set before the Churches, so general rebukes too should be given, so that each person may have occasion to think about his own faults, which still lie hidden.

units.la: Caeterum ne praeter rationem verbis durioribus vti videretur Paulus, causam huius tam se‐uerae comminationis subijcit, dicens: Quandoquidem experimentū quaeritis in me loquentis Chri‐sti: Id est, quoniam me Christi causam agere non creditis, sed propter indomitam contumaciam opus habetis singulari aliquo documento, quo experiamini illum cum meo ministerio esse coniun‐ctum: Id vero illos quaerere dicit, non quòd reuera tale quid cuperent fieri, sed quòd sua incredulitate & peruicacia Christi vindicem manum contra seipsos prouocarent. Rursus ergo admonemur, ministrorum Verbi & minarum, quas illi annuntiant, contemptum in ipsum Christum redundare. Nam (vt alibi diximus) huius legati sunt, qui simul suo Spiritu & virtute in illis agit. Quod Moses obseruans, Deum ipsum ab illis tentari dicebat, qui eius mandatis audacius obganniebat. Qui enim nos sumus? inquit. Non contra nos sunt querimoniae vestrae, sed contra Dominum. Item: Cur mecum expostulatis? Cur tentatis Dominum? Et Isaiam Achaz Regi impio eiusq; improbis consiliarijs dixisse scimus: An parum est, quòd hominibus molestiam exhibetis, nisi & Deo meo molesti sitis? At parum mouent ista hodie nonnullos, quibus lusus & iocus est scurrilius sua in ministros dicteria iaculari: vt iam nihil dicatur de impijs illusoribus, qui (vt Petrus praedixit) postremum quoque Domini aduentum scurrili sua dicacitate in dubium vocare audent. Sed sen‐tient omnes illi aliquando, quid sit cum Deo ludere. Ministros autem, si quando in tales incidunt, constantia decet & intrepida animi fortitudo, vt impios illos scurras & omnis admonitionis contemptores ad Christi tribunal citent, qui abs se instituto Euangelij sui ministerio nunquam deerit, quò minus hoc à contemptu vindicet.
units.tr: Moreover, lest Paul seem to use harsher words without reason, he adds the cause of so severe a warning, saying: "Since you seek a proof of Christ speaking in me" (2 Cor. 13:3). That is, since you do not believe that I am pleading Christ's cause, but because of your untamed obstinacy you need some singular proof, by which you may experience that Christ is joined with my ministry. He says they seek this, not because they really wished such a thing to happen, but because by their unbelief and stubbornness they were provoking Christ's avenging hand against themselves. Again, then, we are reminded that contempt for the ministers of the Word, and for the threats they announce, rebounds upon Christ himself. For (as we have said elsewhere) they are his envoys, and he acts in them by his own Spirit and power. Moses, observing this, said that God himself was tested by those who rebelled too boldly against his commands: "Who are we?" he said. "Your complaints are not against us, but against the Lord" (Exod. 16:7–8). Likewise: "Why do you contend with me? Why do you tempt the Lord?" (Exod. 17:2). And we know that Isaiah said to the impious king Ahaz and his wicked counsellors: "Is it a small thing that you weary men, but will you weary my God too?" (Isa. 7:13). Yet such things move some people little today, who take pleasure in play and jokes and hurl their scurrilous insults at the ministers in a buffoonish way. Not to mention the impious mockers who (as Peter foretold) dare by their scoffing wit to call even the last coming of the Lord into doubt (2 Pet. 3:3–4). But all of them will one day feel what it is to trifle with God. As for ministers, if they ever fall into such hands, constancy and an unshaken courage of spirit become them, so that they may summon those impious jesters and all despisers of admonition to the tribunal of Christ, who, having instituted the ministry of his Gospel, will never be lacking to it, so that it is not avenged for this contempt.

units.la: At obijcere quis poterat, Paulum Christi nomine & authoritate falsò gloriari, & proinde eius comminationes nò debere magni fieri. Ad id ergo Praeoccupatione respondens, proprio exem‐plo eos confutat. Nam de Christo, cuius experimentum eos quaerere dixerat, subijcit: Qui ergà vos non est infirmus, sed potens est in vobis. Quasi diceret: Ferri poterat, si Domini nostri IESV CHRISTI virtutem nunquam experti tam insolenter contra me, qui illius legatum ago, proteruiretis. Sed si verum fateri libeat, illum diuinam suam potentiam per meum ministerium erga vos abunde declarauisse, & adhuc declarare non negabitis. Ne dubitetis ergo, quin idem in po‐sterum quoq; facturus sit. Loquitur autem de ijs, quae hactenus inter illos Christi auspicijs & virtute facta fuerant. Hic enim Paulum ad Corinthios miserat, eundem inter omnis generis pericula seruarat, per eius item ministerium in ciuitate totius orbis corruptissima Ecclesiam constituerat donis varijs & præstantissimis ornatam. Hæc certè non humanæ industriæ opera, sed divinæ virtutis documenta erant, quæ Paulum Christi seruum esse, & non priuatum negotium, sed Dei causam agere testabantur. Accedebat his exemplum in fornicatore incesto editum, quem ex eius mandato & consensu ipsi Satanæ tradiderant, & ita viderant affligi, ut Paulo intercessore opus esset, ne totus desperatione absorberetur. Erat ergo hæc nimis crassa & inexcusabilis stupiditas, qua excæcati adhuc dubitabant, an Christi seruus esset, qui huius virtute armatus ipsos castigare & punire posset.
units.tr: But someone could object that Paul falsely boasts of Christ's name and authority, and that therefore his threats ought not to be taken seriously. To meet this objection in advance, he refutes them by their own experience. For about Christ, whose proof they had said they were seeking, he adds: "who toward you is not weak, but is mighty in you" (2 Cor. 13:3). As if he said: It could be borne if you, who had never experienced the power of our Lord Jesus Christ, were so insolent against me, who am acting as his envoy. But if you are willing to tell the truth, you will not deny that he has abundantly displayed his divine power toward you through my ministry, and still displays it. Do not doubt, therefore, that he will do the same in the future also. He speaks of what had until then been done among them under Christ's auspices and by his power. For he had sent Paul to the Corinthians, had preserved him among dangers of every kind, and through his ministry had established in the most corrupt city of the whole world a Church adorned with various and outstanding gifts. These were certainly not the works of human industry but proofs of divine power, which testified that Paul was the servant of Christ, and that he was pleading not a private affair but God's cause. To these was added the example of the incestuous fornicator, whom they had, at Paul's command and with their consent, handed over to Satan himself, and had seen him so afflicted that Paul's intercession was needed, lest he be swallowed up entirely by despair. Therefore it was a very gross and inexcusable stupidity by which they, still blinded, doubted whether he was the servant of Christ, when he could, armed with Christ's power, chastise and punish them.

units.la: Vtinam vero non etiam hodie similis stupor multorum animos occupauisset: Vident omnes homines, quanta sit prædicationis Euangelicæ virtus, qua non modo superstitiones, quæ æternæ fore videbantur, sublatæ, & hominum mentes illuminatæ sunt, ut subito relictis erroribus in Veritatis via ambulent: verumetiam Pontificum regnum debellatum est, quod antea seculis aliquot toti mundo intolerabile nullis regum aut Imperatorum armis euerti potuit. Adhuc tamen de Euangelij Veritate multi non modo dubitant, sed aduersus eam conspirant quoque, & suis viribus siue armis eandem opprimi posse sibi persuadent. Potuit olim Gamaliel collegas suos mouere, ne quid temere contra nascentem fidei Christianæ doctrinam tentarent, quia sponte collapsura esset, si non alia quam hominum authoritate niteretur. Cur ergo non agnoscunt infelices illi Euangelij doctrinam ex Deo esse, cum tot iam seculis nullis Regum armis & consiliis opprimi potuerit? At quid de istis attinet dicere, quando idem stupor multos ex nostris inuasit, qui cum Euangelij professione glorientur, & ex illo noua quotidie beneficia percipiant, tamen hoc sibi impune fore arbitrantur, si eadem ipsi faciant, quæ olim Romani Pontifices & horum conniuentes fecerunt: si scilicet Ecclesiæ gubernacula quæstus priuati causa sibi vendicent, si Verbi ministris superbe dominentur, ijsdem dicendi & tacendi leges præscribant, opes Ecclesiarum & Cœnobiorum partim aperte diripiant, partim sub dispensatorum titulo iniquis & fraudulentis rationibus intercipiant, multisque alijs fame percuntibus ipsi subito diuites & potentes fiant, si denique effreni licentia in omne scelus ruendo omnes Verbi Dei admonitiones scurriliter rideant, & simul hostibus quoque deridendum propinent. Quis vero istos Corinthiorum, de quibus hic agitur, similes esse negauerit? Annon ergo illi quoque experimentum Christi quærunt per seruos suos loquentis? At profecto illud magno suo malo inuenient, quando insanum hunc stuporem illis Deus dignis pœnis excutiet.
units.tr: Would that a similar stupor had not today also seized the minds of many! All men see how great is the power of the Gospel preaching, by which not only superstitions, which seemed to be eternal, have been removed and men's minds enlightened, so that they suddenly abandon their errors and walk in the way of truth, but also the kingdom of the Pontiffs has been overthrown, which for some centuries had been intolerable to the whole world and could not be destroyed by the arms of any kings or emperors. Yet even now many not only doubt the truth of the Gospel, but also conspire against it, and persuade themselves that it can be crushed by their own strength or arms. Gamaliel once was able to move his colleagues not to attempt anything rashly against the newborn doctrine of the Christian faith, because it would fall of its own accord if it rested on no authority but that of men (Acts 5:38–39). Why then do those wretched men not acknowledge that the doctrine of the Gospel is from God, since for so many centuries it has been unable to be crushed by the arms and counsels of kings? But why speak of these men, when the same stupor has seized many of our own people, who boast of their profession of the Gospel and receive new benefits from it every day, yet think they will go unpunished if they do the very things which the Roman Pontiffs and those who tolerated them once did: namely, if they claim the government of the Church for private gain, if they lord it arrogantly over the ministers of the Word, prescribing to them laws of what to say and what to keep silent, if they openly plunder the goods of the Churches and monasteries, or partly seize them under the title of stewards by unjust and fraudulent reckonings, and while many perish of hunger they themselves suddenly become rich and powerful, and finally, rushing headlong into every crime with unbridled licence, they mock all the admonitions of God's Word with buffoonery and at the same time offer them as a laughingstock to the enemies. Who, indeed, will deny that these men are like those Corinthians of whom we are speaking here? Do they not too seek a proof of Christ speaking through his servants? But they will surely find it to their great cost, when God, by the punishments they deserve, shakes off from them this mad stupor.

units.la: Porro obstabat Pauli authoritati, quod vilis & plerisque exosus egeret, & variis diuersisque casibus hinc inde iactaretur. Pudet enim fere homines doctorum eiusmodi, & alios sibi dari vel lent, qui huius seculi gloria illustres ab omnibus obseruarentur, adeo ut ex eis ad ipsos quoque honor & commodum aliquod rediret. Quapropter huic etiam scandalo manum admouet Apostolus, & eos nimium stultos, imo iniquos esse docet, qui ipsum hoc nomine minoris faciant, cum nihil ei exprobrari vel obijci possit, quam quod ipsi cum æterno Dei Filio IESV CHRISTO sit commune. Sic enim dicit: Nam etsi crucifixus fuit ex infirmitate, viuit tamen ex potentia aut virtute Dei. Christum ex infirmitate crucifixum dicit, non quod ipse obstare nequiuerit, quo minus id fieret, (sed ut Theodoretus exposuit) propter assumptam hominis naturam infirmam & mortalem, in qua mortuus est, quia mori voluit, ut humanum genus mortis suæ merito redimeret. Ideo priusquam moreretur, dicebat: Potestatem habeo ponendi animam meam, & potestatem habeo rursus sumendi eam. Quo Paulus in præsenti respiciens, infirmitati, quam nostra causa ille assumpsit, potentiam Dei opponit, quæ in eius resurrectione sese exeruit, quando effractis mortis claustris seipsum in vitam restituit, & de hostibus suis tam carnalibus quam spiritualibus trium phum egit, quo nullum Sol hic gloriosiorem & lætiorem spectauit. Id vero exemplum Paulus sibi & reliquis Apostolis applicat dicens: Nam & nos infirmi sumus in eo, sed viuemus cum eo ex virtute Dei erga vos. Quorum verborum sensus est: Quemadmodum Christus, quoad assumptam carnem mortalem, in terris hisce infirmus & omnibus casibus humanis obnoxius vixit, tandem mortem non minus infamem quam acerbam & diram in ara Crucis subijt, idem vero in resurrectione se Deum verum & æternum, adhæc vitæ mortisque dominum esse declarauit, qui nunc in cœlis viuit & regnat: Ita nos Apostoli etiamsi plerisque infirmi, calamitosi, adeoque mortui & nulli videamur, attamen tales in Christo sumus, id est, propter Christum haec omnia patimur, & proinde eius infirmitati & cruci communicamus, cuius serui sumus & legati, qui nos virtute plus quam humana instruxit, qua & vos & omnes vestri similes, si opus fit, ita possumus coercere, ut omnibus pateat nos revera viuere. Perinde ergo Paulus hoc loco loquitur, ut princeps aliquis, qui si peregre aliis negotijs occupatus se a suis scurriliter contemni & proscindi audiat, ad illos fere in hanc sententiam literas dat: Videor vobis nunc peregrinus esse, & patrijs finibus expulsus exulare, & ideo tam licenter proteruitis. Sed sentite de me ut liber, attamen prin ceps vester sum, adhaec authoritate & viribus abunde instructus sum, ut & vos & alios hostes vlcisci possim, talemque me esse breui sentietis.
units.tr: Moreover, what stood in the way of Paul's authority was that he was humble and unimpressive in appearance, disliked by most people, and tossed about from place to place by all kinds of misfortunes. People are almost ashamed of teachers of this sort, and they would rather have others who are famous by the glory of this age and esteemed by everyone, so that honour and some advantage come back to themselves from them. So the Apostle also takes this stumbling block in hand, and teaches that those who despise him on this account are very foolish, indeed unjust, since nothing can be reproached or objected against him except that he shares a bond with the eternal Son of God, Jesus Christ. For he says: "For though he was crucified through weakness, yet he lives by the power or virtue of God." Christ is said to have been crucified through weakness, not because he was unable to prevent it (as Theodoret explained), but because of the human nature he had assumed, which was weak and mortal, and in which he died, because he willed to die, so that he might redeem the human race by the merit of his death. Therefore, before he died, he said: "I have power to lay down my life, and I have power to take it up again." Here Paul, looking to the weakness which Christ took on for our sake, sets against it the power of God, which showed itself in his resurrection, when he broke the bars of death and restored himself to life, and triumphed over his enemies, both fleshly and spiritual, so that the sun has never seen a more glorious and joyful victory. Paul applies this example to himself and the other Apostles, saying: "For we also are weak in him, but we shall live with him by the power of God toward you." The sense of these words is this: just as Christ, as to his assumed mortal flesh, lived on this earth weak and subject to all human misfortunes, and at last underwent a death no less infamous than bitter and dreadful on the altar of the cross, yet in the resurrection declared himself to be the true and eternal God and also Lord of life and death, who now lives and reigns in heaven; so we Apostles, even though we seem to most people weak, wretched, and indeed dead and of no account, nevertheless are such in Christ, that is, we suffer all these things for Christ's sake, and therefore share in his weakness and cross, whose servants and ambassadors we are, and he has equipped us with a power more than human, by which we can also restrain you and all like you, if need be, so that it is plain to all that we truly live. Paul speaks in this place much as a prince would who, when he is away on other business and hears that he is being scornfully mocked and torn to pieces by his own people, writes to them to this effect: "I seem to you now to be a stranger and to be an exile, driven from my native borders, and so you insult me so freely. But think of me as you like; nevertheless I am your prince, and I am abundantly furnished with authority and strength so that I can take vengeance on you and on other enemies, and you will soon feel that I am such a one.

units.la: Docemur autem hoc loco, neminem propter abiectam & calamitosam huius seculi conditionem siue speciem contemni, sed potius vniuscuiusque personam, quam ei Deus pro suae vocationis ratione impossuit, spectari debere. Admonet de eo Solomon, & huius admonitionis grauissimam rationem adducit, inquiens: Qui pauperem videt, probro afficit factorem eius. Adhaec in CHRISTVM IESVM contemptrix iste redundat, qui vt ipse talis propter nos factus est, ita suos sibi vult similes fieri. Cur enim potior sit serui quam heri conditio? aut cur discipulus meliori forte quam praeceptor eius vtatur? Quibus adde, quod turpissime falluntur, quicunque in sola hominis specie externa haerent: quod in Dauide & electionis eius historia Deus docuit. Cum enim Samuel huius fratrem Eliabum in Regem destinatum putaret, eo quod illum statura & corporis viribus praestantem cerneret, dixit illi Dominus: Ne respicias ad formam eius & ad procentitatem staturae eius, quoniam reprobaui hunc: non enim quod videt homo, ego respicio: Homo enim videt quod oculis obuersatur, sed Dominus intuetur cor. Et sane si plerosque ex Dei seruis inspicias, eos quoad externam magnificentiam, huius seculi filijs multo inferiores fuisse patebit. Obseruarent haec vtinam homines ambitiosi, quos fere aliorum pudet, qui ipsis minus possunt conferri. At hi sunt, quos Deus suo fauore prosequitur, qui (vt Petrus scribit) superbis resistit, humilibus vero dat gratiam. Imo hi sunt, qui Domini & Seruatoris nostri IESV CHRISTI imaginem in terris hisce gestant, & quos ille pro suis agnoscet in magno illo die, quo veniet iudicaturus vivos & mortuos: quando sempiterna ignominia multabuntur tyranni & superbi orbis terrarum dominatores, qui & illum & eius seruos vel contempserunt, vel hostiliter persecuti sunt.
units.tr: We are taught in this place that no one should be despised because of the lowly and wretched condition or appearance he has in this age, but rather that each person should be regarded for the office which God has laid upon him according to his calling. Solomon also warns of this, and gives a very weighty reason for this warning, saying: "He who mocks the poor insults his Maker." Moreover, the one who despises such people also insults Christ Jesus, who, having himself become such for our sake, wants his own to be made like him. For why should the condition of a servant be better than that of his master? Or why should a disciple perhaps fare better than his teacher? Add to this that those are most shamefully mistaken who cling only to a man's outward appearance, as God taught in the case of David and his election. When Samuel thought that Eliab, David's brother, was destined to be king because he saw that he excelled in stature and bodily strength, the Lord said to him: "Do not look on his form or on the height of his stature, for I have rejected him; for I do not regard what man sees: man looks on what is before his eyes, but the Lord looks on the heart." Indeed, if you examine most of God's servants, it will be plain that in outward splendour they were far inferior to the sons of this age. Would that ambitious men, who are almost ashamed of others who cannot be compared with them, would take note of this! But these are the ones whom God favours with his grace, who (as Peter writes) resists the proud but gives grace to the humble. Indeed, these are the ones who bear on earth the image of our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ, and whom he will acknowledge as his own on that great day when he comes to judge the living and the dead; when the tyrants and proud rulers of the world, who either despised him and his servants or persecuted them with hostility, will be punished with everlasting shame.

units.la: Debet praeterea nos confirmare huius loci consideratio, ne cui graue sit aut molestum cum Christo aut pro eius nomine contemni & reijci. Ita enim eius socij efficimur quoad crucem & afflictiones, qui nos ideo Spiritu suo dignatur, qui paracleti & aduocati partes fideliter in nobis agit: idem denique sui regni cohaeredes faciet tandem, si cum ipso in tentationibus constanter perseueremus. Eius enim promissio est: Volo, ut vbi ego sum, etiam sit minister meus. Et ad omnes pios atque credentes pertinet, quod ille in vltima Coena Apostolis dixit: Vos vos estis, qui permansistis mecum in tentationibus meis: & ego pacisco vobis, prout pactus est mihi Pater meus regnum, &c. Et sane est multa consideratione dignum exemplum, quod in illis proponitur: Fuerunt contemptissimi mortalium adeo vt Paulus eos toti mundo, Angelis item & hominibus spectaculum factos fuisse scribat. At ijdem in Christo vixerunt, imo fortes & validi fuerunt, adeo vt mundum & huius principem debellarint, & ea perfecerunt, quae nullis Regum armis siue authoritate perfici potuissent. Et ijdem nunc in coelis vitam vere beatam viuunt & regnant, in terris vero floret & ab omnibus pijs colitur eorum memoria. Idem de Martyribus reliquis dici potest, qui in ipsis tormentis se diuina virtute viuere & vincere inuita & ipsis carnificibus terribili patientia sua declarauerunt. Cuius generis exempla multa hodie videmus, quando homines obscuri inuitis & multum reluctantibus potentissimis Monarchis Christum praedicant, Ecclesias colligunt, & tandem moriendo vincunt atque triumphant. Ista singuli in priuatis calamitatibus atque periculis ad se transferant. Quid multis? Agnoscamus in his Domini & redemptoris nostri, IESV CHRISTI, potentiam, & huius fiducia confirmati constanter tueamur Veritatis & fidei causam, quam ille suo patrocinio nunquam destitui patietur. Ipsi debetur benedictio, honor, gloria & potestas in aeternum, Amen.
units.tr: Moreover, the consideration of this passage ought to strengthen us, so that no one thinks it hard or burdensome to be despised and rejected with Christ or for his name. For we thus become his companions in the cross and afflictions, and he deigns to give us his Spirit for this, who faithfully performs the part of the Paraclete and Advocate in us; and finally he will make us co-heirs of his kingdom, if we persevere constantly with him in temptations. For his promise is: "I want those who are mine, where I am, to be there with me also." And what he said to the Apostles at the last supper pertains to all the godly and believers: "You are those who have remained with me in my temptations; and I make a covenant with you, as my Father has made a covenant with me concerning the kingdom, etc." Indeed, the example set before us in these men is worthy of much consideration: they were the most despised of mortals, so much so that Paul writes that they have been made a spectacle to the whole world, to angels as well as to men. Yet these same men lived in Christ; indeed they were brave and strong, so that they overcame the world and its prince, and accomplished things which could not have been accomplished by the arms or authority of kings. And these same men now live and reign in heaven a truly blessed life, while on earth their memory flourishes and is honoured by all the godly. The same may be said of the other martyrs, who by their terrible patience, in the very torments and against the will of their executioners, showed that they lived and conquered by divine power. We see many examples of this kind today, when obscure men preach Christ, gather churches, against the wishes and great resistance of the most powerful monarchs, and at last conquer and triumph by dying. Let each one apply these things to his own private troubles and dangers. What more need be said? Let us acknowledge in these things the power of our Lord and Redeemer Jesus Christ, and, strengthened by trust in him, let us constantly defend the cause of truth and faith, which he will never allow to be deserted under his protection. To him be blessing, honour, glory and power for ever. Amen.

units.la: Vos ipsos tentate an non estis in fide, vosipsos probate: aut num non agnoscitis vosmetipsos, quod videlicet IESVS CHRISTVS in vobis est? nisi reprobi estis. At spero fore vt cognoscatis nos non esse reprobos. Opto autem a Deo, ne quid mali faciatis: non vt nos probati comperiamur, sed vt quod honestum est faciatis, nos vero velut reprobi simus. Non enim possumus quicquam aduersus veritatem, sed pro veritate. Gaudemus enim cum nos infirmi sueri-mus, vos autem validi fueritis.
units.tr: Test yourselves, whether you are in the faith; prove yourselves. Or do you not recognise in yourselves that Jesus Christ is in you? Unless indeed you are reprobate. But I hope you will come to know that we are not reprobate. Yet I pray God that you do no evil: not so that we may be found approved, but so that you may do what is honourable, even though we seem to be reprobate. For we can do nothing against the truth, but only for the truth. For we rejoice when we are weak and you are strong.

units.la: QVoniam Diuus Paulus propter vilem & ignobilem suae personae speciem & varias calamitates, quibus iactabatur, multis apud Corinthios, homines opulentos & magnificentiae affluetos, contemptui erat, & ex eo aemuli ipsius calumniandi occasionem arripiebant, ipse e contra suam authoritatem multis tuebatur. Et nuper illos ad Dominum nostrum IESVM CHRISTVM remisit, & huius exemplo de duobus illis admonuit, quae in tota hac causa imprimis considerari merebantur. Primum est, quod nihil patiatur, quam quod ipsi cum Christo commune sit, ideo illos nimium iniquos esse, qui hoc nomine ipsum contemnant. Alterum, quod sicut Christus etsi ex infirmitate assumpta crucifixus sit, viuat tamen & regnet: ita se quoque, quamuis propter Christum varie exerceatur, in eodem viuere & abunde instructum esse, vt contumacius sibi contradicentes coerceat. At quia nullis rationibus cedunt, qui Dei Verbum semel caeperunt contemnere, pergit modo, & ipsorum conscientias appellat, vt proprio testimonio convicti tandem cogantur manus dare.
units.tr: Since the divine Paul, because of the humble and unimpressive appearance of his person and the various hardships he suffered, was an object of contempt to many Corinthians, wealthy men who abounded in splendour, his rivals seized the chance to slander him, and he for his part defended his authority against many. Recently he sent them back to our Lord Jesus Christ and, by Christ's example, admonished them about two points that especially deserved consideration in the whole matter. The first is that he suffers nothing except what he shares with Christ, so those who despise him on this account are being far too unjust. The second is that just as Christ, although he was crucified through the weakness he had taken on, nevertheless lives and reigns, so Paul too, although he is variously afflicted for Christ's sake, lives in the same way and is abundantly equipped, so that he may more firmly restrain those who oppose him stubbornly. But since those who have once begun to despise the Word of God yield to no arguments, he goes on and appeals to their consciences, so that, convicted by their own testimony, they may at last be compelled to give in.

units.la: Sic enim ait: Vosipsos tentate an non estis in fide, vosipsos probate: aut num non agnoscitis vosmetipsos, quod videlicet IESVS CHRISTVS in vobis est? nisi reprobi estis. Quod perinde est ac si diceret: Nolo plura de me dicere: ad vestras conscientias & vestri cordis iudicium vos remitto. Descendite ergo in vosipsos, & animos vestros excutite, num videlicet fidei instructi. Nam si hoc feceritis, non puto tam stupidos fore, quin cogniturí sitis, Christum in vobis esse: nisi revera reprobi sitis, id est, a fide simul & Christo alieni. At nunquam puto, vos a Christo alienos esse fatebimini. Quod si vero fide donati estis, si Christum habetis in vobis manentem, dicite quaeso, unde hoc acceperitis, & per cuius ministerium? Nonne ego primus vobis Euangelium praedicaui? in fide instituí? Christo adduxi? denique Ecclesiam inter vos constitui, in qua Christus habitat & efficaciter agit? Cur ergo me Christi fratrem & germanum Apostolum esse quidam negant? cur illis infirmus & nulla Christi virtute instructus aut armatus esse dicor? Etenim huius manifesta & certa documenta in vobis ipsis inuenitis, charismatum videlicet omnis generis abundantiam, veram Dei cognitionem & singularem rerum ad salutem necessariarum scientiam. Haec si in vobis ipsis non agnoscitis, ego vos non ex Christianorum & verè fidelium numero, sed reprobos & a Christo alienos esse dixero. Ineste ergo his verbis mirifica vehementia, qua Corinthios ita stringit & vrget, vt vel ipsius ministerium probare, vel seipsos reprobos fateri cogantur. Ratio autem totius argumenti ex eo dependet, quod Corinthiorum fides in Euangelio, quod ipse illis praedicauerat, erat fundata, cum illam ex nullo alio didicissent. Nam vt fides electionis signum est, ita reprobi sint oportet, quicunque ea deflituuntur.
units.tr: For he says: "Test yourselves to see whether you are in the faith; prove yourselves. Or do you not recognise yourselves, that Jesus Christ is in you? Unless you are reprobates." This is just as if he said: "I do not want to say more about myself; I refer you to your own consciences and the judgement of your hearts. Go down into yourselves, then, and search your minds, to see whether you are indeed furnished with faith. For if you do this, I do not think you will be so stupid as not to recognise that Christ is in you, unless indeed you are reprobates, that is, aliens both from the faith and from Christ. But I never think you will confess that you are aliens from Christ. But if you have indeed been given the faith, if you have Christ dwelling in you, tell me, I beg, where you received this, and through whose ministry? Was it not I who first preached the Gospel to you? Who instructed you in the faith? Who brought you to Christ? Finally, who established among you the Church, in which Christ dwells and works effectively? Why then do some deny that I am Christ's brother and a true apostle? Why am I said to be weak and to have no power of Christ to equip or arm me? For you find clear and certain proofs of this in yourselves: namely, an abundance of gifts of every kind, true knowledge of God, and a unique understanding of the things necessary for salvation. If you do not recognise these in yourselves, I will say that you are not among the number of Christians and truly faithful, but reprobates and aliens from Christ." So in these words there is a remarkable vehemence by which he presses and urges the Corinthians so hard that they are compelled either to acknowledge his ministry or to confess themselves reprobates. The whole force of the argument rests on this: the faith of the Corinthians was founded on the Gospel that he had preached to them, since they had learned it from no other source. For just as faith is a sign of election, so whoever lacks it must be reprobate.

units.la: Est autem obseruatu dignissima relatio illa, quae est inter fidem & praedicationem. Etenim fidem ex praedicatione Verbi Dei in nobis nasci, Paulus in Epistola ad Romanos docet: nimirum ad illud Christi respiciens: Qui audit Verbum meum, & credit ei qui misit me, habet vitam aeternam. Quid enim credat is, qui nihil audit, aut cui nihil praedicatur? Id vero officij sui admonet homines Christianos, ne doctores suos temere contemnant, a quibus in fide instructi sunt. Nam id facere non possunt, nisi maior contumelia in ipsos redundet. Nam & proprio suo testimonio seipsos damnant (quod magnam leuitatem arguit) & se ex reprobatorum numero esse produnt, cum quibus Christo non possit conuenire. Potest enim illis idem dici, quod Paulus in praesenti Corinthijs thijs dicit: Num in fide & Christianus es? Unde vero hoc habes? Ex Deo vtique. Cuius autem ministerio is erga te vsus est? Quis te baptizauit? quis in externam Ecclesiam Christi societatem recepit? per quem in huius albu adscriptus es? quis te in fide instituit? quis vitae aeternae mysteria tibi annuntiauit? Annon haec omnia eius ministerio tibi obtigerunt, quem Deus tibi doctorem dedit? Neque hic mihi vitia ministrorum obijcias. Nam homines nos esse, & ijsdem cum alijs cum animi tum corporis affectionibus obnoxios esse, ipsimet fatemur. At si illa tibi in tuo doctore tantopere displicent, vt propter ea illum contemptu aut odio dignum esse iudices, cur eadem in alijs non aequè odisti? cur ijsdem, imò grauioribus laborantes, in pretio & honore habes? eos nimirum, qui non solum quoad mores peccant, verumetiam Dei Verbum cauponantur; seductores sunt; canes muti sunt, sacrilegi denique sunt, dum & Christum sui meriti gloria, & eius Ecclesiam Verbi thesauro spoliant, quo nullus nobilior, nullus pretiosior, nullus salubrior habetur? At cum istos feras, ames, colas, certè non te vitiorum, sed Verbi Dei & saniorix doctrinae hostem esse probas. Nemo tamen ista abs me ideo dici putet, quòd aliquorum petulantia aut nequitia patrocinari velim, qui reuera odio digni sunt, quando nomen IESV CHRISTI & Euangelium eius improbè prophanant ijs moribus, quos nemo vel in milite, vel in nugatore aliquo ferat, qui denique histriones, mimos, aleatores & comessatores agunt, & ita viuunt, vt non immeritò dubites, num vel Deum aliquem esse, vel coelum & inferos esse serio credant. Etenim Verbi administros decet, vt ea fide, diligentia, studio, probitate & honestate in suo munere versentur, vt auditorum conscientias appellare, & contemptores suos proprio testimonio conuincere possint. Haec enim efficacissima est suendae authoritatis ratio, si ipse effectus ministerij ipsos officio suo probè functos esse docet.
units.tr: The relation between faith and preaching is also most worthy of notice. Paul teaches in the Epistle to the Romans that faith is born in us from the preaching of the Word of God, clearly looking to Christ's saying: "He who hears my word and believes him who sent me has eternal life." For what can a man believe who hears nothing, or to whom nothing is preached? This reminds Christians not to despise rashly their teachers, by whom they have been instructed in the faith. For they cannot do so without great disgrace falling back on themselves. They both condemn themselves by their own testimony, which argues great levity, and show themselves to belong to the number of the reprobate, with whom Christ cannot agree. For the same can be said to them as Paul says to the Corinthians in the present passage: "Are you a Christian in the faith? But where did you get this? From God, surely. But through whose ministry did he deal with you? Who baptised you? Who received you into the outward fellowship of Christ's Church? By whom were you enrolled in that register? Who instructed you in the faith? Who announced to you the mysteries of eternal life? Have not all these things come to you through the ministry of the man whom God gave you as teacher? And do not object to me here the faults of ministers. For we ourselves admit that we are men, and subject to the same disorders of mind and body as others. But if those faults in your teacher displease you so much that you judge him worthy of contempt or hatred because of them, why do you not hate the same faults equally in others? Why do you hold in esteem and honour those who labour under the same or even graver faults? Namely, those who not only sin in their morals but also peddle the Word of God; who are seducers, dumb dogs, and finally sacrilegious, since they rob Christ of his glory and his Church of the treasure of the Word, than which none is nobler, none more precious, none more wholesome? But when you tolerate, love and cultivate such men, you certainly prove yourself an enemy not of vices but of the Word of God and of sound doctrine." Yet let no one think I say these things because I want to defend the wantonness or wickedness of certain men who truly deserve hatred, since they profanely dishonour the name of Jesus Christ and his Gospel by a way of life that no one would tolerate even in a soldier or a trifler: who act as stage-players, mimes, gamblers and revellers, and live in such a way that one may reasonably doubt whether they seriously believe that there is a God at all, or heaven and hell. For it is fitting that the ministers of the Word conduct themselves in their office with such faith, diligence, zeal, uprightness and honesty that they can appeal to the consciences of their hearers and convict their despisers by their own testimony. For this is the most effective way of securing authority, if the very effect of the ministry shows that they have discharged their office well.

units.la: Est praeterea alius quoque huius loci vsus. Quia enim Paulus Corinthios ad propriae fidei examen remittit, vt ita cognoscant, num fide vera Christum apprehenderint, non obscure docet, posse homines de eo certos fieri. Quomodo enim fidem suam homo ignoret, cuius tam multa tamque praeclara effecta sunt? certa nimirum in Deum fiducia, pax conscientiae, Dei dilectio, obedientia fidelis, patientia, charitas denique, quae totius vitae & actionum regula est infallibilis? Quis item tam stupidus fuerit, vt non sentiat Christum intra se agentem, cuius virtutem omnes creaturae agnoscunt, & mali quoque daemones exhorrescunt? Petrus certè cum fide cognitionem coniungit, dicens: Nos credimus & cognouimus, quòd tu es Christus ille Filius Dei viuentis. Confutatur his impium & desperationis plenum dogma Scholasticorum, qui hominem de gratia Dei & propria salute certum fieri posse negant. Enimuerò Paulus Corinthios nimium stupidos esse ait, si non intelligant Christum in ipsis agere, imò reprobos dicit, nisi huius virtutem sentiant in semetipsis. At vbi Christus adest, illic certissimum quoque est gratia Dei pignus, illic liber ad Patrem accessus, illic praesentissima salus: de quibus nemo dubitare potest, nisi Dei Patris fidem in dubium vocare velit, qui coelitus de IESV CHRISTO pronuntiauit: Hic est Filius ille meus dilectus, in quo placatus sum. Procul ergo facessant tenebriones isti, qui homines de Dei gratia dubitare docent, vt ex miserabili conscientiarum carnificina quaestum vberiorem faciant.
units.tr: There is also another use of this passage. Because Paul sends the Corinthians back to examine their own faith, so that they may know whether they have laid hold of Christ by true faith, he clearly teaches that men can be made certain of this. For how could a man be ignorant of his own faith, when it has so many and such splendid effects? Namely, a sure trust in God, peace of conscience, love of God, faithful obedience, patience, and finally charity, which is the infallible rule of the whole of life and conduct? Likewise, who would be so dull as not to feel Christ working within him, whose power all creatures acknowledge, and before whom even the evil demons tremble? Peter certainly joins knowledge to faith, saying: "We believe and know that you are that Christ, the Son of the living God." By these words the impious and despair-filled dogma of the Schoolmen is refuted, the dogma that denies a man can be made certain of the grace of God and his own salvation. Indeed Paul says the Corinthians are too stupid if they do not understand that Christ is working in them, and he calls them reprobates unless they feel his power in themselves. But where Christ is present, there is also the most certain pledge of the grace of God, there is free access to the Father, there is the most present salvation. No one can doubt these things, unless he wishes to call in question the faithfulness of God the Father, who from heaven pronounced concerning Jesus Christ: "This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased." Let those scoundrels keep far away who teach men to doubt the grace of God, so that they may make a richer profit from the wretched butchering of consciences.

units.la: At quia dixerat Paulus, Corinthios facilè intellecturos esse num in ipsis sit Christus, si quidem non sint reprobi: poterat aliquis obijcere: Ergòne reprobi erimus, nisi tibi per omnia obtempe- remus? Quid si tu sis reprobus?
