Ita enim solent homines praefracti, quales hodie multos est videre, qui cum neque Deum neque propriam salutem curent, indignissimè tamen ferunt, si quis ipsos à Christo alienos & salutis expertes esse dicat. Praeoccupat ergo obiectionem istam Apostolus, dicens: At spero fore, vt cognoscatis nos non esse reprobos. Habent autem verba ista comminationis speciem. Quasi diceret: Ne quaeso insolentius hanc meam admonitionem contemnite. Nam si positis aliquantisper affectibus vosipsos examinaueritis, facilè videbitis me nulli officio apud vos defuisse. Quòd si verò vos nihil horum moueat, & omnino pergetis pro more vestro agere, spero breui fore, vt sentiatis me non esse à Christo alienum, quando huius virtutem vindicem poenis non contemnendis erga vos declarabimus.
units.tr: But because Paul had said that the Corinthians would easily understand whether Christ is in them, if indeed they are not reprobate, someone might object: "So shall we be reprobate unless we obey you in everything? What if you yourself are reprobate?" For stubborn men of this kind, of whom there are many to be seen today, who care neither for God nor for their own salvation, take it very badly if anyone says they are alien to Christ and without salvation. The Apostle therefore anticipates this objection, saying: "But I hope that you will recognise that we are not reprobate." These words have the appearance of a threat, as if he were saying: "I beg you, do not despise my admonition too insolently. For if, having set aside your emotions for a while, you examine yourselves, you will easily see that I have been wanting in no duty towards you. But if nothing of this moves you, and you go on acting as you are accustomed to, I hope that before long you will feel that I am not alien to Christ, when we show the power of his avenging hand upon you in punishments not to be scorned."

units.la: Quo loco admonemur, Verbi administris ita agendum esse, vt quamuis aliqui non credant, multi etiam se illis contumaciter opponant, & (quod reprobi solent) in proprium exitium ruant, fit ministris in sua functione.
units.tr: Here we are reminded that the ministers of the Word must so conduct themselves in their office that, although some do not believe and many even stubbornly oppose them, and (as the reprobate usually do) rush to their own destruction, the ministers are not thereby held responsible.

units.la: Possunt homines de gratia Dei certi fieri.
units.tr: Men can be made certain of the grace of God.

units.la: Minatur proteris responsoribus.
units.tr: He threatens the stubborn opponents.

units.la: Ioan. 6. ipsi tamen se fideles Christi & Ecclesiæ ministros esse probent, & improbi illi tandem tales erga se fuisse suo malo experiantur. Id vero fiet, si neque socordes sint, neq; adulatores, qui puluillos (vt Propheta loquitur) consuant & supponant impijs, neq; etiam eorundem audaci proteruia se vinci patiantur, sed vtut res cadat, constanter Dei Verbum prædicent, moneant, increpent, hortentur, & in omnem occasionem intenti vitam quoque viuant, cuius exemplo doctrina eorum confirmetur. Ita olim Prophetas fecisse scimus, quos in præsenti Paulus quoque imitatur. Quod si hoc suo studio nihil proficiant apud aliquos, non tamen operam suam luserunt: Nam ita fidem suam liberarunt apud Deum, & eandem pijs omnibus approbarunt, alteri vero illi se ex reproborum numero esse produnt, qui vt terra maledicta & arbores steriles nulla cultura sanari possint. Quapropter nihil dicunt, qui ideo sibi tacendum & ab opere cessandum esse arbitrantur, quod apud plerosque nihil proficiant. At quod de ministris Ecclesiæ dicitur, hoc ad se quoq; transferant, qui ad Reipub. gubernacula sedent, ne ipsis imputari possit hominum improborum nequitia, qui ipsis multum reluctantibus in exitium ruunt.
units.tr: John 6. Yet they themselves may prove that they are faithful servants of Christ and of the Church, and those wicked men may at last experience to their own harm that they have been such towards them. This will indeed happen if they are neither slothful nor flatterers, who (as the Prophet says) sew cushions and place them under the ungodly, nor allow themselves to be overcome by the bold insolence of the same men; but however the matter turns out, they constantly preach, admonish, rebuke and exhort the Word of God, and, attentive to every opportunity, also live a life by whose example their teaching is confirmed. So we know the Prophets did in former times, and Paul in the present passage imitates them. But if by such zeal they accomplish nothing with some people, they have not nonetheless wasted their labour: for in this way they have freed their faith before God and approved it to all the godly, whereas those others reveal themselves to be of the number of the reprobate, who, like cursed land and barren trees, cannot be healed by any cultivation. Therefore they speak wrongly who think that they ought to keep silent and cease from their work because they accomplish nothing with most people. But what is said of the ministers of the Church, let those who sit at the helm of the commonwealth also apply to themselves, lest the wickedness of wicked men, who rush to their destruction though the rulers struggle hard against it, be imputed to them.

units.la: Porrò ne videretur rigidius cum Corinthijs agere Apostolus, idque non aliam ob causam, quàm vt suæ existimationi consuleret, dictum hoc aliquantum mitigat, dicens: Opto autem à Deo, ne quid mali faciatis, non vt nos probati comperiamur, sed vt quod honestum est faciatis, nos vero velut reprobi simus. Sensus horum verborum est, se adeò non solicitum esse de suo honore, vt contemptissimus mortalium omnium, adeoque reprobus haberi cupiat, modò ipsi nihil mali designent, cuius causa cogatur ipse sua potestate in illos seuerius uti. Et huius sui affectus teste adducit Deum, quando se hoc ab illo optare aut precari dicit. Respicit autem ad illud, quod sciebat æmulos ipsum mirificè ludibrio habituros esse, si post tam multas tamque graues comminationes nullum pænæ grauioris exemplum sequeretur. Non poterat autem ipse vanitatis accusari, nisi simul alienus à Christo, & proinde reprobus diceretur. Sed hoc (inquit) ego non moror, imò Deum precor, vt ab omni malo abstinentes faciatis ea quæ vos decent, & ita destinatas vobis pænas subterfugiatis.
units.tr: Moreover, lest the Apostle should seem to deal too harshly with the Corinthians, and this for no other reason than to look after his own reputation, he softens what he has said somewhat, saying: "Now I pray to God that you may do no evil, not that we may be found approved, but that you may do what is honourable, and that we may be as reprobate." The sense of these words is that he is so little concerned about his own honour that he desires to be held the most despised of all mortals, and so reprobate, provided that they designate no wrong for which he would be compelled to use his authority more severely against them. He calls God as witness of this feeling of his, when he says that he prays or asks this of him. But he has in view what he knew: that his rivals would wonderfully mock him if, after so many and so grave threats, no example of a heavier punishment followed. Yet he could not be accused of vanity unless at the same time he were called alien to Christ and therefore reprobate. "But this," he says, "I do not mind; rather I pray God that you may abstain from all evil and do the things that befit you, and so escape the punishments prepared for you."

units.la: Est autem multa obseruatione dignum Pauli studium, qui non solùm docuit, monuit, corripuit, verumetiam assiduis precibus apud Deum in hoc incubuit, vt Ecclesiæ florerent, & singuli ea facerent, quæ Deo probantur. Nam quod hoc loco scribit, id ipsum pro Philippensibus, Colossensibus & multis alijs eum fecisse constat. Quid quòd pro Iudæis, hostibus iuratis preces fudit dies & noctes, proque ijsdem anathema fieri voluit, vt ipsi seruarentur? Precum verò istarum haud dubiè causa hæc fuit, quòd sciret ministros neque plantando neque rigando aliquid posse, nisi Deus incrementum dederit. Quæ causa Prophetas quoque olim mouit. Imitentur hos quicunque in Verbi prædicatione Deo seruiunt. Ita enim minus superbient, simulq; accendentur, vt quod ipsis creditum est negotium ardentius agant. Debent autem hoc ad se quoque transferre qui in magistratu versantur: ne videlicet subditorum multis aut supplicijs cruentis delectentur, sed patrum instar hæc cum aperta & syncera doloris sui significatione exigant. Quid enim inhonestius, absurdius, crudelius, quàm ex ijs voluptatem capere, quæ per se mala sunt, & vt Deo improbantur, ita alijs exitium & infamiam pariunt?
units.tr: Paul's zeal is, however, worthy of much attention: he not only taught, admonished and rebuked, but also laboured at this with constant prayers to God, that the Churches might flourish and each one do those things which are pleasing to God. For that which he writes in this passage, it is certain that he did the same for the Philippians, the Colossians and many others. What of the fact that he poured out prayers day and night for the Jews, his sworn enemies, and wished himself to become accursed for their sake, that they might be saved? Certainly the cause of these prayers was that he knew ministers can accomplish nothing by planting or watering, unless God gives the increase. This same consideration moved the Prophets also in former times. Let all who serve God in the preaching of the Word imitate them. For in this way they will be less proud, and at the same time they will be kindled to pursue more ardently the business entrusted to them. Those who hold office ought also to apply this to themselves: namely, that they should not take pleasure in the many punishments or bloody executions of their subjects, but exact them as fathers do, with a clear and sincere display of their grief. For what is more dishonourable, absurd or cruel than to take delight in those things which are evil in themselves, and which are condemned by God, and which bring destruction and infamy to others?

units.la: Quid verò precatur Paulus? Primùm, ne quid mali faciant: Deinde vt faciant quod honestum est, id est, quod homines Christianos decet. Conueniunt hæc cum alijs Scripturæ locis. Apud Isaiam certè clamat Dominus: Definite male facere, discite bene facere. Et in Psalmo scribitur: Recede à malo, & fac bonum. Hic ergo scopus fit hominis Christiani. Primus ad hunc gradus est, abstinere à malo, imò ab omni etiam specie mali, vt alibi Paulus ait: Atqui malum reuera est, quicquid cum expressa Dei Opt. Max. voluntate pugnat. Falluntur ergo qui tale quid excusant exemplis, consuetudine, vetustate, aut quibuscunque alijs rationibus. Cur enim mundi exemplo se defendant ij, quos Christus è mundo hoc selegit, vt eos sibi consecraret? At quia Deus nequaquam vult seruos habere otiosos, alterum accedat necesse est, vt singuli quod honestum est, quodque ipsos decet faciant. Atqui omnes Christiani nominis professores decet, vt sanctitati studeant, Deo in spiritu & Veritate seruiant, hunc unum colant, & in dictis factisque suis omnibus glorificent. Item vt vitam viuant innocuam & charitati studeant erga omnes. Singulorum lorum vero esse, vt quisque pro suae vocationis ratione omnibus, quae ipsis debentur, officia praestet. Et huc illud Pauli pertinet: Reddite omnibus quod debetis: cui tributum debetur, tributum: cui vectigal, vectigal: cui timor, timorem: cui honor, honorem. Quod vnum si diligentius obseruarent omnes, non tantam haberent calumniandi occasionem siue materiam hostes Euangelicae doctrinae, & felicius multo propagaretur regnum IESV CHRISTI, quod passim scandalis impeditur, quae illi ipsi obijciunt, qui illius nomine prae aliis gloriantur.
units.tr: What, then, does Paul pray for? First, that they may do no evil; then that they may do what is honourable, that is, what befits Christian men. These things agree with other passages of Scripture. Indeed the Lord cries out in Isaiah: "Cease to do evil, learn to do good." And in a Psalm it is written: "Depart from evil, and do good." This, therefore, is the aim of the Christian man. The first step towards it is to abstain from evil, indeed from every appearance of evil, as Paul says elsewhere: "Whatever is truly evil is whatever conflicts with the express will of God, the best and greatest." They are therefore mistaken who excuse such things by examples, custom, antiquity or any other reasons. For why should those defend themselves by the example of the world whom Christ selected out of this world, that he might consecrate them to himself? But since God by no means wishes his servants to be idle, it is necessary that the other follows, so that each one may do what is honourable and what befits them. Now it befits all who profess the Christian name to strive for holiness, to serve God in spirit and truth, to worship him alone, and to glorify him in all their words and deeds. Likewise to live an innocent life and to strive for love towards all. It is the duty of each, moreover, that each one, according to the reason of his calling, render to all the duties that are owed to them. To this belongs the saying of Paul: "Render to all what you owe: tribute to whom tribute is owed, custom to whom custom, fear to whom fear, honour to whom honour." If all men would observe this one thing more diligently, the enemies of the Evangelical doctrine would not have so great an occasion or matter for calumny, and the kingdom of Jesus Christ would be propagated far more happily; it is everywhere hindered by scandals, which are thrown in its face by those very men who boast above others in his name.

units.la: Sed ad Paulum redeamus, qui quod dixit confirmat ratione ab officio seu ministerij sui fine desumpta, sic dicens: Non enim possumus quicquam aduersus veritatem, sed pro veritate, &c. Per veritatem procul dubio doctrinam Christi intelligit, & per consequens eos omnes, qui fidem suam atque mores secundum huius praescriptum instituunt. Itaque sensus est: Dixi me a Deo hoc flagitare, vt vos officium faciatis, licet ego tunc vanus & mendax dicar, qui vos hucusque inanibus minis perterrefacere voluerim. Nec id temere dixi. Nam etsi Christus nos Apostolos magna & formidabili potestate armauerit, nihil tamen possumus contra veritatem, neque etiam contra eos, qui secundum hanc ambulant: sed vt veritatem propugnemus atque promouebamus, potestas illa nobis data est. Quapropter si quod vos decet fecerit, non est quod vobis a me timeatis. Nam si maxime vellem meae existimationis ergo aliquid contra vos moliri, nihil tamen possem contra ingenuos veritatis cultores. At tam procul abest a me vobis nocendi voluntas, vt potius gaudium & voluptatem ex eo singularem concipiam, si hac in parte me infirmiorem, vos autem validos esse videam, in CHRISTO IESV nimirum, quoad fidem, studium veritatis, pietatem, vitam denique Christiana professione dignam.
units.tr: But let us return to Paul, who confirms what he said by a reason taken from his office or the purpose of his ministry, saying: "For we can do nothing against the truth, but for the truth," etc. By truth he undoubtedly means the doctrine of Christ, and consequently all those who order their faith and morals according to its rule. The sense therefore is: "I have said that I ask this of God, that you may do your duty, although I may then be called vain and a liar, since I have wished until now to terrify you with empty threats. Nor have I said this rashly. For although Christ has armed us Apostles with great and formidable power, we can nevertheless do nothing against the truth, nor against those who walk according to it; but that power has been given to us so that we may defend and advance the truth. Therefore, if you do what befits you, there is no reason for you to fear me. For even if I wished, for the sake of my own reputation, to undertake something against you, I could do nothing against those who are sincere lovers of the truth. But so far is the will to harm you from me, that I should rather conceive a singular joy and delight from it, if in this respect I see myself weaker and you strong, namely in Christ Jesus, in faith, zeal for the truth, piety, and finally in a life worthy of the Christian profession."

units.la: Proponitur hic rursus in Pauli exemplo generalis regula, quam omnes Ecclesiarum pastores siue ministri sequantur, quae est, vt non suae existimationi vel gloriae, sed publicae omnium saluti atque aedificationi studeant. Licet quidem illis, imo necesse est, vt sui nominis existimationem tueantur, quatenus hoc Dei gloria & ministerij sui conditio requirit. Quod Paulum hucusque fecisse vidimus, & quidem secundum Christi exemplum, qui idem saepius fecit. At hic diligenter cauere debet, ne quid insolentius fiat cum totius Ecclesiae ignominia, aut scandalo infirmorum. Nam nisi existimationem suam minister publicae saluti postponat, nihil vnquam faciet quod laudem meretur. Quis enim nescit quam multis & crebris iniurijs obnoxij sint boni pastores, quae ipsos facile vincent, nisi carnis affectus per fidei obedientiam subegerint? Tunc ergo precibus quam maxime opus est. Quod enim Paulus in praesenti pro Corinthijs fecit, hoc ipsum pro Israelitis suis Mosem & Prophetas non semel fecisse constat.
units.tr: Here, again, Paul's example sets out a general rule which all the pastors or ministers of the churches should follow: that they should aim not at their own reputation or glory, but at the salvation and edification of all. Indeed it is permitted to them, nay it is necessary, that they protect the reputation of their name, insofar as the glory of God and the condition of their ministry require it. We have seen that Paul has done this so far, and indeed following the example of Christ, who often did the same. But here he must take careful care that nothing be done too arrogantly, to the shame of the whole Church or the scandal of the weak. For unless a minister puts his own reputation after the public salvation, he will never do anything that deserves praise. For who does not know how many and how frequent the injuries are to which good pastors are exposed, which would easily overcome them, unless they subdued the desires of the flesh by obedience of faith? Then there is great need of prayers. For what Paul has done now for the Corinthians, it is established that Moses and the Prophets did the same more than once for their Israelites.

units.la: Obseruabis praeterea Verbi administros potestate quidem instructos esse, sed limitata aut certis finibus circumscripta, non autem libera siue absoluta, vt pro suo arbitrio omnia agant. Finis, qui illam totam includit, est Veritas Christi, ex qua vniuersa hominum salus dependet. Hunc transilire, aut quocunque modo excedere nefas est. Confutantur ergo huius loci authoritate, quicunque sub ministerij praetextu omnibus negotium faciunt, qui Deo secundum veritatis doctrinam seruire volunt. Illi enim aut potestatem sibi vendicant, quam non acceperunt, aut accepta male vtuntur. Quid vero aliud hodie faciunt Pontifices? Ad se transferunt Christi verba: Qui vos audit, me audit. Item: Tibi dabo claues regni caelorum: Si quis recipit quem ego misero, me recipit. Et illud Apostoli: Obedite praepositis vestris. At idem omnia faciunt contra veritatem. Nam huius doctrinam vtriusque testamenti libris comprehensam, mendacij, imo haereseos accusant: ab vnius Dei cultu atque inuocatione homines abducunt: imagines adorare atque venerari cogunt: Sacramenta venalia habent: traditionibus partim ineptis & superstitiosis, partim impijs Ecclesiam grauant: & insuper in pios Christi cultores ferro & igne crudelissime grassantur. Habent ergo illi potestatem, sed non a Deo, neque legitimam: & quia eadem vtuntur contra veritatem, iure tenebrarum potestas dicetur, cui nullam obedientiam deberi, alibi diximus. Oportet enim (vt Apostoli monuerunt) Deo magis obedire quam hominibus. Actor. 4. & 5.
units.tr: You will observe, moreover, that the ministers of the Word are indeed furnished with authority, but one that is limited, or circumscribed by certain boundaries, and not free or absolute, so that they may do everything at their own pleasure. The boundary which encloses all that authority is the truth of Christ, on which the whole salvation of men depends. To overstep this, or to exceed it in any way, is wicked. Therefore by the authority of this passage are refuted all those who, under the pretext of the ministry, make trouble for everyone who wishes to serve God according to the doctrine of truth. For they either claim for themselves an authority which they have not received, or they misuse what they have received. And what else do the Pontiffs do today? They transfer to themselves the words of Christ: "He who hears you hears me"; likewise: "I will give you the keys of the kingdom of heaven"; "Whoever receives the one whom I send receives me"; and that saying of the Apostle: "Obey your leaders." Yet they do all these things against the truth. For they accuse of falsehood, indeed of heresy, the doctrine contained in the books of both Testaments; they draw men away from the worship and invocation of the one God; they compel them to adore and venerate images; they sell the sacraments; they burden the Church with traditions, partly foolish and superstitious, partly impious; and besides, they rage most cruelly with sword and fire against the pious worshippers of Christ. They therefore have power, but not from God, nor lawful; and because they use it against the truth, it is rightly called the power of darkness, to which, as we have said elsewhere, no obedience is owed. For (as the Apostles warned) we ought to obey God rather than men. Acts 4 and 5.

units.la: Debent ista ad alios quoque hominum ordines transferri. Habent quidem potestatem non magnam modo, verumetiam sacrosanctam, iij qui in magistratu sunt constituti, quibus sua iura fiue iudicia & eorundem executionem Deus commisit. Sed huic etiam fines suos Deus praefixit, ne quid contra ius & aquum audeant facere, neue pro personarum respectu sententias varient. Tyranni enim fiunt, si iura & leges in suo arbitrio constituere putent, & (vt ille olim) dicant: Sic volo, sic iubeo, sit pro ratione voluntas. Possunt quidem isti leges torquere, multos praeter meritum multare & pro suo nutu cogere, sed & pij tunc quoque eos patienter ferre debent: attamen potestas illa non ordinaria aut legitima, & proinde ne durabilis quidem est. Idem de potestate patrum in liberos, herorum in seruos, maritorum in vxores dici potest: qui omnes nisi se intra suos fines contineant, hoc Pauli dicto notantur, & in potestatem tenebrarum degenerant. Agnoscant singuli paternam plane Dei bonitatem, qui quacunque instituit, nostro bono & publicae omnium saluti seruire vult: oremus autem benignissimum illum Patrem misericordiarum, vt quos per Filium suum IESVM CHRISTVM ex potestate diaboli & inferorum asseruit, tueatur, vt ipsi vni seruiant: cui debetur benedictio, honor, gloria & potestas in aeternum. Amen.
units.tr: These things must be applied to the other orders of men as well. Those who are placed in the magistracy have a power that is not only considerable but even sacred; to them God has committed their rights, that is, their judgments, and the execution of these. But God has also set boundaries for this power, so that they dare do nothing against right and equity, nor vary their sentences out of regard for persons. For they become tyrants if they think they may establish rights and laws at their own will, and (as that man once said) declare: "Thus I wish, thus I command; let my will stand for reason." Indeed such men can twist the laws, fine many beyond their deserts, and compel people at their nod; yet even the pious must then bear them patiently; still, that power is neither ordinary nor lawful, and therefore is not even lasting. The same can be said of the power of fathers over children, of masters over servants, of husbands over wives: all of whom, unless they keep themselves within their own limits, are marked by this saying of Paul, and degenerate into the power of darkness. Let each acknowledge the plainly fatherly goodness of God, who has ordained all things and wills them to serve our good and the common salvation of all. Let us pray, moreover, that most kind Father of mercies to protect those whom He has rescued through His Son Jesus Christ from the power of the devil and of hell, so that they may serve Him alone, to whom belong blessing, honour, glory and power for ever. Amen.

units.la: HOMILIA LXIII.
units.tr: HOMILY LXIII.

units.la: Hoc autem etiam optamus, vestram videlicet perfectionem. Propterea haec absens scribo, ne praesens seueritate vtar secundum potestatem, quam dedit mihi Dominus ad aedificationem, & non ad destructionem.
units.tr: This too we wish for you, namely your perfection. For this reason I write these things while absent, so that when I am present I may not use severity according to the authority which the Lord gave me for building up, and not for tearing down.

units.la: VT homines propter naturae suae vitiositatem facile in vitia labuntur: ita eodem in viam reuocare admodum difficile est. Nam quemadmodum qui morbis graouoribus laborant, plerunque pharmaca salubria fastidiunt propter amaritudinem, quae illis coniuncta est: sic etiam Dei Verbum, quae vnica animarum medicina est, auersari solent, qui vitiis assueuerunt, & corruptissimis suis desideriis indulgent. Intolerabile enim & iniquum illis esse videtur, quicquid cupiditatibus ipsorum & studijs prauis repugnat. Exempla eius rei passim in Scripturis sacris occurrunt, & quotidie multa in nostri seculi hominibus licet videre. Laborarunt hoc vitio etiam Corinthij. Cum enim Paulinae doctrinae immemores simul a Veritatis & fidei simplicitate atque morum sanctitate defecissent, imo licentiam iam assueuissent, correptiones illius impatientius ferebant: neque deerant, qui eum non solum nimij rigoris, verum etiam tyrannidis accusarent, quodque ex aliorum incommodis siue infamia voluptatem caperet: quod olim Prophetis quoque exprobratum fuisse scimus. Ideo sub finem huius Epistolae multis hoc agit, vt intelligant, quo animo erga ipsos sit praeditus: non hostili nimirum, sed amico & paterno, qui sui nominis exististimationem & proprium honorem saluti ipsorum longe postponat, & cupiat multis infirmior videri, modo ipsi in fide proficiant, & nouis quotidie Spiritus sancti viribus confirmentur. Id vero in praesenti amplius confirmat.
units.tr: As human beings easily fall into vices because of the corruption of their nature, so it is very difficult to call them back to the right way. For just as those who suffer from grievous diseases often reject healthful medicines because of the bitterness that goes with them, so too those who have grown accustomed to vices and indulge their most corrupt desires are wont to shrink from the Word of God, which is the only medicine of souls. For whatever opposes their appetites and their perverse pursuits seems to them intolerable and unjust. Examples of this are found everywhere in the Scriptures, and every day one may see many such things among the people of our own age. The Corinthians too were afflicted with this vice. For when they had forgotten the teaching of Paul, and had fallen away at once from the simplicity of truth and faith and from holiness of life, indeed had already grown accustomed to licence, they bore his corrections more impatiently. Nor were there lacking those who accused him not only of excessive harshness but even of tyranny, and said that he took pleasure in the discomfort or disgrace of others; we know that this was once objected to the Prophets as well. Therefore near the end of this Epistle he takes pains to make them understand what disposition he has toward them: not a hostile one, but a friendly and fatherly one, which places the esteem of his own name and his personal honour far below their salvation, and which desires to appear weaker than many, provided they make progress in faith and are strengthened daily with fresh powers of the Holy Spirit. And he confirms this more fully in what follows.

units.la: Sic enim dicit: Hoc autem etiam optamus, vestram videlicet perfectionem. Dixerat se ipsorum incolumitate gaudere, neque sibi graue videri, si sibi aliquid decedat ex sua exististimatione, modo ipsi sint validi. Nunc plus quiddam addit. Non modo gaudemus (inquit) vestra salute & incolumitate, verumetiam assiduis votis atq; precibus hoc vobis a Deo impetrare satagimus, vt vobis ad plenam perfectionem peruenire liceat. In Graeco habetur, quae vox proprie iustam & concinnam corporis atq; membrorum constitutionem significat, vel potius eorum quae loco mota aut lacerata sunt restitutionem. Probe autem haec Metaphora atque votum illud Corinthijs conueniebat. Nam qui in CHRISTO IESV vnum corpus esse debebant, variis atq; diuersis modis erant distracti. Etenim doctores reliqua Euangelicae doctrinae simplicitate circa inutiles & superuacaneas speculationes occupabantur, & in his ambitiose nimis suam eruditionem siue ingenij acumen & eloquentiam ostentabant. Hinc sectae exortae fuerant, vt factiosis nominibus inter se sciscitari essent, qui vnum Christum vno ore & corde debebant profiteri. Multi cum idololatris colludentes eorundem sacris communicabant. Alij lites forenses sectabantur, & vilis pecuniae causa fratres suos ad prophanorum hominum tribunalia non sine fidei Christianae contumelia trahebant. Plerique ad veterem morum licentiam relapsi vagis libidinibus indulgebant, adeo ut ne ab incestibus omnino essent immunes. Erat denique Ecclesiae istius facies omnino distorta & corporis luxati instar, in quo nullum membrum suo loco est, aut suum facit officium. Recte ergo illius instaurationem sive restitutionem optat Apostolus, ex qua possint pro vera Christi Ecclesia agnosci.
units.tr: For he says: "This we also wish, namely your perfection." He had said that he rejoiced in their safety and soundness, and that it seemed no burden to him if something was lost from his own reputation, provided they themselves were strong. Now he adds something more. "Not only do we rejoice," he says, "in your salvation and soundness, but we also labour by constant vows and prayers to obtain from God for you that you may be permitted to come to full perfection." In the Greek it is [καταρτισμός], a word which properly signifies the right and well-fitted constitution of the body and its members, or rather the restoration of things that have been dislocated or torn. This metaphor and this wish were most fitting for the Corinthians. For those who ought to be one body in Christ Jesus had been torn apart in various and diverse ways. For teachers, leaving aside the simplicity of the gospel teaching, were occupied with useless and superfluous speculations, and in these they too ambitiously displayed their learning, their keenness of wit and their eloquence. From this, sects had arisen, so that they were quarrelling among themselves under factious names, when they ought to have confessed one Christ with one mouth and one heart. Many, colluding with idolaters, took part in their sacred rites. Others pursued lawsuits and, for the sake of paltry money, dragged their brothers before the courts of profane men, not without dishonour to the Christian faith. Many, having relapsed into their old licence of life, indulged in wandering lusts, to such an extent that they were not wholly free even from incest. In short, the face of that Church was altogether distorted, like a dislocated body in which no member is in its place or performs its office. Rightly, therefore, the Apostle wishes for its restoration or re-establishment, by which it might be recognised as the true Church of Christ.

units.la: Debet autem hic finis omnibus Ecclesiae ministris propositus esse, ut nimirum totius Ecclesiae simul atque singulorum membrorum eius integritatem atque perfectionem pro viribus tueantur, aut collapsam instaurent. Vbi ante omnia est opus, ut omnes unum sint in IESV CHRISTO, neque diversis opinionibus & doctrinis scindantur. Nam nisi hoc observetur, iam ne Ecclesia quidem dici merebitur. Ea enim in Symbolo Catholica, id est, universalis omnium sanctorum communio esse definitur. At quomodo universalis Ecclesiae membra esse, aut cum aliis sanctis communionem habere dicentur, qui inter se scissi diversa dogmata profitentur, & factiones apertas fovent? Non temere ergo Christus iam mortem aditurus tam serio precatus est, ut qui ipsius discipuli sunt, unum sint in ipso, quemadmodum ipse in Patre, & Pater in illo est. Deinde ut charitatis quoque vinculo inter se connexi sint Christiani homines necesse est, & alii aliorum commodis atque incommodis serio afficiantur, seque mutuo iuvent, quemadmodum nostri corporis membra facere alibi audiuimus. Hic tertium accedat oportet, ut singuli pro suae vocationis ratione officium faciant, & a Deo sibi creditam stationem constanter tueantur. Ministri ergo fideliter excubent pro publica salute, doceant, moneant, hortentur, arguant, increpent, consolentur, & simul doctrinam proprio exemplo confirment. Qui in magistratu sunt, Dei cultum provehant atque tueantur, sanctè ius dicant, defendant bonos, puniant malos, honestatem & pacem publicam conservare pro viribus studeant. Reliqui vero cuiuscunque loci aut ordinis, parentes, coniuges, liberi, servi, opifices, ea diligenter & bona fide faciant, ad quae destinati sunt, nec temere alii aliorum partes invadant, quae praecipua confusionis causa est. Ideo Apostoli frequenter in suis epistolis de omnium ordinum officiis differunt, & quae illi dederunt praecepta, hodie omnes Ecclesiarum ministri apud suos indesinenter urgere debent. Ita enim ministerium suum approbabunt Deo, qui labores eorum dignis praemiis remunerabitur.
units.tr: This end ought to be set before all ministers of the Church, namely that they should, as far as their strength allows, guard the integrity and perfection of the whole Church and of each of its members, or restore it when it has fallen. Here above all there is need that all be one in Jesus Christ, and that they not be split apart by divergent opinions and doctrines. For unless this is observed, the Church will no longer even deserve to be called such. For in the Creed it is defined as the Catholic, that is, the universal communion of all saints. But how can those be said to be members of the universal Church, or to have fellowship with other saints, who are divided among themselves, profess differing dogmas, and foster open factions? Not without reason, therefore, did Christ, about to go to death, pray so earnestly that those who are his disciples might be one in him, just as he is in the Father and the Father in him. Next, it is necessary that Christian people also be bound together by the bond of charity, and that they be seriously affected by one another's advantages and disadvantages, and help one another, just as we have heard elsewhere that the members of our body do. Here a third thing ought to be added: that each person, according to the nature of his calling, perform his duty and steadfastly keep the station entrusted to him by God. Let ministers therefore keep faithful watch for the public welfare, teach, admonish, exhort, reprove, rebuke, console, and at the same time confirm the teaching by their own example. Let those who are in the magistracy advance and protect the worship of God, judge justly, defend the good, punish the wicked, and strive as far as they can to preserve honesty and public peace. As for the rest, of whatever place or rank—parents, spouses, children, servants, workmen—let them diligently and in good faith do those things for which they are destined, and let them not rashly invade one another's parts, which is the chief cause of confusion. Therefore the Apostles often treat in their epistles of the duties of every order, and the precepts they gave ought today to be urged unceasingly by all ministers of the Churches among their own people. For in this way they will approve their ministry before God, who will reward their labours with worthy prizes.

units.la: At si haec ad nostri seculi mores atque studia transferas, horribilem omnium ordinum confusionem videbis. Nam qui populum sana & simplici Veritatis Euangelicae doctrina ad pietatem veram instituere, Ecclesiam aedificare, concordiam mutuam fovere, poenitentiam & publicam morum honestatem tradere & suo exemplo reliquis praeire debebant: hi fere ambitione & contendendi libidine abrepti circa disputationes non inutiles modo, verumetiam noxias occupantur, veteres haereses postliminio revocant, populum in partes distrahunt, ministerij sui collegas & conservos ignominiosis conuitijs flagellant, in corripiendis autem publicis scelaribus canes muti sunt, ad illa conniuent, nisi quando de ipsorum existimatione agitur, adhaec exemplo proprio multos corrumpunt, ut de doctrinae Veritate dubitare incipiant, denique sal sunt infatuatus, quem ne flerquilibet quidem dignum esse Christus testatur. At principes viri vel religionem nihil ad se pertinere putant, & proinde eam omnino negligunt, vel illam suo imperio subjiciunt, & tam huic quam eius administris dominantur, quasi in ipsorum arbitrio sit, huius formam constituere, sicut olim Jeroboamus fecit, primus Rex Israelitarum. Quod si ad privatos homines transeas, paucissimi officium faciunt. Inter coniuges rixae & contentiones sunt: parentes ex se natos vel securi negligunt, vel artibus malis instituunt, in hoc unum intenti, ut opes corradant, & illis patrimonium relinquant, quod eis possit sufficere: e contra liberi parentes contemnunt, & disciplinam omnem oderunt. Heri duro imperio servos premunt, & plerique aliorum laboribus gratuitis abutuntur: hi vero vicissim non bona fide heris suis serviunt. Taceo nunc factiones, quibus totus fere orbis terrarum scinditur. Amos Propheta olim quasi ad spectaculum vocabat vicinas Israelitas gentes: Congregamini super montes Samariae, & spectate tumultus magnos in medio eius. At quanto iustius hoc de ijs dici poterat hodie, qui Christiani haberi volunt, & tamen caecis affectibus abrepti publicè & privatim tumultuantur absque omni ordine, tam in ijs quae ad religionem spectant, quam in politicis & privatis uniuscuiusque negotijs? Et haec quidem deplorare possumus, eadem vero emendare nemo poterit, nisi bonus ille medicus, IESVS CHRISTVS, afflictissimo suo corpori manu adhibeat.
units.tr: But if you transfer these things to the manners and pursuits of our own age, you will see a dreadful confusion in every order. For those who ought to instruct the people in true piety by the sound and simple teaching of the gospel truth, to build up the Church, to foster mutual concord, to deliver repentance and public honesty of life, and to go before the rest by their own example, these, for the most part carried away by ambition and a lust for contention, are occupied with disputations that are not only useless but even harmful; they recall old heresies from exile, tear the people into factions, lash their colleagues and fellow servants of the ministry with disgraceful insults; yet in rebuking public crimes they are dumb dogs, and they wink at them, unless their own reputation is at stake. Besides, by their own example they corrupt many, so that these begin to doubt the truth of doctrine; in short they have become salt that has lost its savour, which Christ testifies is not fit even for the dunghill. And princes either think religion has nothing to do with them and therefore neglect it altogether, or they subject it to their own rule and lord it over both it and its ministers, as if it were in their power to set its form, as Jeroboam, the first king of the Israelites, once did. But if you pass to private persons, very few perform their duty. Among spouses there are quarrels and contentions; parents either carelessly neglect the children born of them or train them by evil arts, intent on this alone, that they may amass wealth and leave them an inheritance sufficient for them; on the other hand, children despise their parents and hate all discipline. Masters oppress their servants with harsh rule, and many abuse the free labour of others; these in turn do not serve their masters in good faith. I say nothing now of the factions by which almost the whole world is split. Long ago the prophet Amos called the neighbouring nations of Israel, as to a spectacle: "Gather yourselves upon the mountains of Samaria, and behold the great tumults in the midst of it." But how much more justly could this be said today of those who wish to be called Christians, and yet, carried away by blind passions, make tumult publicly and privately without any order, both in matters that concern religion and in the political and private affairs of each one? These things we may lament, but no one will be able to correct them, unless that good physician, Jesus Christ, lays his hand upon his most afflicted body.

units.la: Scopus quis debeat ministris propositus esse.
units.tr: What goal ought to be set before ministers.

units.la: Nostri seculi confusio. ferri debere admonitiones & correptiones, imo illis gaudere debere Christianos homines, cum hic Deus (vt modo diximus) suum erga nos fauorem testetur, & eadem nobis ad salutem adiumento sint. Nam vt amariora pharmaca noxios humores expellunt, sectiones item atque vstiones membris putridis & contabescentibus medentur: ita prudens atque seuera correptio eos in viam salutis reuocat, qui nisi illa adhiberetur, in sua licentia perirent. Qui vero illis exacerbantur, & contra fidos monitores contumaciter insurgunt, ij sibijpsis pessime consulunt, vt in Achabi & similium exemplis esse videre.
units.tr: The confusion of our age. Admonitions and rebukes ought to be welcomed, and indeed Christians ought to rejoice in them, since here God (as we have just said) bears witness to his favour towards us, and these things serve us for our salvation. For just as bitter medicines expel harmful humours, and cutting and burning heal decayed and rotting limbs, so wise and severe correction calls back to the way of salvation those who, unless it were applied, would perish in their own licence. Those, however, who are exasperated by it and stubbornly rise up against faithful monitors, do the worst possible harm to themselves, as we can see in the examples of Ahab and others like him.

units.la: Secundo, Perficiamini, inquit. In Graeco legitur, καταρτίζεσθε, quod ad perfectionem illam refertur, quam supra καταρτισμου dixit, Metaphora ab humani corporis constitutione desumpta. Vule ergo nunc, vt singuli operas suas ad Ecclesiae instaurationem conferant, vt tandem sublatis e medio sectis & dissidijs omnique confusione, vnu sint in CHRISTO IESV, & huc in integritate fidei morumque puritate seruiant. Arguit hoc eos, qui quod vitam priuatam degunt, res Ecclesiae, adeoque totam religionis causam nihil ad se pertinere arbitrantur: quod perinde est ac si manus salutem corporis nihil ad se pertinere diceret, quia ipsa non sit caput. Interim praeceptum hoc singuli priuatim sibijpsis applicent. Nam ab omnibus, qui cultores sui esse volunt, perfectionem Deus requirit, & generale est mandatum, quod Abrahamo dictum fuit: Ambula coram me, & esto perfectus siue integer. Cui consentit quod in Lege toties inculcatur: Sancti estote, quia ego Sanctus sum, Dominus Deus vester. Et Christus in Euangelio ait: Estote perfecti, quemadmodum Pater vester, qui in caelis, perfectus est. Quid, quod idem seipsum in exemplum nobis proponit, ex quo vitae totius simul & fidei nostrae regula petamus? Recte ergo perfectionem hanc Apostoli quoque passim ab hominibus Christianis exigunt. At quam diu in hac carne mortali viuimus, ad perfectionis istius metam non possumus peruenire, & in multis indies deficimus. Semper ergo nos anniti oportet, vt reliquis ijs quae a tergo sunt, indesinenter proficiamus, vt alibi suo exemplo Paulus docet. Arguit ergo hoc praeceptum ignauos atque desides, qui quasi ipsis nihil omnino reliquet agendum sibijpsis in suo otio placent. Sunt hi fere similes iuuenis illius opulenti, qui apud Christum gloriabatur, quod Legem totam a pueris obseruauissęt, mox autem tristis abijt, quando illum Christus charitatis praecepto propius cepit vrgere. Ita isti se quidem omnia praestitisse putant, at si in seipsos paulo altius descenderent, multo plura adhuc sibi deesse sentirent, quam adhuc praestiterint.
units.tr: Secondly, he says, "Be perfected." In the Greek it reads καταρτίζεσθε [katartizesthe], which refers to that perfection which he called καταρτισμός [katartismos] above, a metaphor taken from the constitution of the human body. He wills, therefore, that now each one should bring his efforts to the restoration of the Church, so that at last, with divisions and schisms and all confusion removed, they may be one in Christ Jesus and serve him here in the integrity of faith and purity of morals. This rebukes those who, because they live a private life, think that the affairs of the Church, and therefore the whole cause of religion, have nothing to do with them. This is just as if the hand were to say that the health of the body has nothing to do with it, because it is not the head. Meanwhile, let each one apply this precept to himself privately. For God requires perfection from all who wish to be his worshippers, and the command given to Abraham is a general one: "Walk before me, and be perfect" or "upright." With this agrees what is so often impressed upon us in the Law: "Be holy, for I am holy, the Lord your God." And Christ says in the Gospel: "Be perfect, as your Father in heaven is perfect." Moreover, does he not set himself before us as an example, from which we may seek the rule both of our whole life and of our faith? Rightly, therefore, the Apostles also everywhere require this perfection from Christian men. But as long as we live in this mortal flesh, we cannot attain the goal of that perfection, and daily we fall short in many things. We ought always, then, to strive to make continual progress, "forgetting those things which are behind," as Paul teaches elsewhere by his own example. This precept therefore rebukes the idle and the lazy, who, as if there were nothing at all left for them to do, are pleased with their own ease. Such people are much like that rich young man who boasted before Christ that he had kept the whole Law from his boyhood, but went away sad as soon as Christ began to press him more closely with the command of love. So these people think they have done everything; but if they went down a little deeper into themselves, they would feel that far more is still lacking to them than what they have so far accomplished.

units.la: Tertio loco ait Paulus: Consolationem habete. In Graeco ponitur verbum παρακαλεῖσθε, quod tam de adhortatione quam consolatione mutua potest intelligi, & vtrumque Corinthijs conueniebat, vel potius necessarium erat: vt nimirum se mutuo hortarentur ad faciendum fiocium, & alij alios mutuis consolationibus confirmarent. Et hodie adhuc vtrumque inter homines Christianos sedulo fieri debet. Etsi enim vias Domini semel ingressi fimus, multa tamen nos remorantur, multa nos remissiores faciunt, multa ab opere Domini reuocant. Opus igitur nobis est stimulo, quae etsi Deus per Verbum suum nobis adhibeat, efficacissima tamen sunt quotidiana eorum, qui nobiscum versantur, admonitiones atque correptiones. Et has nobis in Lege commendat Dominus, quando vt proximi, imo inimici quoque, bonum errantem ad ipsum reducamus, & eiusdem asinum, si oneri imposito succubuerit, subleuemus praecipit. Similiter quia vita haec laborum & periculorum plena est, frequenti etiam consolatione opus habemus. Suggerit hanc quidem efficacissime fidelis ille paracletus, Spiritus Sanctus, quem nobis Christus consolatorem & consultorem siue aduocatum destinauit: sed idem organis vtitur, Verbi ministris & multis alijs, qui hoc officium exeunt suggestione nobis praestant. Huic ergo singuli sese pro suae vocationis ratione & dilectionis Christianae officio sese accommodent. Ita enim opus illud misericordiae facient, quod suis rationibus adscribet Dei Filius, quando in magno illo die electis suis dicet: Inualidus fui, & visitastis me: in custodia fui, & veniistis ad me. At quae nostri saeculi calamitas est, hodie in utroque plurimum peccatur. Nam multi quidem sunt, qui ad scelera per se plus satis proclives excitant, aut ad superstitiones atque illicitos cultus rerum imperitos magnificis promissis exhortantur: imo inueniuntur passim qui quosuis improbe vrgent, & tantumnon cogunt, vt perpotent, helluentur, ludant, alijsque buius saeculi studijs sese mancipent. At qui ad pietatem, temperantiam, sobrietatem, innocentiam & alias virtutes adhortentur, perpauci sunt. Quid, quod qui recta in praecipitium perditionis ruunt unt, àplerisque negliguntur, & sæpe ab ijs quoque, qui ex officio diuinitus sibi impositò debebant pro publica salute excubare? Quibus adde, quòd afflictos, peregrinos & egenos quoque pauci suis consolationibus & ope subleuant, plerique autem, dummodo ipsis bene sit, aliorum calamitates spectare possunt.
units.tr: Thirdly, Paul says: "Have comfort." In the Greek the word is παρακαλεῖσθε [parakaleisthe], which may be understood both of mutual exhortation and of mutual consolation. Both were fitting for the Corinthians, or rather both were necessary, namely that they might exhort one another to do their duty, and that one might strengthen another with mutual comforts. And even today both ought to be diligently practised among Christian people. For although we have once entered upon the ways of the Lord, many things still hold us back, many things make us more slack, many things call us away from the work of the Lord. We therefore need a spur. Although God applies this to us through his Word, the daily admonitions and rebukes of those who live with us are nonetheless most effective. The Lord commends these to us in the Law, when he commands us, as neighbours, and even as enemies, to bring back to him a good man who has gone astray, and to help his ass if it has collapsed under its load. Likewise, since this life is full of labours and dangers, we also have constant need of consolation. That faithful Paraclete, the Holy Spirit, whom Christ appointed for us as comforter and counsellor or advocate, certainly furnishes this most effectively; but he also uses instruments, the ministers of the Word and many others who discharge this office, to provide it for us by their encouragement. Let each one, therefore, accommodate himself to this according to the nature of his calling and the duty of Christian love. For thus they will do that work of mercy which the Son of God will count to their credit, when on that great day he says to his elect: "I was sick, and you visited me; I was in prison, and you came to me." But what a calamity of our age it is that today people sin very much in both respects! For there are many who stir up men who are already quite prone to wickedness, or who with grand promises urge the ignorant towards superstitions and unlawful forms of worship. Indeed, everywhere are found those who shamelessly press upon whoever they can, and almost compel them to drink heavily, to gorge, to gamble, and to devote themselves to the pursuits of this world. But those who exhort to piety, temperance, sobriety, innocence and the other virtues are very few. And what of those who are rushing headlong into the precipice of destruction? They are neglected by most, and often even by those who ought, by the office divinely laid upon them, to keep watch for the public welfare. To these add that few relieve the afflicted, strangers and the needy with their consolations and help, while most, provided that things go well for themselves, are able to look on at the calamities of others.

units.la: Quartum huius loci membrum est: Idem sentire, vel Vnanimes esse. Potest hoc primò de doctrina & fide intelligi, ne diuersis dogmatibus aut opinionibus scindantur: Deinde, vt quoad charitatem mutuam vna omnium mens sit, & mutuo concordiæ studio ardeant. Vtrumque in prioris epistolæ Cap. primo vna sententia comprehendit, sic dicens: Precor vos, fratres, per nomen Domini nostri IESV CHRISTI, vt idem loquamini omnes, & non sint inter vos diuisidia, sed sitis coagmentati, aut concinnè perfecti, eadem mente & sententia. Et ad Philippenses hoc ipsum diligentius explicans, scribit: Sitis itidem affecti, eandem charitatem habentes, vnanimes, & sententijs vni: nihil per contentionem fiat, aut per inanem gloriam, sed ex modestia alium quisque se præstantiorem putet. Ne sua quisque spectetis, sed quæ sunt aliorum, etc. Vide locū Philip. secundo Cap.
units.tr: The fourth part of this passage is: "Think the same thing," or "Be of one mind." This may be understood first of doctrine and faith, that they should not be split by different dogmas or opinions; then, that as regards mutual love there should be one mind among all, and that they should burn with a shared zeal for concord. In the first chapter of his earlier letter he sums up both in one sentence, saying: "I beseech you, brothers, through the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that you all speak the same thing, and that there be no divisions among you, but that you be joined together, or perfectly united, in the same mind and the same judgement." And explaining the same thing more carefully in his letter to the Philippians, he writes: "Be likewise disposed, having the same love, being of one accord and of one mind; let nothing be done through contention or vainglory, but in humility let each esteem the other better than himself. Let each of you look not only on his own things, but also on the things of others," and so on. See the passage in Philippians, chapter two.

units.la: Et huc facit, quòd hic quintum adijcitur: In pace agite, vel pacem inter vos colite. Id vero proprie charitatem & benevolentiam mutuam commendat. Sunt enim, qui quoad dogmata fidei & religionis idem sentiunt, at interea alias ob causas diffident, & sæpe propter res leuiculas tumultuantur. Iubet ergo vt fidei & religionis consensum externis quoque factis, & imprimis publicæ aut communis pacis studio testentur. Istis vero omnibus rationis & stimuli loco promissionem magnificam adijcit: Et Deus charitatis & pacis erit vobiscum. Ita vero dicitur Deus, quia vt ipse charitas est (teste Ioanne Apostolo) ita hominum charitate & pace gaudet, atque earundem author est. Quia enim homo natura φιλαυτος, id est, suiipsius amans est, fraternam dilectionem facile negligimus, ex quo deinde apertæ dissensiones & dissidia nascuntur, At Deus suo Spiritu animos mutare & charitatis ignem in nobis accendere potest. Hunc qui admittunt, ij postea indies in vera pietate proficiunt, & Deo propitio vtuntur, qui donafua in ipsis auget, & eosdem tuetur atque gubernat. Docet hoc eleganter Dauid, qui de fraternis piorum consensione & concordia loquens, inter alia ait: Dominus mandauit, vt illic sit benedictio & vita sempiterna. Ex quo contrarium colligi potest, eos nimirum, qui odijs, simultatibus, dissidijs, rixis & contentionibus vacant, diabolum sibi præsentem habere, qui iam inde ab initio homicida fuit, & hominum exitio gaudet.
units.tr: To this also belongs the fifth point added here: "Live in peace," or "Cultivate peace among yourselves." This properly commends mutual love and goodwill. For there are some who agree in doctrines of faith and religion, and yet for other reasons are at odds with one another, and often make an uproar over trifling matters. He therefore bids them to attest their agreement in faith and religion also by outward deeds, and above all by the pursuit of public or common peace. To all these, in place of reason and spur, he adds a magnificent promise: "And the God of love and peace will be with you." God is called this because, as he himself is love (as the Apostle John witnesses), so he delights in love and peace among men, and is their author. For since man is by nature φίλαυτος [philautos], that is, a lover of himself, we easily neglect brotherly love, from which open dissensions and divisions then arise. But God by his Spirit can change minds and kindle the fire of love in us. Those who admit this make progress day by day in true godliness, and enjoy the favour of God, who increases his gifts in them and keeps and governs them. David teaches this admirably, speaking of the brotherly agreement and concord of the godly, and among other things he says: "The Lord has commanded that there be blessing and eternal life there." From this the opposite may be inferred: that those who are given over to hatreds, rivalries, divisions, quarrels and contentions have the devil present with them, who has been a murderer from the beginning and delights in the destruction of men.

units.la: Docet ego prima huius loci pars, quid de nostri sæculi moribus atque statu iudices. Mirantur multi calamitates continuas, quibus totus orbis terrarum affligitur, imprimis autem ij, qui Christianum nomen profitentur. Sed quid mirari ista opus est? Deus charitatis & pacis Deus est, neque alijs quàm pacis & charitatis cultoribus delectatur, & his solis sese propitium præbet. Notum est enim illud Christi, qui cùm charitatis præceptum suis vnicè commendaret, inter alia dixit: Qui tenet præcepta mea, & seruat ea, is ille est qui diligit me: qui autem diligit me, diligetur à Patre meo, & ego diligam eum, & me ei conspicuum exhibebo. Et rursum: Si quis diligit me, sermonem meum seruabit: & Pater meus diliget eum, & ad eum veniemus, & mansionem apud eum faciemus. At Christi dilectionem non alio euidentiori argumento possumus declarare, quàm cùm eius membra syncero amore complectimur. Quàm pauci verò hodie sunt, qui hoc præstent? Regnant vbique superstitiones, quæ eos etiam diuellunt, qui prius coniunctissimi erant. Accedit his auaritia, quæ omnes charitatis leges violat, & insuper fraudis, impostura, vsurarum, furtorum & omnis iniquitatis fecundissima mater est: ex quibus odia & inimicitiæ passim pullulant. Alios ambitio in fratres armat, quæ inuidiam & æmulationem parit, qua fit, vt perditos velint eos, quos debebant amare. Et hæc quidem vulgò fiunt. Quod si Ecclesiarum ministros inspicias, inter hos quoque rarum esse videbis charitatis & pacis studium. Nam multi horum ambitionis æstro & contendendi libidine accensi pro rebus non magni momenti altercantur, Ecclesias in partes distrahunt, & vt noui quidam Pontifices anathematismis & excommunicatione pugnant, aliique alios diris devouent. Quis ergo Deum suo Spiritu talibus præsentem adesse dixerit? aut quis istos maligno spiritu agitari neget? At vbi iste dominatur, ibi nihil sanum, nihil laetum aut iucundum sperari potest. Itaque procul relictis istis moribus, Apostolicæ huic admonitioni sese accommodent, qui Reipub. & Ecclesiæ hodie multum consultum esse volunt.
units.tr: The first part of this passage shows you what to make of the morals and condition of our own age. Many people are amazed at the constant calamities that afflict the whole world, and especially those who profess the Christian name. But why should we be amazed at these things? God is the God of love and peace. He takes pleasure in no one but the cultivators of peace and love, and he shows himself favourable to them alone. Christ's saying is well known. When he especially commended the command of love to his own, he said among other things: "Whoever has my commandments and keeps them, he is the one who loves me. And whoever loves me will be loved by my Father, and I will love him and reveal myself to him." And again: "If anyone loves me, he will keep my word, and my Father will love him, and we will come to him and make our home with him." But we cannot show our love for Christ by any clearer proof than by embracing his members with sincere affection. How few, though, are there today who do this? Superstitions reign everywhere, and they tear apart even those who were once most closely joined. To these is added avarice, which violates all the laws of love and is the most fruitful mother of fraud, imposture, usury, theft and every kind of wickedness. From these, hatreds and enmities spring up everywhere. Ambition arms others against their brothers, and it gives birth to envy and rivalry, so that people wish ruin on those whom they ought to love. These things happen commonly enough. But if you look at the ministers of the churches, you will see that among them too the pursuit of love and peace is rare. For many of them, inflamed by the goad of ambition and the lust for contention, quarrel over matters of little importance, tear churches into factions, and, like certain new popes, fight with anathemas and excommunication, while others curse one another with dreadful imprecations. Who, then, would say that God is present among such people by his Spirit? Or who would deny that these men are driven by an evil spirit? Where that spirit rules, nothing sound, nothing joyful or pleasant can be hoped for. Therefore, let those who wish well to the commonwealth and to the Church today put such habits far away and accommodate themselves to this apostolic admonition.

units.la: Sequitur secunda Epilogi pars, quæ salutationes habet, quas pro more Apostolus adscribit. Præcipuum in his est, quòd ut se mutuò salutent præcipit. Nam credibile est, propter sectas, simultates & dissidia multorum animos ita distractos fuisse, ut ne alloquio quidem mutuo alij alios dignarentur. Prudenter ergo & recte iubet, ut positis simultatibus atque odijs, ad mutuam benevolentiam se excitent. Et quia Orientales populi (ut alias diximus) inter salutandum osculo uti solebant, quod charitatis symbolum erat, imò reverentiæ quoque & observantiæ: mos iste ad Græcas quoque Ecclesias transijt, & ideo huius in præsenti Corinthios admonet. Sanctum verò osculum dicit, ut simulationem omnem excludat, quæ ut in omni alia re turpis, ita in amicitijs turpissima simul & nocentissima est. Deinde fratrum, qui secum erant, nomine illis salutem dicit, ut quemadmodum ipsos inter se conciliare studet, ita eos exteris quoque obstringat. Nec enim obstat loci distantia, quo minus se mutuum amare debeant, quos unitas fidei coniunxit, ut in CHRISTO IESV corpus unum sint. Perstringimus hæc breviter, quia in prioris epistolæ fine diximus, quæ hic dici poterant.
units.tr: The second part of the Epilogue follows, which contains the greetings that the Apostle, as is his custom, adds. The chief point in these is that he instructs them to greet one another. For it is credible that, because of sects, quarrels and dissensions, the minds of many were so divided that they did not even deign to speak to one another. Wisely and rightly, then, he bids them, with rivalries and hatreds laid aside, to stir themselves up to mutual goodwill. And because the peoples of the East (as we said elsewhere) were accustomed to use a kiss in greeting, which was a symbol of love and indeed of respect and deference as well, this custom passed to the Greek churches too, and therefore he admonishes the Corinthians about it here. He calls it a holy kiss so as to exclude all pretence, which, as in every other matter is base, so in friendships is at once most base and most harmful. Then, in the name of the brothers who were with him, he gives them greeting, so that just as he takes care to reconcile them to one another, so he may bind them to those who are absent too. For distance of place does not prevent those whom the unity of faith has joined from loving one another, since they are one body in Christ Jesus. We touch on these things briefly, because what could be said here we have already said at the end of the former epistle.

units.la: Restat ultima Epilogi pars, quæ Epistolam concludit benedictione vere Apostolica, qua omnia comprehendit, quæ ad perfectam hominis salutem faciunt: Gratia Domini IESV CHRISTI, & charitas Dei, & communicatio Spiritus Sancti, sit cum omnibus vobis, Amen. Per gratiam Christi omne id intelligit, quod hic nobis sua morte & obedientia meruit, adeoque totum nostræ redemptionis beneficium. Id verò omne gratiam dicit, quòd ut ipse nobis ex gratuita miseri cordia datus est: ita nos quoque, qui filij irâ eramus, cum Patre in gratiam reduxit, secundum huius testimonium, quod cœlitus delatum est: Hic est Filius ille meus dilectus, in quo placatus sum. Precatur ergo illis Paulus, ne unquam excidant à Christo & gratia illa Dei, quam ille nobis acquisivit. Deinde charitatem Dei subijcit, quæ prioris est consequens. Nam etiamsi Deus nos ab æterno dilexerit, & ideo Filium suum pro nobis tradiderit in mortem, nos tamen dilectionis ipsius fructum non sentimus, neque de ea certi esse possumus, donec Christum fide vera apprehendimus, quæ illum pro nobis datum esse, proque nobis satisfecisse folaintelligit. Etenim tunc demum cum Paulo possumus dicere: Iustificati ex fide, pacem habemus erga Deum per Dominum nostrum IESVM CHRISTVM. Item: Christus est, qui mortuus est: imò verò qui etiam excitatus est: qui etiam est ad dexteram Dei, qui etiam intercedit sive postulat pro nobis. Quis nos separabit à Charitate Christi? &c. Eenimvero non potest Pater eos odisse aut abijcere, quos æterno ipsius decreto destinatus Mediator ei reconciliavit. Tertio communicationem Spiritus Sancti illis precatur. Est hæc societas illa atque coniunctio, qua fit, ut fideles omnes eodem Dei Spiritu animentur, eiusque donorum participes fiant. Hunc enim Christus iam in mortem abiturus pollicitus est, ut eis consultor atque advocatus sit, quoad in carne hac mortali vixerint. Idem ille salutis nostræ arrhabo est, & ideo Spiritus ἀῤῥαβών, id est, adoptionis dicitur: ad hæc omni donorum genere, quæ hanc vitam viventibus necessaria sunt, fideles ornat & instruit: dirigit denique eosdem, ut & Veritatis cognitionem assequantur, & ad cœlestis hæreditatis possessionem perveniant. Quid multa? quicquid in nobis boni est, hoc omne Spiritus illius opus est, cùm ipsi ne ad cogitandum quidem idonei simus.
units.tr: There remains the last part of the Epilogue, which concludes the Epistle with a truly apostolic blessing, in which he gathers up everything that contributes to the complete salvation of man: "The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, and the love of God, and the fellowship of the Holy Spirit be with you all. Amen." By the grace of Christ he means all that he has merited for us by his death and obedience, and so the whole benefit of our redemption. He calls all this grace because, just as he was given to us out of free mercy, so he also brought us, who were children of wrath, back into favour with the Father, according to that testimony which was delivered from heaven: "This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased." Paul therefore prays for them that they may never fall away from Christ and from that grace of God which he has won for us. Next he adds the love of God, which follows from the former. For even if God loved us from eternity, and therefore delivered his Son to death for us, we do not feel the fruit of that love, nor can we be certain of it, until we lay hold of Christ by true faith, which understands that he was given for us and made satisfaction for us. Indeed, only then can we say with Paul: "Justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ." Likewise: "It is Christ who died, yes rather, who was also raised, who is also at the right hand of God, who also intercedes, that is, makes request for us. Who will separate us from the love of Christ?" and so on. For the Father cannot hate or cast off those whom the Mediator, destined by his eternal decree, has reconciled to him. Thirdly, he prays for the fellowship of the Holy Spirit for them. This is that partnership and union by which all the faithful are animated by the same Spirit of God and become partakers of his gifts. For Christ, about to go to his death, promised this Spirit, that he might be their counsellor and advocate as long as they lived in this mortal flesh. He is also the pledge of our salvation, and therefore the Spirit is called the earnest (arrhabon), that is, of adoption. Moreover, he adorns and equips the faithful with every kind of gift that is necessary for those who live this life, and finally he guides them so that they may both attain the knowledge of the truth and come to the possession of the heavenly inheritance. What need is there of many words? Whatever good is in us, all that is the work of that Spirit, since we are not even fit to think anything.

units.la: Est autem hic dignissimum observatu, quòd cum circa finem prioris Epistolæ simpliciter dixisset: Gratia Domini nostri IESV CHRISTI sit vobiscum, hic & Filij & Patris & Spiritus Sancti meminit. Causa plerisque ea esse videtur, quòd plerique Corinthiorum Trinitatis mysterium adhuc ignorarent. Ideo personas quidem tres diserte nominat, simul autem non obscure unam & eandem Deitatem hisce omnibus tribuit. Id ex eo apparet, quòd quæ alibi Patri tribuuntur, in præsenti Filio ascribit, & rursus Spiritui Sancto ea, quæ alibi Filio ascribi solent. Etenim Gratia plerunque ad Patrem refertur, & ab eo Apostoli illam credentibus precantur, ut in plerisque Epistolarum Inscriptionibus aut Salutationibus Apostolicis est videre. Similiter charitatem & dilectionem Christo ascribit in eo loco, quem paulo ante ex Epist. ad Romanos adduximus. Et in priori ad Corinth. primo Cap. communionis Filij Dei IESV CHRISTI meminit. Nam ut Chryvt Chrysostomus annotauit, τὰ τῆς τελειότητος ἀδιαίρετα εἶναι, id est, quaecunque propria sunt Trinitati, ea inseparabilia sunt, & proinde personis simul omnibus communia, secundum illud Christi: Omnia quaecunque habet Pater, mea sunt. Item: Et mea omnia tua sunt. Quod D. Athanasius olim recte obseruauit, quando in fidei Confessione haec verba interposuit: Qualis Pater, talis Filius, talis Spiritus Sanctus: Increatus Pater, increatus Filius, increatus Spiritus Sanctus: Immensus Pater, immensus Filius, immensus Spiritus Sanctus: Aeternus Pater, aeternus Filius, aeternus Spiritus Sanctus. Item: Omnipotens Pater, omnipotens Filius, omnipotens Spiritus Sanctus: Dominus Pater, Dominus Filius, Dominus Spiritus Sanctus, &c. Debent ista diligenter obseruari propter eos, qui propter attributorum, quae personis singulis propria sunt, diuersitatem, vel tres Deos fabricant, vel Filium Patre, & Spiritum Sanctum utroque minorem fingunt. At quia de his dicendi locus commodior alibi sese offert, ista nunc obiter dixisse sufficiat.
units.tr: Now it is most worthy of observation here that, whereas near the end of the former Epistle he had simply said, "The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you," here he mentions the Son, the Father and the Holy Spirit. The reason for this seems to be that many of the Corinthians were still ignorant of the mystery of the Trinity. So he indeed names the three persons expressly, and at the same time not obscurely ascribes one and the same Deity to all of them. This appears from the fact that what elsewhere is attributed to the Father, here he ascribes to the Son, and again to the Holy Spirit what is usually ascribed elsewhere to the Son. For grace is generally referred to the Father, and the Apostles ask it from him for believers, as may be seen in most of the openings and apostolic greetings of the Epistles. Similarly, in the passage we cited a little earlier from the Epistle to the Romans, he ascribes love and affection to Christ. And in the first chapter of the former Epistle to the Corinthians he mentions the communion of the Son of God, Jesus Christ. For, as Chrysostom observed, the things that belong to perfection are indivisible [τὰ τῆς τελειότητος ἀδιαίρετα εἶναι], that is, whatever is proper to the Trinity is inseparable, and therefore common to all the persons together, according to that saying of Christ: "All that the Father has is mine." And again: "All my things are yours." Saint Athanasius long ago rightly noted this, when in his confession of faith he inserted these words: "Such the Father, such the Son, such the Holy Spirit; uncreated the Father, uncreated the Son, uncreated the Holy Spirit; immeasurable the Father, immeasurable the Son, immeasurable the Holy Spirit; eternal the Father, eternal the Son, eternal the Holy Spirit." Again: "Almighty the Father, almighty the Son, almighty the Holy Spirit; Lord the Father, Lord the Son, Lord the Holy Spirit," and so on. These things ought to be carefully observed on account of those who, on the ground of the difference of the attributes proper to each person, either make three Gods or imagine the Son and the Holy Spirit to be less than the Father. But since a more suitable place for speaking of these matters presents itself elsewhere, it is enough to have said these things in passing for now.

units.la: Nunc obseruemus, hoc commune Christianis omnibus votum esse debere, quod & pastores Ecclesijs suae fidei creditis, & alij alijs priuatim atque publice precentur, vt gratia IESV CHRISTI, & dilectio Dei Patris, & Spiritus Sancti communio cum omnibus maneat. Ex his enim vniuersa salutis nostrae ratio dependet, qua omnibus huius saeculi bonis praeferunt, quicunque aliquem vitae futurae gustum perceperunt. Et cum Paulus haec tanta bona Corinthijs obtingere optarit, qui tam multis tamque indignis modis ipsum offenderant, quanto magis illa ijs precari debemus, quos nisi pro fratribus agnoscamus in Christo, nos neque Christiani neque filij Dei dici merebimur?
units.tr: Now let us observe that this should be the common prayer of all Christians: that both ministers pray for the churches entrusted to their faith, and others pray for one another, privately and publicly, that the grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, and the love of God the Father, and the fellowship of the Holy Spirit may remain with all. For the whole reckoning of our salvation depends on these things, and they are preferred to all the good things of this age by everyone who has tasted something of the life to come. And since Paul wished such great blessings for the Corinthians, who had offended him in so many and such unworthy ways, how much more ought we to pray these things for those whom, unless we acknowledge them as brethren in Christ, we shall not deserve to be called Christians or sons of God?

units.la: Habetis Viri Christiani & fratres in Christo dilecti, quae in vtramque Diui Pauli ad Corinthios epistolam pro talenti, quod nobis Deus ex gratuita misericordia largitus est, ratione dedimus. Quae quam probe nostris temporibus conueniant, alibi dictum est, & nemo non videt, qui horum statum atque mores propius inspexerit. Nos quod potuimus pro virili fecimus bona fide, neque nobis alicuius doli aut dissimulatae Veritatis, multo minus adulteratae, fumus conscij. Faxit Deus Opt. Max. vt sicuti Apostoli cura atque industria apud illos olim non absque fructu euanuit: ita noster quoque labor aliquam Ecclesiae morbis & vulneribus medicinam afferat, eoque nomine pijs gratus sit.
units.tr: You have, men and brethren beloved in Christ, what we have given, in accordance with the talent which God has bestowed on us by his free mercy, in explanation of both epistles of the divine Paul to the Corinthians. How well these fit our own times has been said elsewhere, and everyone sees it who has looked more closely at the condition and manners of these days. We have done what we could, to the best of our ability, in good faith, and we are conscious of no deceit or dissembling of the truth, much less of its corruption. May God, the best and greatest, grant that, just as the Apostle's care and labour once did not vanish there without fruit, so our work too may bring some remedy to the diseases and wounds of the Church, and so be pleasing to the godly on that account.

units.la: Tibi vero IESV CHRISTE, Fili Dei aeterne, redemptor & vindex generis humani vnice, gratias agimus, qui in hac postrema mundi senecta multis modis afflictissima, Ecclesias vbique gentium colligis: teque supplici animo & ardentibus votis rogamus, vt easdem inter ambitiosos contentionum fluctus, inter scandala item & undique imminentia omnis generis pericula, tua dextera protegere & tueri, atque Spiritus tui consilio regere digneris: ne vel tua gratia, vel Patris dilectione, vel Spiritus Sancti communione indigni reperiamur: sed tibi Deo & redemptori nostro seruiamus in fidei puritate, vitae innocentia & charitate non fucata, vsque in eum diem, quo tu miseros nos, in te autem vno felices & beatos, mortalis huius corporis vinculis solutos in regni tui coelestis possessionem transferas, vt tecum viuamus atque gaudeamus: cui vnà cum Patre & Spiritu Sancto, Deo vno, & solo immortali & aeterno, debetur benedictio, honor, gloria & potestas in aeternum,
units.tr: To you, however, Jesus Christ, eternal Son of God, the sole redeemer and avenger of the human race, we give thanks, you who gather churches everywhere among the nations in this last old age of the world, which is afflicted in many ways. We beseech you with a suppliant spirit and fervent prayers that you would deign to protect and defend these churches with your right hand amid the stormy waves of ambitious strife, likewise amid scandals and dangers of every kind hanging over us on all sides, and to rule them by the counsel of your Spirit, so that we may not be found unworthy of your grace, or of the Father's love, or of the fellowship of the Holy Spirit; but that we may serve you, our God and Redeemer, in purity of faith, innocence of life, and unfeigned love, until that day when you transfer us wretched ones, but happy and blessed in you alone, freed from the chains of this mortal body, into the possession of your heavenly kingdom, that we may live and rejoice with you; to whom, together with the Father and the Holy Spirit, the one God, the only immortal and eternal God, belong blessing, honour, glory and power for ever,

units.la: Amen.
units.tr: Amen.
